articles.title: Wall Street’s Plumbing Goes Onchain as Morgan Stanley Tokenizes Securities - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Morgan Stanley said it’s among the first banks to tokenize U.S. equities and Treasuries through the DTCC Tokenization Service, which launched Oct. 28.
- The service converts DTC-held securities into tokenized “digital twins” with the same rights as the originals, running on the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network.
- Twenty firms have signed on so far, including Bank of America, Citi and J.P. Morgan.
Morgan Stanley has started moving U.S. stocks and Treasuries onto blockchain rails, using Wall Street’s own plumbing to do it.
The bank said Tuesday that it’s among the first to tokenize real-world assets through the DTCC Tokenization Service, converting U.S. equities and Treasuries into tokenized form.
The service, which went live Oct. 28, is run by the Depository Trust Co., a subsidiary of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp. The DTC is the post-trade backbone of U.S. markets, with more than $114 trillion in assets under custody.
“The hands-on experience of integrating tokenized securities with established market infrastructure will inform the continued development of the firm’s digital asset capabilities as the market evolves,” said Amy Oldenburg, Morgan Stanley’s head of digital assets strategy.
The service lets eligible firms convert securities held at DTC into tokenized “digital twins” and back again, delivering them to digital wallets of their choice. The tokens keep the same ownership rights, investor protections and economic entitlements as the originals, according to DTCC, and are designed to let firms move collateral and tap new pools of liquidity within minutes. The service currently runs on the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network, with more blockchains planned for 2027.
Morgan Stanley is one of 20 DTC participants that have signed up so far, alongside Bank of America, Citi, J.P. Morgan, Fidelity Investments, Citadel Securities, and UBS, among others. DTCC said it developed the service with input from more than 150 firms.
The launch caps a regulatory path that began in December 2025, when the SEC gave DTC a no-action letter allowing it to tokenize Russell 1000 stocks, major index ETFs and U.S. Treasuries. DTCC has also worked with Chainlink on tokenized collateral management and laid out its plans for the service earlier this year as major Wall Street firms signed on.
The bank-led approach contrasts with crypto-native efforts to tokenize stocks. Fifty-six companies, including Tesla, SpaceX, Amazon, and Nvidia, have objected to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, a planned tokenized stock venue from OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange. Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, those objections bar the venue from listing third-party tokenized versions of their stock.
Demand is building, but the market is still young. The International Monetary Fund found last month that tokenized stocks trade mostly outside U.S. market hours, though they remain more volatile and less liquid than their traditional counterparts.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Above $80,000 in Post-Midterm Risk-Asset Rally
articles.text:
Bitcoin hits $80.5K as US stocks rally on midterm election results
Bitcoin climbed toward $80,500 as risk assets rallied on Democrats’ midterm election gains and oil prices fell.
Bitcoin (BTC) returned to $80,000 at Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks surged following a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections.
Key points:
- Bitcoin jumped past $80,500 at the start of Wednesday’s Wall Street trading session as risk assets gained following the US midterm election results.
- S&P 500 futures rebounded from a three-month low of 7,490 points as The Kobeissi Letter described the equities move as a “textbook bear trap.”
- Hopes for an end to the US-Iran war sent WTI crude oil below $93 per barrel.
Analyst eyes BTC price “relief rally” after midterms
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD up by over 4%, having rebounded from its lowest levels in seven weeks.
BTC/USD four-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
US stock futures made swift gains on Wednesday after initially dipping overnight. S&P 500 futures fell as low as 7,490 points, their lowest level since July 31, before reaching 7,690 points, approaching new month-to-date highs.
S&P 500 futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
In its latest analysis on X, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter called the initial equities weakness that accompanied news of the Democratic gains a “textbook bear trap.”
“This marks one of the largest shifts in US political power in nearly two decades,” it added, noting that the Democrats had flipped seven seats in the Senate and 25 in the House of Representatives.
In comments sent to Cointelegraph, James Butterfill, head of research at crypto asset manager CoinShares, saw the potential for a wider Bitcoin “relief rally” as election uncertainty faded.
“For Bitcoin, real yields, dollar liquidity and ETP flows still carry more weight than the elections,” he wrote, referring to Bitcoin exchange-traded products.
“We are seeing oil prices plummet, relieving some inflationary pressure and consequent rate hike expectations could moderate.”
Iran war optimism sends WTI crude to three-week low
Iran’s reaction to Democratic gains helped push US WTI crude oil prices to their lowest levels since mid-October.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
In an X post, Iran’s speaker of parliament, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, wrote that voters had “said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message.”
WTI dipped below $93 per barrel, down as much as 11.9% for the week, while Brent crude approached sub-$100 levels for the first time since Oct. 7.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Earlier on Wednesday, US President Donald Trump conceded that the Iran conflict was partly responsible for the Republicans’ election losses.
Economist Robin Brooks said that oil markets had priced in a risk premium that was “too high” before the midterms.
“The key question now is whether this causes the President to dial back on war with Iran or whether he escalates,” he wrote in a blog post.

articles.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Confirms Cyberattack After ZachXBT Ties It to $133M Crypto Theft - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed a cyberattack that allowed fraudulent operations, a day after ZachXBT named it as the alleged victim of a $133 million crypto theft.
- The French bank said the incident is now under control and customer assets are unaffected, but did not say how much was taken or confirm any crypto losses.
- ZachXBT said the attack took place over multiple days, and that he suspects the total is higher once over-the-counter activity is counted.
French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa has confirmed that it was hit by a cyberattack that allowed fraudulent operations, a day after onchain investigator ZachXBT named it as the alleged victim of a crypto theft of more than $133 million.
In a statement shared with Decrypt on Wednesday, the bank said the incident was "closed and now under control," and that operations were resuming gradually after it put stronger security measures in place. It said customers' assets were not affected, and that the attack had only delayed the execution of some transfers.
The bank did not mention crypto or say how much was taken. The amounts affected are still being assessed, but are "in any event not of a nature to call into question the solidity and financial health of the group," it said, according to Decrypt's translation.
Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said it informed the relevant supervisory authorities as soon as it detected the attack, and temporarily suspended some transactions as a precaution to prevent further fraudulent movements. It also warned customers to watch out for phishing attempts following the attack. Decrypt has reached out to Crédit Mutuel Arkéa for further comment, including on whether the losses involved crypto.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
ZachXBT's allegations
"Disclosing the EU financial institution exploited for $133M+ is allegedly Credit Mutuel Arkea, a French bank with $235B in assets," ZachXBT wrote on his Telegram channel on Tuesday. "The attack on the bank occurred for multiple days. I suspect the amount stolen is larger when accounting for OTC activity."
ZachXBT first flagged the suspected theft on Monday, saying an unnamed entity in the European Union may have lost more than $106 million from accounts at several crypto exchanges on November 1. The funds were withdrawn as USDC and USDT, he said in his original post, and the attacker then swapped USDC for ETH, moved funds through instant exchanges, converted some into privacy coin Monero and bridged across multiple chains.
In an update on Tuesday, he said he had identified a further $27 million in exchange withdrawals by the attacker, bringing the total to more than $133 million, and that some of those withdrawals took place after his initial disclosure. He also published four Ethereum addresses he said were linked to the theft.
"My working theory is a large financial institution in Western Europe was exploited and it's currently being covered up," ZachXBT wrote at the time, accusing it of not having conducted "proper incident disclosure" and thereby preventing law enforcement from freezing some $30 million in stolen funds.
He did not say how he had identified the bank, or how the attacker gained access to its exchange accounts.
The mutual banking group has been preparing to move into crypto. In May, French financial newspaper L'Agefi reported that it had applied for a license under MiCA, the EU's crypto rulebook, to offer crypto services to its retail customers and to provide them as a white-label service through its Arkéa Banking Services division.
The allegation comes days after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the largest crypto theft on record, which the FBI has attributed to North Korean hackers. ZachXBT said the attacker in the suspected EU theft remains unidentified, but that he could say "with a high degree of confidence it is NOT Lazarus Group," the North Korean hacking collective, "based on multiple laundering indicators."
This story has been updated to add comment from Crédit Mutuel Arkéa.

articles.title: France Backs Reporting of Self-Custodied Crypto Worth 100,000 Euros
articles.text:
France backs reporting for self-custodied crypto worth 100K euros or more
The amendment would require taxpayers to report holdings worth at least $112,000, but the measure still needs to survive the budget process.
The French National Assembly approved an amendment that would require taxpayers to report self-custodied crypto holdings totaling at least 100,000 euros ($112,000) to tax authorities.
Amendment I-2701 was adopted on Tuesday in a 150–44 vote, with eight abstentions, according to the Assembly’s official voting record. The threshold would be assessed on Dec. 31 of the relevant tax year.
Separately, the Assembly rejected an amendment that would have exempted gains on crypto payments for goods and services from tax if the payments totaled no more than 1,000 euros ($1,120) during the tax year. The proposal was defeated 69–14, according to the Assembly’s transcript.
The reporting requirement forms part of the 2027 Finance Bill and would need to be retained in the final legislation to become law. The Assembly faces a Nov. 17 deadline to complete its first reading of the bill. Senate debate is scheduled to begin Nov. 20, according to its schedule.
Crypto measures await final budget approval
The National Assembly postponed Tuesday’s scheduled vote on the budget’s revenue section for the second time as lawmakers continued debating amendments. The vote was originally scheduled for Oct. 20.
The vote’s postponement itself does not introduce a significant change, but the “likely rejection” of the budget’s revenue section could “result in the rejection of the entire bill in the National Assembly, including provisions adopted by way of amendments,” Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph.
On Friday, the Assembly rejected two proposals that would have applied exit taxes to unrealized crypto gains when taxpayers transferred their tax residence abroad.
Lawmakers also approved an amendment on Oct. 16 that would tax gains from converting crypto into stablecoins. The proposal covers stablecoins classified as electronic money tokens under EU rules and would still need to be retained in the final law.
Related: French Senate adopts bill for automatic sharing of crypto tax data

articles.title: Morning Minute: CFTC Clears Stock Perps, Gets Sued the Same Day - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors green after Dems sweep midterms; BTC at $78.3k
- Crypto’s $64M campaign against Sherrod Brown fails, several pro-crypto candidates lose
- Binance traced its $6.3B hack to a fake job interview & bad software download
- CFTC clears U.S. equity perps for trading; Citadel & others sue to stop it
- Circle reports earnings, revenue up 17% yoy (CRCL -3% premarket)
⚖️ CFTC Clears Stock Perps, Gets Sued the Same Day
A perpetual future is a leveraged bet on a price that never expires. You hold it as long as you can meet margin and keep paying a funding rate. It’s analog product would be options in TradFi, with a few differences (primarily no expiration date). Crypto traders have used them for years, mostly on offshore venues like Binance and onchain platforms like Hyperliquid, because U.S. law had no clear home for the product.
On Tuesday the CFTC said Americans can now trade them on individual stocks.
Hours later, Wall Street sued to stop it.
The approval came as a statement from CFTC Chairman Michael Selig. Equity perpetual futures are now tradable on CFTC-registered exchanges, classified as security futures products under the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000, which puts them under joint CFTC and SEC oversight.
The list of venues that can actually do this is short, and it was assembled quietly. A firm needs to be a CFTC-designated contract market and separately notice-registered with the SEC as a national securities exchange for security futures products. Seven entities hold both today: Cboe, CME, Coinbase, Kalshi, Bitnomial, Nadex, and ICE Futures U.S. Five of those seven filed inside a single 30-day window in September.
Kalshi is furthest along, with a filing covering 56 to 58 names and a launch expected within days. Coinbase has filed to list perps on Apple, Tesla and Nvidia. So those two are immediate winners. But Hyperliquid and Lighter, the top crypto perps protocols, are next in line for potential CFTC approvals and are likely future winners as well (LIT +10% on the day).
Then came the lawsuit. A new group called the Capital Markets Alliance filed in the Southern District of New York, naming Cboe, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association among its members. Its argument runs on two tracks.
- First, that stock perps are securities-based swaps and belong to the SEC, not the CFTC.
- Second, that the CFTC violated the Administrative Procedure Act by never explaining why it reversed an earlier position.
The group wants the policy eliminated. The American Securities Association piled on separately, pointing out that Congress banned selling security-based swaps to retail investors at all.
A CFTC spokesman called the suit “troubling,” adding that “our markets should be governed by law, not litigation campaigns intended to block innovation.” The CME already tried this once, suing over the CFTC’s crypto perps approval on the theory that perpetuals are swaps rather than futures. That one went nowhere.
So where does that leave us?
Well, remember that old phrase: “First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you, then you win."
We’re at the fight stage. Next stop, winning.
🌎 Macro Crypto and Markets
- Crypto majors are green post-Midterms with ZEC leading; BTC +1.6% at $78.3k; ETH +2% at $2,320; SOL even at $93; HYPE even at $85; ZEC +9% at $1,285
- LIT (+8%), VVV (+6%), RAY (+6%) and ENA (+5%) led top alt movers
- Oil -3% at $95; Gold +3% at $4,054
- Stock futures are green after the Democrat sweep; DOW +1.6%, Nasdaq +0.5%
- Crypto’s $64 million campaign against Sherrod Brown failed as he returns to the Senate, where he could land a committee leadership role with jurisdiction over the industry, capping a bruising night for crypto’s political operation; pro-crypto House Republicans Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn and Ann Wagner lost their seats, while Pete Ricketts held Nebraska and Andy Barr won Kentucky’s open Senate seat to replace Mitch McConnell
- Circle reported third-quarter revenue and reserve income of $865 million, up 17% year over year, with average USDC circulation reaching $73.3 billion
- Documentation platform GitBook disclosed a breach of its infrastructure credentials that it called “a sophisticated, highly targeted attack using AI agents,” exposing API tokens, integration secrets and Git Sync keys
- Justin Sun asked a federal court to sanction World Liberty Financial over a disclosure that initially listed the Trump-backed venture as a Florida company; Sun says the late amendment was a tactic to push his $45 million dispute out of federal court
- Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company holds “give or take 150,000 Bitcoin” at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, worth roughly $11.5 billion; the Q3 attestation accounts for $8.37 billion of Bitcoin, or about 100,100 coins, leaving some 50,000 unexplained
Ethereum privacy network Aztec shipped its Tierra upgrade, patching a critical vulnerability from the prior version and cutting client-side proof generation for private transactions to about one second
The SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance said it won’t recommend enforcement over Canton Coin’s programmatic issuance, treating the token as a digital commodity in a no-action letter
Binance traced the $6.34 billion hack to a fake job interview in which an engineer was asked to download a coding assignment that installed malware its endpoint tools never flagged; attackers then spent weeks moving laterally, abusing an internal AI tool to take over two more employees’ machines before reaching the wallet signing service on October 29

articles.title: Canton CC Rises 4% After SEC Staff No-Action Letter
articles.text:
Canton’s CC rises 4% as SEC staff view it as ‘digital commodity’
SEC staff’s no-action letter covers CC earned by running infrastructure and applications, but is not a binding ruling on its legal status.
Canton Network’s native cryptocurrency rose 4% on Wednesday after the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) Division of Corporation Finance issued a no-action letter stating it views the token as a “digital commodity.”
Canton Coin (CC) traded at $0.098 at 10:27 am UTC, but was still down roughly 4.2% over the past week, according to CoinMarketCap.
Canton Network is a privacy-focused network that enables banks and financial institutions to tokenize assets, trade and settle transactions across different platforms.
In its Tuesday letter, SEC staff accepted the explanation that CC’s value comes from how the network operates and demand for the token, rather than a central team’s efforts to generate profits for holders.
The division also said it would not recommend enforcement action over CC’s issuance without securities registration, provided the tokens are created under the conditions described by Canton.
In Friday’s letter to the SEC, Canton developer Digital Asset said network participants earn CC by operating infrastructure and applications, with the protocol determining how many tokens they can mint based on their activity.
The SEC issued guidance in March distinguishing digital commodities, such as Bitcoin and Ether, from securities. It said these tokens are not themselves securities, although the way they are offered and sold can still be subject to securities laws.
The SEC’s response reflects its staff’s position and is not a binding ruling on CC’s legal status.
SEC staff previously issued token-related no-action letters to crypto projects, including DoubleZero (2Z) in September 2025 and Solana-native decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) project Fuse in November 2025.

articles.title: Bitcoin Shrugs Off Midterms as Experts Say Democratic Sweep Was 'Priced In' - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin is up 1.6% to $78,277 after a brief dip, after the Democrats took both the House and the Senate.
- Analysts say the result was priced in, but it raises fresh uncertainty for the stalled Clarity Act and future pro-crypto policy.
- Crypto policy didn't decide the vote, one expert said, but the industry now carries "baggage" from President Trump's activity.
Democrats flipped both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the U.S. midterms, handing President Donald Trump a major political setback.
Experts say this was not the "preferred outcome" for crypto markets and that it has increased "uncertainty" for future pro-crypto policy. However, after a brief dip, Bitcoin is up 1.6% over the past 24 hours and now sits at $78,277, per Decrypt data. Broadly, almost every top 100 crypto token by market cap is in the green for the day.
"I think the Democratic sweep was largely priced in going into the midterms," André Dragosch, head of research at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt. "The downside risks were fairly limited going into these midterms as sentiment was already very bearish and there were already signs of seller exhaustion again. So, it is no surprise that we have seen this kind of V-shaped recovery on an intraday basis during the midterms."
Polymarket put odds of the Democratic Party sweeping both the House and Senate during the midterms at 65.5% at the start of the week. Dragosch said these odds meant that markets weren't shocked by Tuesday's results.
James Butterfill, head of research at CoinShares, agreed. "My sense is that Bitcoin had largely priced in a Democratic sweep, leaving room for a relief rally as uncertainty clears," he said in comments shared with Decrypt. "Therefore, the anticipated result need not trigger another sell-off."
"Crypto policy did not decide the midterms. The economy, gas prices, the Iran situation, and Trump's unmet promises did," Heslin Kim, co-founder and CBO of Zenith, told Decrypt. "Crypto policy was irrelevant to the broader voting pool, but it now has the baggage of all the egregious activity that was stirred up in our ecosystem associated with the Trump family."
Tim Sun, senior analyst at HashKey, told Decrypt that the results do "increase the uncertainty surrounding the progress of crypto policy," but that Bitcoin's price action means that the market doesn't interpret it as a "major negative catalyst."
Specifically, this may be because the midterm results don't mean the Democrats can roll back existing pro-crypto guidelines set out by the SEC and CFTC, Dragosch said. However, it does mean that going forward, the market cannot rely as heavily on Trump's "political tailwinds for momentum," Sun added.
It also complicates the picture for the Clarity Act, which would establish rules for crypto markets. The bill has been in limbo since it was introduced in 2025, with many Democrats opposing it due to Trump's crypto conflicts of interest.
Dmitry Machikhin, CEO of BitOK, predicted in a note shared with Decrypt that the Clarity Act will remain in limbo well into 2027, thanks to the midterm results.
"The greater concern is slower crypto reform," Butterfill said. "CLARITY faces a harder path, while investigations into Trump-linked ventures could consume political capital and generate uncomfortable headlines across the sector. But the administration remains in place, and existing regulatory progress, including GENIUS, does not simply disappear."
He expects U.S. exchanges, token issuers and businesses that rely on new regulatory permissions to be more sensitive to the result than Bitcoin, and said established, compliant operators could even gain if scrutiny falls disproportionately on weaker competitors.
"A Democratic Congress may even be good for the industry in one way," Marcin Kaźmierczak, co-founder and COO of RedStone, told Decrypt. "Crypto shouldn't depend on one political camp. Infrastructure has to work for whoever is in power and bring most value to the ecosystem participants. Finance is changing, and politics will not stop it."
Despite the switch-up in the House and Senate, Dragosch expects little to change over the next two years.
Will the Clarity Act be signed into law in 2026?
"I personally expect more disputes, disagreements, and simply more of 'nothing stops this train,'" he said, pointing to a lack of significant progress to rein in fiscal deficits. "We will probably remain in a fiscally dominant environment with increasing fiscal risks, which I think is ultimately a tailwind for hard assets like Bitcoin."
Instead, he believes macro factors "remain in the driver's seat for now." Specifically, he points to a potential upcoming pivot from the Federal Reserve as a response to "increasing risk" around the AI trade.
"This will likely cause renewed interest in debasement-resistant assets like Bitcoin," Dragosch said, "and will continue to drive institutional adoption via ETPs and treasury companies as well."
Butterfill also pointed to macro factors. "For Bitcoin, real yields, dollar liquidity and ETP flows still carry more weight than the elections," he said. "I would temper expectations for the pace of U.S. reform, while remaining constructive on institutional adoption. How Trump responds to being constrained is the less predictable part."

articles.title: Binance Hack May Be ‘Temporary Setback’ for Crypto, Grayscale Says
articles.text:
Binance hack may be ‘temporary setback’ for crypto, Grayscale’s Pandl says
Zach Pandl highlighted institutional custody safeguards as crypto markets recovered some losses following the record $6.3 billion Binance hack.
Binance’s $6.3 billion hack could temporarily hurt confidence in crypto markets but would ultimately lead to stronger security practices across exchanges, according to Grayscale.
“It also underscores the importance of institutional custody, such as offered by US-based crypto [exchange-traded products],” said Grayscale’s head of research, Zach Pandl, in a Tuesday report.
“These vehicles hold their assets at state-chartered banks and qualified custodians, typically offering offline storage, multi-signature wallets, SOC attestations and insurance policies,” he added.
Binance suffered a record $6.3 billion hack Thursday and pledged to cover all customer losses. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea. Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the allegations as “absurd rhetoric.”
The hack was followed by a market sell-off, with Bitcoin falling below $77,000 and BNB losing more than 8% over 24 hours by early Friday.
By Wednesday, total crypto market capitalization had rebounded 2% over the past 24 hours to about $2.63 trillion, after touching a weekly low of about $2.55 trillion earlier in the day. The recovery left the market about $100 billion below its Oct. 28 level.
Bitwise’s head of research, André Dragosch, told Cointelegraph that recent outflows from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds were “related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment.”
Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis

articles.title: USDC Issuer Circle Quietly Cuts 5% of Staff in Profitable Quarter - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Circle has cut about 5% of its workforce to better align its organization with its operating model and strategic priorities, it disclosed in its Q3 results.
- The USDC issuer booked $9.1 million in restructuring charges, mainly severance and notice-period payments, even as quarterly net income rose 5% to $226 million.
- Circle joins a string of crypto firms that have cut staff this year, including Coinbase, BitGo, Bitwise and the Ethereum Foundation.
Circle, the company behind the USDC stablecoin, has cut about 5% of its workforce, according to its third-quarter earnings release on Wednesday.
The reduction was "designed to better align our organizational structure with our operating model and strategic priorities," the company said in footnotes to its financial tables. Circle did not say how many employees were affected or which teams were cut.
It recorded $9.1 million in restructuring expenses in the quarter, mostly cash payments for notice periods and severance, employee benefits and related costs. Those were partly offset by a $5.7 million reversal of stock-based compensation, as unvested shares held by departing employees were forfeited.
The cuts came in a profitable quarter. Circle reported net income from continuing operations of $226 million, up 5% from a year earlier, on total revenue and reserve income of $865 million, up 17%. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 85% year-on-year to $317 million.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
Much of that growth came from outside Circle's core business. Other revenue rose to $207 million, including $182 million from the presale of ARC, the token for its Arc blockchain. Reserve income, the interest Circle earns on the assets backing USDC and its largest source of revenue, fell 8% to $658 million as interest rates on those reserves declined.
The average amount of USDC in circulation rose 8% from a year earlier to $73.3 billion, but ended the quarter flat at $73.9 billion. USDC's share of the U.S. dollar stablecoin market slipped to 27%, according to the company.
CEO Jeremy Allaire did not mention the job cuts in his comments on the results, or in a tweet on Wednesday calling Q3 "a big quarter for Circle." He said USDC carried 79% of all stablecoin transaction volume, up from 66% a year earlier, and that Circle's payments network ended the quarter at $41 billion in annualized volume, up 15-fold. "In January, the GENIUS Act takes effect and regulated digital dollars go mainstream," Allaire wrote. "Every layer of our platform is live and ready for it."
Q3 was a big quarter for Circle.
→ USDC carried 79% of all stablecoin transaction volume, up from 66% a year ago, and $13.9T moved onchain (+49%)
→ A record $208B of USDC was minted and redeemed, about $2.3B every day
→ Arc mainnet went live, with 100+ institutions and apps… pic.twitter.com/euVfyHBUXX
— Jeremy Allaire (@jerallaire) November 4, 2026
The cuts come as Circle expands. In September, it launched the public mainnet of its Arc blockchain, with BlackRock, DTCC and Visa among its permissioned validators. Allaire said in October that Circle plans to enter about 40 emerging and developing markets, and the company has since teamed up with payments-technology firm ACI Worldwide to pilot USDC settlement on Colombia's instant-payments network.
Crypto's layoff wave
Circle is the latest in a string of crypto companies to cut staff this year, citing weaker markets, artificial intelligence or both.
Coinbase cut 14% of its workforce in May, with CEO Brian Armstrong pointing to the crypto downturn and the company's adoption of AI. The Ethereum Foundation cut 20% of its staff in June as part of a reorganization, while custody firm BitGo cut 15% that month to focus on AI and stablecoins.
Exchange Luno cut a fifth of its global staff in July, citing automation, and crypto ETF issuer Bitwise cut 14% of its staff in August.

articles.title: Justin Sun Seeks $264K Sanctions Against World Liberty
articles.text:
Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure
Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10.
Tron founder Justin Sun is seeking $263,821.20 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial and its lawyers, accusing the Trump family-linked crypto company of submitting a misleading court disclosure about its ownership in a legal dispute over his $45 million WLFI token investment.
In a federal court filing, Sun and two co-plaintiffs alleged that World Liberty initially listed Florida as its sole citizenship before amending its disclosure nearly three months later to identify 22 individuals and entities in its ownership chain, including those in the United Arab Emirates.
“World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were,” Sun said. “When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.”
The amended disclosure came six days after a federal judge questioned World Liberty’s bid to move Sun’s claims into arbitration. World Liberty’s lawyers subsequently argued that the company’s UAE citizenship deprived the federal court of jurisdiction because foreign parties were on both sides of the lawsuit.
World Liberty Financial did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for comment.
Related: Circle shareholder sues Trump, World Liberty and Steve Witkoff over crypto deals
In April, Sun sued World Liberty, alleging fraud and the unlawful freezing of his tokens. World Liberty filed a defamation lawsuit against Sun in May, alleging false statements and violations of token-sale terms. Sun denied the allegations.
The legal back-and-forth followed a January 2025 agreement by an Abu Dhabi-backed investment vehicle to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.
Sun previously backed the Trump family’s crypto ventures by investing in World Liberty and buying President Donald Trump’s TRUMP memecoin. He topped the token’s leaderboard for a May 2025 dinner with Trump, with holdings valued at about $18.5 million.
UAE ownership disclosure prompts jurisdiction dispute
In an Aug. 26 email included in the court exhibits, World Liberty’s lawyer Sam Cleveland said his team had “recently” learned of additional citizenship information. He maintained that World Liberty already had UAE citizenship when Sun filed the lawsuit in April.
Sun’s lawyers subsequently sought corporate records and testimony about World Liberty’s ownership and when its attorneys learned of the UAE connection. They allege that World Liberty provided limited documentation but declined to explain why its original disclosure omitted that information.
According to attorney Edward Moss’s sworn declaration, the $263,821.20 request covers fees for four attorneys’ work opposing arbitration. It excludes other lawyers’ fees and costs related to jurisdictional discovery and the sanctions motion.
Sun said Tuesday he plans to refile in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is scheduled for Dec. 10.

articles.title: Midterms Blue Wave Makes $917K for One Polymarket Trader, If Alaska Doesn’t Flip - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- A Polymarket trader known as 0xa2 topped the platform’s daily leaderboard with $917,000 of profits after Democrats took both the House and the Senate during the US midterm elections.
- Most of those gains are unrealized, sitting in an active market that Republicans won’t win any swing states while Alaska waits on a final result.
- Polymarket gives the Alaska upset a 14% chance. Two weeks ago, its traders gave Lula a 20% chance in Brazil, and he won.
A "blue wave” swept the U.S. midterms as the Democrats took control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, in a crushing blow to President Donald Trump.
Polymarket predictor 0xA2 is the platform's most profitable trader over the past 24 hours, according to the site's daily leaderboard. They are currently $917,000 in profit, although most of that is still in an active position that has a real (ableit small) chance of upset.
The user wagered $609,644 on the Republicans not winning any Senate swing states when odds sat at just 36%, a market which has since surged to 87%. This turned his stake in to $1.48 million, putting him $860,000 in the green.
Its important to remember: these are unrealized gains and could drop at any moment as 0xA2 waits for Alaska's final verdict. Polymarket traders put a 14% chance on an upset—and while this may seem small, the site has seen similarly sized upsets recently—as in the case of Brazil's presidential election two weeks ago.
0xA2 also profited $106,115 by predicting that the Democrats would win the Texas Senate—profits that have been realized. Oddly, the user's second largest active position is $1.42 million on the U.S. not confirming that aliens exist before 2027.
Will the Clarity Act be signed into law in 2026?
"Election night showed how quickly round-the-clock markets move when traditional exchanges are closed. As polls began closing at 6pm ET, Kalshi’s odds of a Democratic sweep went from about 74% to 99%," Kelly Ye, Head of Research at digital asset management firm Talos, said in a note shared with Decrypt. "Prediction-market trading peaked between 8pm and 10pm ET, led by a small number of large trades."
It was a big day for Polymarket users profiting, with the top 10 users on the platform profiting more than $170,000, per the leaderboard. To put that into perspective, on a fairly random day in March this year, the top daily winner on Polymarket profited $154,000, according to the WayBackMachine, and the 10th biggest winner that day gained $29,700.
Prediction markets and elections
The midterms attracted major activity on leading prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi. According to Precition.com data, midterm markets attracted more than $546 million in notional volume over the past two weeks.
"The 2024 election was the breakthrough moment for prediction markets. It was their first major real-world test and the event that really drove volume and open interest," Dash, the pseudonymous data lead at Prediction.com, told Decrypt. "Today, sports dominate trading volume, but Politics is still the key driving factor for open interest."
During the 2024 presidential race, Polymarket became what Bernstein analysts called the world’s largest election prediction market, with its flagship market topping $3.6 billion in volume. Maybe more importantly, predictors favored Trump for most of the campaign, while traditional polls kept him neck and neck with Kamala Harris. Prediction market users took this as a sign that prediction markets are more accurate than traditional political polling.
"Increasingly, people are looking for accurate forecasts on election results," Dash said, "and prediction markets are one place they can be found."
Those forecasts aren't always accurate, though. Just two weeks ago, Polymarket predictors whiffed Brazil's presidential election, with users giving Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva about a 20% chance of winning ahead of election day, before he ultimately beat Flávio Bolsonaro to take a fourth term.
Experts told Decrypt at the time that Brazil’s prediction market ban had left the odds in the hands of traders with little local knowledge to correct the odds. Plus, experts warned that a 20% chance of something happening is still a very real chance.
"Ultimately, something that has an 80% chance of happening does not happen 20% of the time," Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, said.
So that 14% chance that 0xA2 loses his $860,000 in profit should be taken seriously.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $1.16B as Bitwise Sees Short-Term Selling
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs lose $1.16B as Bitwise calls selling ‘short-term’
Bitwise’s André Dragosch attributed Bitcoin ETF outflows to weaker market sentiment, saying institutions have largely maintained their exposure.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded more than $1 billion in net outflows over three trading days, but crypto asset manager Bitwise says the withdrawals do not signal a lasting retreat by institutional investors.
Investors pulled another $116 million from the funds on Tuesday, bringing net outflows since Friday to $1.16 billion, according to SoSoValue data.
“I do think it’s related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment,” Bitwise’s head of research, André Dragosch, told Cointelegraph.
The withdrawals followed Binance’s $6.3 billion hack on Thursday, which raised concerns about investor confidence and ETF custody security.
Dragosch attributed the outflows to weaker market sentiment rather than fears over the safety of ETF holdings.
Institutions are holding on
Dragosch said ETF flows reflect both long-term institutional adoption and shorter-term changes in investor sentiment.
He cited a recent Bitwise survey of 15 institutions, none of which had reduced their Bitcoin ETF exposure during the bear market. US regulatory filings also showed that most institutional investor categories, apart from hedge funds, had largely maintained their positions.
Related: Bitcoin ETF inflows leave institutional demand unclear: CoinShares
Retail investors still account for the majority of Bitcoin ETF holdings and tend to react more strongly to market volatility, according to Dragosch.
Bitwise’s analysis found that ETF inflows are closely tracked broader crypto market sentiment, which weakened around the Binance hack, he said.
Outflows slow as Bitcoin sentiment improves
Tuesday’s $116 million in outflows marked a slowdown from Monday’s $399 million and Friday’s $643 million, extending the funds’ withdrawal streak to three trading sessions.
The Crypto Fear & Greed Index rose to 34 from 26 on Monday, though it remained in the “Fear” category. Bitcoin gained about 1.6% over the past 24 hours, to trade near $78,000 at publication, according to CoinGecko.
The latest withdrawals brought the funds’ net outflows for 2026 to approximately $153 million.
Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool
Binance hack raises questions about ETF custody
The Binance hack has raised concerns among some industry observers about crypto ETFs custody, particularly because major funds rely on a small number of custodians.
Dragosch pointed to differences between the security arrangements used by crypto exchanges and institutional custodians, noting that the Binance incident affected hot wallets, which are connected to the internet, rather than cold wallets.
“In contrast, institutional funds held at Coinbase custody are custodied in cold storage which, by definition, are not connected to the internet,” Dragosch said.

articles.title: 2026 US Midterm Election Recap: Democrats Win Control of Congress
articles.text:
US midterm elections 2026 as it happened: Democrats win control of Congress
Democrats won control of Congress in the 2026 US midterms. Catch up on key races, crypto-backed candidates and the outlook for crypto regulation.
Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress, reshaping the outlook for cryptocurrency legislation and giving the party greater power to scrutinize President Donald Trump’s crypto ventures during the final two years of his term.
What the crypto industry needs to know now:
- Democrats have taken control of the US Senate, securing 54 seats to Republicans’ 44.
- Democrats have won 228 House seats to Republicans’ 139.
- Democrats need 51 Senate seats and 218 House seats to secure majorities in both chambers.
- The Blockchain Association’s election dashboard identifies 62 priority congressional races, including 18 Senate and 44 House contests.
- The results could influence the future of US cryptocurrency regulation, including the stalled CLARITY Act, and potentially intensify scrutiny of Trump’s crypto ventures if Democrats gain control of either chamber.
Election updates — coverage concluded
Live coverage has ended. Read our updates on key congressional races, crypto-backed candidates and election-night reactions below. Results and race calls are based on Associated Press reporting. Entries appear in reverse chronological order.
Nov. 4 at 03:35 ET:
Crypto-backed Republican Pete Ricketts wins Nebraska
Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts has defeated independent challenger Dan Osborn in Nebraska, where crypto political action committee Fairshake had reportedly spent nearly $11 million supporting Ricketts.
More recent spending data shows Fairshake-affiliated crypto super PAC Defend American Jobs spent approximately $13.5 million opposing Osborn, according to Federal Election Commission data compiled by Bankrolled as of Nov. 3.
Ricketts, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, has supported cryptocurrency legislation including the CLARITY Act and GENIUS Act. He voted to advance the CLARITY Act out of committee in May and supported an unsuccessful Senate procedural vote on the legislation in September, according to crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto.
Nov. 4 at 01:29 ET:
Democrats win US House, taking control of both chambers of Congress
Democrats have won control of the US House of Representatives, according to the Associated Press, flipping a chamber Republicans have held since 2023. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become Speaker.
Control of the House gives Democrats the committee chairs and subpoena power. NBC says that includes oversight of Trump’s family and business ventures.
Nov. 4 at 01:02 ET:
Democrat Troy Jackson unseats Susan Collins in Maine Senate race
Democrat Troy Jackson defeated Republican Sen. Susan Collins in Maine, according to the Associated Press.
Collins was one of four Republicans to oppose advancing the CLARITY Act in September, expressing concerns over its impact on bank deposits.
Unlike Collins, Jackson has expressed support for clear cryptocurrency legislation in the run-up to the election. According to Stand with Crypto, which rates Jackson as “very pro crypto,” he called to end the debanking of “lawful crypto businesses, and ensure Americans’ right to self-custody digital assets.”
Nov. 3 at 23:51 ET:
Trump congratulates Democrats on Senate win
“My message is congratulations to the Democrats, and I look forward to working with you for the good of our country,” President Donald Trump told CBS News’ senior White House correspondent Weijia Jiang.
Nov. 3 at 23:37 ET:
Democrats win US Senate majority
Democrats have won control of the US Senate, according to the Associated Press.
The majority was secured after Democrat Josh Turek won the Senate race in Iowa, bringing Democrats and independents who caucus with them to 51 seats.
The result reshapes the outlook for the stalled CLARITY Act and determines which lawmakers lead committees overseeing the industry.
Democratic control could also bring more congressional scrutiny of Trump-linked crypto businesses and regulators’ decisions. Control of the Senate could also affect confirmation of future presidential nominees to regulatory posts.
“It’s too early to say exactly what this means for crypto, but one thing is clear: nothing will pass without cross-partisan support,” Jerome de Tychey, president of Ethereum France and co-founder of EthCC, told Cointelegraph.
Nov. 3 at 23:28 ET:
Democrats on brink of controlling Congress
Democrats are now in control of 50 Senate seats — one short of a majority — after flipping five seats in GOP states, some that hadn’t seen a Democratic senator in power for decades.
Earlier, Decision Desk HQ projected the Democratic Party to win a majority in the US House of Representatives.
Nov. 3 at 23:12 ET:
Sherrod Brown wins in Ohio, flips Senate seat to the Democrats
In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown, a longtime crypto critic, beat incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted in a race that has attracted approximately $63 million in crypto industry spending.
That includes about $56 million from Fairshake and $7 million from the Winklevoss-backed Digital Freedom Fund, with both groups spending to support Husted or oppose Brown.
Crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto characterizes Brown as strongly opposed to cryptocurrency, citing 17 statements and his 2024 vote against overturning the SEC’s SAB 121 crypto custody accounting guidance.
Brown was also targeted by crypto industry spending in 2024, when Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs spent more than $40 million supporting Republican Bernie Moreno, who defeated Brown in that year’s Senate election.
Nov. 3 at 23:11 ET:
Another GOP stronghold falls: Democrats win Texas Senate race
Democrat James Talarico has won Texas’ US Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton, according to the Associated Press, flipping another Republican-held seat.
Talarico becomes the first Democrat to win a statewide election in Texas since 1994. As of 11 pm ET, he led Paxton by approximately 1.09 million votes, with 56.1% to Paxton’s 42.2%, according to Decision Desk HQ. Counting was continuing.
Paxton received support from the Winklevoss-backed Digital Freedom Fund, although both candidates earned A ratings from crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto.
Paxton has called for the passage of the CLARITY Act, arguing that clear regulations are necessary to maintain US competitiveness in digital assets. In a June statement, he said the country must become the “crypto capital of the world” and support innovation and growth.
Talarico has similarly called for clear regulations that protect consumers while allowing innovation. As a Texas state representative, he also voted in 2025 to establish a state strategic Bitcoin reserve, according to legislative records cited by Stand With Crypto.
Nov. 3 at 22:38 ET:
Democrats win South Carolina Senate seat in major upset
Democrat Annie Andrews has defeated Republican Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina, according to the Associated Press, giving Democrats another pickup.
Andrews’ victory ends more than two decades of Republican control of the seat. The last time South Carolina elected a Democrat to the Senate was in 1998.
Following their victory in North Carolina, Democrats would need two further Republican-held seats to reach a majority, provided they retain all their Democratic-held seats.
Nov. 3 at 22:25 ET:
Democrats projected to win House of Representatives
Decision Desk HQ has projected the Democratic Party to win a majority in the US House of Representatives.
Nov. 3 at 22:02 ET:
Democrats six seats short of Senate majority
Democrats and allied independents stood at 45 Senate seats as of 10:02 pm ET, six short of the 51 needed for a majority.
Their path includes retaining Democratic-held seats in Oregon, Michigan and Minnesota and flipping three additional Republican-held seats. Democrats have already picked up North Carolina.
NBC News has projected that Democrat Annie Andrews will defeat incumbent Republican Senator Darline Graham in South Carolina in a major upset. Associated Press has not yet called this race.
Nov. 3 at 21:21 ET:
Crypto-backed Republican Andy Barr wins Kentucky Senate seat
Republican Representative Andy Barr has won Kentucky’s US Senate race, sending a supporter of the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts to the upper chamber.
Fairshake-affiliated political action committees spent more than $7 million supporting Barr in the Republican primary. Barr has also introduced legislation aimed at protecting lawful businesses, including crypto firms, from debanking.
Nov. 3 at 21:17 ET:
Democrat Juliana Stratton wins Illinois Senate seat
Democrat Juliana Stratton has won Illinois’ US Senate race, succeeding retiring Democratic Sen. Dick Durbin.
Stratton advanced through the Democratic primary despite substantial opposition from crypto-backed PAC Fairshake, which had spent more than $5.5 million against her by early March.
Nov. 3 at 21:05 ET:
Republican Hageman wins Wyoming Senate seat
Republican Representative Harriet Hageman has won Wyoming’s US Senate race against Democrat James Byrd, succeeding retiring crypto advocate Senator Cynthia Lummis.
Lummis, who chairs the Senate Banking Subcommittee on Digital Assets, sponsored the BITCOIN Act of 2025 to establish a US strategic Bitcoin reserve and has supported the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts.
Hageman has also backed cryptocurrency legislation, voting to pass the CLARITY and GENIUS Acts in 2025 and the FIT21 market structure bill in 2024. She also cosponsored legislation seeking to prohibit the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency, according to Stand With Crypto. The advocacy group lists no documented position on cryptocurrency for Byrd.
Nov. 3 at 21:05 ET:
Prediction markets price Democratic control of both chambers
Kalshi and Polymarket traders now give Democrats a 99% chance of winning Senate control and price House control at nearly 100%. It came as Democrats flipped North Carolina’s Senate seat, while holding Georgia and New Hampshire.
Nov. 3 at 20:08 ET:
Democratic Senate odds climb above 90%
Prediction markets increasingly favored Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress on Tuesday evening.
As of 8:05 pm ET, the Blockchain Association’s election dashboard showed Democratic Senate-control odds at 94% on Kalshi and 93% on Polymarket, up from 75% and 75.5%, respectively, earlier in the day. Democratic House-control odds stood at 98% and 99%.
At the time, Democrats and allied independents have secured 42 Senate seats to Republicans’ 31.
Nov. 3 at 20:01 ET:
Democratic senators Markey and Coons win reelection
Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey and Delaware Senator Chris Coons, both Democrats, win reelection, according to the Associated Press.
Markey voted against the GENIUS stablecoin bill in 2025, while Coons has criticized President Donald Trump’s crypto ventures, calling his latest memecoin-holder event “corruption.”
Nov. 3 at 19:57 ET:
Democrat Jon Ossoff retains Georgia Senate seat
Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff has won reelection in Georgia, beating Republican Representative Mike Collins.
Ossoff expressed support for impeaching Trump in April 2025 over plans to host a private dinner for top holders of the president’s TRUMP memecoin, arguing that the arrangement amounted to selling access to the presidency.
Nov. 3 at 19:41 ET:
1inch sees agencies driving US crypto regulation
Maylea Ma, deputy general counsel at 1inch, said she expects federal agencies to drive the next phase of crypto regulation.
The election could reshape the path forward for the stalled CLARITY Act, but Ma said “real movement” in US digital-asset regulation over the next few years will come from the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Treasury, rather than Congress.
Ma said those agencies were increasingly engaging with crypto projects. However, agency engagement does not provide the stability the industry had hoped to secure through legislation.
“The long-term goal, of course, remains a statute that cannot be reversed every time a government changes,” said Ma.
Nov. 3 at 19:09 ET:
CLARITY opponent Wasserman Schultz wins reelection
Democratic Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz wins Florida’s 20th Congressional District. Wasserman Schultz voted against the CLARITY crypto market structure bill when it passed the House in July 2025.
Nov. 3 at 19:05 ET:
Democrat Warner retains Virginia Senate seat
Democratic Senator Mark Warner has won reelection in Virginia, defeating Republican challenger Bert Mizusawa. Warner was widely favored to win.
Warner voted against advancing the CLARITY Act in September, arguing that crypto legislation needs safeguards against President Donald Trump personally benefiting from the industry. Warner supports establishing federal rules for digital assets, with his opposition to the bill focused on its ethics protections.
Nov. 3 at 18:00 ET:
First US polls close
The first polls in the US midterm elections closed at 6 pm ET in parts of Indiana and Kentucky. The remaining polls in both states close at 7 pm ET.
Polls also close at 7 pm ET in Georgia and Virginia, followed by Ohio at 7:30 pm ET, where Republican Sen. Jon Husted faces Democrat Sherrod Brown in a race drawing major crypto industry spending.
Nov. 3 at 11:37 ET:
Early voting surpasses 57 million ahead of midterms
More than 57 million Americans had cast ballots as of Monday, with early voting surpassing 2022 levels in several closely watched states, according to the Associated Press.
Current balance of power in the US House and Senate. Source: Blockchain Association

articles.title: Judge Orders Bitcoin Wallet Returned to Family of Convicted Canadian Killer - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- A Nova Scotia Supreme Court judge ordered that a laptop holding a Bitcoin wallet be returned to the family of convicted killer William Sandeson.
- Justice John Bodurtha found the Crown had failed to prove the Bitcoin was connected to the 2015 murder of Dalhousie University student Taylor Samson.
- The wallet has been valued at anywhere from C$8,000 to more than C$200,000, and was at the center of a wrongful death lawsuit brought by Samson's family.
A Canadian judge has ordered that a laptop containing a Bitcoin wallet be returned to the family of William Sandeson, who is serving a life sentence for the 2015 murder of fellow university student Taylor Samson during a drugs deal, Global News reported.
Justice John Bodurtha of the Nova Scotia Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday that prosecutors had not proved the cryptocurrency was linked to the killing. Sandeson, who appeared virtually at the hearing in Halifax, had filed a motion in April seeking the return of personal items seized when police searched his apartment after his arrest in 2015.
"The Crown has not met its burden to demonstrate the cryptocurrency was used as part of the drug transaction, proceeds of crime, or otherwise tainted by criminality," Bodurtha said, adding that its potential use in the deal was "hypothetical."
The judge did rule that about $3,600 (C$5,000) in cash found in Sandeson's apartment after the murder was "offence-related property," meaning it will not be returned.
Sandeson has said the Bitcoin was worth between about $5,800 and $7,200 (C$8,000 to C$10,000), according to Global News. A lawyer representing Samson's family in a separate wrongful death lawsuit, in which the cryptocurrency had been at the center, has said it could now be worth more than $144,000 (C$200,000). Global News did not report how much Bitcoin the wallet holds.
The Sandeson case
Sandeson, then 23 and about to start medical school at Dalhousie University, arranged for Samson, 22, to come to his apartment on August 15, 2015, to sell him cannabis that Sandeson had arranged to buy for C$40,000, according to prosecutors at his 2023 trial. Sandeson shot Samson, kept the drugs and the money, and later admitted to dumping his body in a river that feeds the Bay of Fundy. Samson's remains have never been found.
Sandeson was convicted of first-degree murder in 2017, but an appeals court overturned the verdict in 2020. At a second trial in 2023, he admitted to shooting Samson but said he acted in self-defense. A jury found him guilty of second-degree murder, which carries an automatic life sentence. He is serving his sentence in Quebec and will be eligible for parole in 2030.

articles.title: Binance Hackers Move 81% Stolen SOL, Use THORChain
articles.text:
Binance hackers move 81% of stolen Solana, route funds via THORChain
The Binance attackers moved most of the stolen SOL and continued laundering funds through THORChain after the protocol resumed swaps.
The attackers behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack have moved about 81% of the stolen Solana (SOL) as they continue laundering assets through the cross-chain swap protocol THORChain.
Wallets grouped under the Binance hacker entity held 182,443 SOL (worth $16.9 million), or roughly 18.8% of the total 970,522 SOL stolen during the exploit, according to blockchain data platform Arkham.
Lookonchain reported on Wednesday that the attackers split SOL across multiple wallets, selling it for USDC, bridging to Ethereum to buy Ether, and ultimately swapping ETH for Bitcoin (BTC) via THORChain.
Binance suffered a record-setting hack on Thursday after attackers compromised employee devices through fake job interviews and malicious software downloads, the exchange said. Binance said Tuesday it replenished 98% of affected tokens and would absorb losses.
The US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hackers on Saturday and urged crypto service providers, including THORNode operators, to block transactions linked to stolen assets.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the accusations as “absurd rhetoric.”
North Korea-linked hacking groups are suspected of using THORChain to launder proceeds from some of the largest cryptocurrency hacks, including the $1.4 billion Bybit hack.
THORChain resumes swaps after halt delayed laundering
THORChain restored trading on Bitcoin, Ethereum and several other chains on Wednesday. Services had been halted on Saturday after an Ethereum block reorganization exposed a refund bug. The halt inadvertently delayed Binance hackers’ laundering activity, according to Chainalysis.
Blockchain investigator SomaXBT estimated that about 54% of the attackers’ more than 47,600 transactions on Tron and Solana were automated.
Binance hackers expanded their laundering activity to Solana on Sunday after emptying most of their temporary holding wallets on Tron. Chainalysis estimated that about $500 million in total value moved through Tron, including repeated transfers between wallets.
Related: Binance’s net inflows turn positive at $2.3B as withdrawals expand

articles.title: Weekend stock tokens predict Monday open, but guessing up scores 55%
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitquery’s stock-token study scored 54% on qualifying opening directions, versus 55% for always predicting a rise.
- A stronger later Sunday result changed timing and sample filters after futures reopened, leaving independent token information unresolved.
- Nasdaq’s conditional 23/5 plan could narrow weekday access differences for investors eligible to use both routes.
Stock tokens kept trading through weekends, but their prices did not reliably guide the next stock-market open in a new study of 121 stocks.
Blockchain data provider Bitquery's Nov. 3 analysis found that Sunday token moves measured before equity-index futures reopened correctly called 54% of qualifying openings, so simply predicting that every stock would open higher scored 55%.
More hours can give investors another opportunity to transact, but they do not show that the resulting prices predict the next opening better.
What the weekend price test measured
Bitquery followed 17 weekends beginning July 10 through Oct. 30, with the final stock opening on Nov. 2. It recorded 791 stock-opening observations across those stocks, and its direction test kept the 533 openings that moved at least 0.5% from Friday's close.
Token moves pointed the right way on 286 of those observations, compared with 291 correct calls for always predicting a rise. Because more openings rose than fell, a 50% coin-toss benchmark alone would flatter the tokens' result.
The study also used balanced accuracy, which averages success on rises and falls. The tokens scored 53%, with a reported 95% interval of 44% to 62%.
Across all 791 observations, including smaller moves, the median error was 1.2% using token moves versus 0.9% assuming the stock opened at Friday's close. Bitquery put the excess error at 0.3%, with a 95% range of 0.2% to 0.5%.
A weekend price is not yet a forecasting edge
Bitquery's study asks different questions about direction and forecast size. The later Sunday reading also changes the information and the sample.
Trading access and useful forecasting information remain separate claims.
- Bitquery's November 3 study of 121 stocks over 17 weekends found no statistically clear directional forecasting advantage in stock-token prices read just before 6 p.m. New York time on Sunday, ahead of the equity-index futures reopening used as its cutoff. Bitquery, November 3, 2026
- Bitquery reports 791 eligible stock-opening observations over weekends beginning July 10–October 30, 2026, ending with November 2's open; its directional test uses only the 533 openings moving at least 0.5% from the previous Friday close. Bitquery, November 3, 2026
- Bitquery reports 53% balanced accuracy, averaging success on rising and falling openings, with a 95% interval of 44%–62%, including the 50% fixed-guess baseline; the hit-rate difference versus always-up spans about minus 20 to plus 16 percentage points. Bitquery, November 3, 2026
- Across all 791 openings, Bitquery reports a median forecast error of 1.2% using token moves, compared with 0.9% using Friday's stock close; its 0.3-percentage-point excess-error estimate has a 95% range of 0.2–0.5 points. Bitquery, November 3, 2026
- The study requires at least $10,000 weekend trading per token listing and a trade in the hour before both cutoffs, excludes split/ex-dividend openings and crypto-sensitive stocks such as MSTR and COIN, then blends issuers into one stock-weekend price weighted by weekend dollar volume. Bitquery, November 3, 2026
- A separate Bitquery sensitivity check using just-before-8 p.m. Sunday prices, a $1 million weekend-volume floor and a changed movement filter reports 59% balanced accuracy, with a 95% range of 53%–65%, on 220 openings; changing timing and eligibility together after futures reopen cannot isolate independent token information. Bitquery, November 3, 2026
Vendor research, not independent raw-data replication. No futures-price benchmark or cost-adjusted strategy. The later cutoff, volume floor and movement filter change together.
Method: Reported study figures only. Main test: 17 weekends beginning July 10–October 30, openings through November 2. Direction filters stock moves below 0.5%; size uses all 791 observations. Panel intervals are reported 95% ranges. Point and interval geometry maps linearly onto the same 40%–70% balanced-accuracy scale; this is an interval plot, not a zero-based bar chart.
The main test read token prices just before 6 p.m. Sunday ET, the futures reopening cutoff used by Bitquery. That timing is important because a later token price could incorporate information already available from equity-index futures.
A separate check using prices just before 8 p.m. returned 59% balanced accuracy, with a 95% range of 53% to 65%, across 220 openings. But it also raised the weekend-volume threshold to $1 million and changed the movement filter.
Listings needed at least $10,000 of weekend trading and a trade in the hour before each cutoff. The study excluded openings affected by stock splits or ex-dividend dates and crypto-sensitive stocks such as Strategy and Coinbase, then combined issuers using weekend-volume weights.
Earlier perpetual-market research reported improved forecasts from final weekend prices in a different sample. Different instruments, liquidity filters and observation times prevent that result from serving as a direct rebuttal to this test.
Nasdaq could narrow the weekday access gap of stock tokens
Nasdaq's Oct. 30 update described Dec. 6 as the expected transition to 23-hour, five-day trading, subject to clearing and market-data infrastructure being ready. Its related market-data proposals also remain subject to regulatory approval.
Its member implementation notice describes an added 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. ET session requiring new member ports.
If the rollout proceeds, wider conventional weekday hours would narrow one stock-token advantage for investors whose brokers and jurisdictions permit both routes. Weekend trading and the ability to hold tokens in a blockchain wallet remain separate benefits to assess.
For example, Kraken's xStocks disclosure excludes the US, Canada, UK and Australia, permits compatible-wallet withdrawals and says holders lack ownership and voting rights in the underlying shares.
The next useful evidence would hold timing and eligibility constant, compare against available market benchmarks, and measure executable results after costs. Until then, an available weekend price should not be mistaken for a demonstrated forecasting advantage.

articles.title: Democrats Win US House and Senate in 2026 Midterms
articles.text:
Democrats win US House to secure control of Congress in midterms
Democrats will take control of House committees in January 2027, giving them power to investigate President Donald Trump’s administration.
Update (Nov. 4, 2026, 11:24 am UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from CertiK’s Stefan Muehlbauer on the election results and the outlook for US crypto legislation.
Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections, giving the party greater influence over legislation and oversight of President Donald Trump’s administration.
The party won House seats in districts where Trump beat his Democratic opponent by as much as 18 percentage points in 2024. Democrats also flipped at least seven Senate seats in Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina, according to the Associated Press.
The result could reshape the outlook for crypto legislation and bring greater congressional scrutiny of Trump-linked digital asset businesses. Democratic committee leaders will gain more influence over which bills advance and which industry activities face investigation.
Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK, said the results could derail the CLARITY crypto market structure bill.
“The immediate read on this election result is that CLARITY bill is likely dead,” he said in comments shared with Cointelegraph, referring to both the upcoming lame-duck session and the next Congress.
Muehlbauer said he expected Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Maxine Waters, both outspoken crypto critics, to chair the Senate Banking Committee and House Financial Services Committee, respectively.
He also said Democrats had fallen short of the Senate’s 60-vote threshold for overcoming a filibuster, limiting their ability to advance legislation.
Democrats will take control of House committees in January 2027, allowing them to issue subpoenas and investigate the Trump administration, the president’s family and their business interests, according to NBC News.
Election results draw early industry reactions
Financial markets commentary publication The Kobeissi Letter pointed to affordability as the defining election issue, citing high energy costs and renewed interest rate increases.
Gokhshtein Media founder David Gokhshtein said Republicans had performed worse than he expected.
“Well, Republicans got their asses handed to them. I thought they’d do better. I was wrong,” he wrote on X Wednesday.
Prediction markets had favored a Democratic sweep. Traders on Kalshi and Polymarket put the probability of Democrats winning both chambers at roughly 75% on Tuesday, before the results were announced.
Related: What’s at stake for crypto as the US votes in the 2026 midterms?

articles.title: Nvidia stock tokens show price spreads, but slippage crushes the arbitrage
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Coin Metrics' modeled $1,000 comparisons leave 1 basis point before fees in one case and negative 15 in another.
- Bitquery's corrected historical prices account for shares and dividends.
- Issuer onboarding, whitelisted wallets and route-specific costs affect how holders can turn Nvidia token price gaps into executable trades.
Tokens tracking Nvidia shares can trade at different prices across issuers and exchanges, but buying the cheaper version and selling a dearer one leaves little room for profit in two modeled comparisons published by data provider Coin Metrics on Nov. 3.
The data provider's execution study shows about one basis point remaining in one $1,000 comparison after entry and exit slippage, and a negative 15 basis points in another.
The results show how a visible price difference can shrink when an order reaches the market, while preserving a small positive remainder in the first example.
A holder must compare the same share exposure, have something to sell on the expensive side, and qualify for the route used to settle the trade.
Coin Metrics' spread and slippage chart compares buying Hyperliquid NVDAx with selling Binance NVDAb, printing a gross gap of 10 basis points, entry and exit slippage of 10 basis points, and a one-basis-point remainder before trading fees.
Its second comparison buys Hyperliquid NVDAx and sells Kraken NVDAx. There, an 18-basis-point gross gap faces 33 basis points of entry and exit slippage, leaving a negative 15-basis-point gap before fees.
The price gap shrinks at execution
Two $1,000 modeled comparisons. June–Nov. 2, 2026 data; published Nov. 3. Trading fees are excluded.
One comparison retains only 1 basis point before fees; the other is already negative.
- Coin Metrics published its Nvidia token execution analysis on November 3, 2026; its spread/slippage section covers June 2026 through November 2, whereas its recent premium and venue-ranking observations cover October 27 through November 2. Coin Metrics / Talos, Nov. 3 execution study
- Coin Metrics' $1,000-notional chart labels a cross-wrapper comparison 'buy Hyperliquid NVDAx / sell Binance NVDAb': gross spread +10 basis points, entry-plus-exit slippage −10 basis points, and a remaining 1 basis point before trading fees, as printed and rounded. Coin Metrics / Talos, Nov. 3 execution study Publisher chart: Spread and Slippage Costs
- Coin Metrics' $1,000-notional chart labels a cross-exchange comparison 'buy Hyperliquid NVDAx / sell Kraken NVDAx': gross spread +18 basis points, entry-plus-exit slippage −33 basis points, and −15 basis points before trading fees. Coin Metrics / Talos, Nov. 3 execution study Publisher chart: Spread and Slippage Costs
- The Coin Metrics chart supports almost no remaining edge in its first example and a negative remainder in its second, before trading fees; it does not establish simultaneous executable quotes, realized profit, or a universal absence of opportunities. Coin Metrics / Talos, Nov. 3 execution study Publisher chart: Spread and Slippage Costs
Historical modeled results, before trading fees, not live quotes or realized returns. Labels are rounded independently; +10 and −10 do not sum to the printed +1. Exact contract mapping and all-in execution conditions are unverified.
Method: Replot literal publisher labels on matching −20 to +20 basis-point axes. Arrows connect each reported gross gap to its reported before-fee remainder, not a time series. Printed slippage and results are rounded independently; no raw data or inferred bar heights are used.
Tokenized-equity framework xStocks announced NVDAx/USDC spot trading on HyperCore on Aug. 10, separately from equity perpetuals. Moving those spot tokens to or from HyperEVM involves wrapping and bridging.
The chart's venue labels alone do not establish that transfer route for every observation in its June-November sample.
One stock, different routes
A second dataset shows why even a clean-looking price comparison needs adjustment. In a Nov. 1 correction, Bitquery normalized its Nvidia tokens per underlying share and adjusted dividend treatment.
Across its Sept. 15-Oct. 13 public-pool sample, pairwise median daily gaps among the four busiest versions rounded to no more than 0.12%. The widest pair was 0.1225%, rounded to 0.12%.
Kraken's multiplier explanation shows that dividend reinvestment can increase the share exposure displayed in an xStock balance while the number of on-chain tokens stays unchanged. For wrapped xStocks, the issuer separately says token prices must be adjusted using its multiplier.
Bitquery says their Nvidia tokens have separate contracts without a direct bridge or issuer swap between them, so buying the cheaper product does not supply the different token needed for the sale.
Kraken's Oct. 30 FAQ lists a 10-basis-point taker fee and a two-basis-point maker rebate for its Pro spot order book. App purchases using US dollars or USDG have no trading fee but may include a spread, while xStock conversions carry a 1% fee.
The issuer's primary-market documentation requires onboarding, identity and anti-money-laundering checks, and whitelisted wallets. Its named cash Market Flow lists a $5,000 minimum, 24/5 availability, and fees currently set to zero.
Kraken also excludes US persons and customers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia from xStocks access. Compatible-wallet withdrawals are supported, but transfers into a traditional brokerage account are not. The issuer classifies xStocks as tracker certificates providing economic exposure, without direct share ownership or voting rights.
The usable margin depends on executable prices for matching exposure, both legs' costs, and the ability to deliver or sell the relevant instrument.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Dips to $75.6K as Democrats Sweep US Midterms
articles.text:
Bitcoin bounces from 7-week low under $76K as Democrats sweep Congress
Bitcoin price downside reached a seven-week-low of $75,618 as 24-hour crypto long liquidations neared $300 million.
Bitcoin (BTC) sought to erase 3% overnight losses on Wednesday as crypto markets digested the Democratic sweep of the midterm elections.
Key points:
- Bitcoin fell to $75,618 as Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the US midterm elections.
- BTC/USD rebounded to overhead resistance at $78,000, while S&P 500 futures were down 0.3% on Wednesday.
- Analysts warned that BTC must defend its 50-week moving average, now at $75,733, to avoid a deeper correction.
US midterm vote sparks sub-$76,000 BTC price dip
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD falling into Tuesday’s daily close as election results came in, with Democrats going on to win control of both the House and Senate. The pair dropped to a low of $75,618 on Bitstamp, a level last seen on Sept. 16, before rebounding as high as $78,039 over the next three hours.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Data from CoinGlass showed the price dip liquidating late BTC long positions below $76,000, while a wall of asks kept upside contained below $78,000. Total crypto long liquidations over the past 24 hours stood at $288 million.
BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
In comments sent to Cointelegraph, Kelly Ye, head of research at institutional digital asset trading platform Talos, said that markets had largely priced in the election outcome.
“Bitcoin moved about 1.7% after the polls closed, close to the roughly 1.8% options had priced, and there was no major leverage flush. The election was the main event, but markets had largely prepared for it,” she said.
US stock futures showed similar moves, initially falling before recouping some losses. S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were both down by about 0.3% at the time of writing.
S&P 500 futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Late Tuesday, Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at financial services company Ameriprise Financial, told CNBC that concerns over data-center and broader AI capital expenditure were producing an adverse market reaction to the Democratic gains.
“If you get some governorships that are Democratic, what does that mean for the data center buildout, which has already seen a lot of skepticism over the last couple weeks in terms of the hyperscaler capex spending?” he asked.
In an interview with The Wall Street Journal, US President Donald Trump, who previously said he could become “Mr. Veto” to block Democratic policy initiatives, struck a conciliatory tone.
