“I think we’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll get along very well with them,” he said.
Bitcoin 50-week trend line key to avoiding “deeper correction”
Bitcoin’s drop to $75,618 coincided with its 50-week simple moving average (SMA), a trend line that has held as support since mid-September.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
In an analysis posted on X, Keith Alan, co-founder of crypto trading suite Material Indicators, identified the 50-week SMA as a line in the sand for Bitcoin bulls. Failure to defend it, he argued, would open the door to a “deeper correction ahead.”
BTC/USD one-day chart with 50 SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital, who had forecast BTC/USD dipping below $76,000 after a failed breakout attempt above $78,000, continued to flag overhead resistance on the three-day chart.
“If this continues then these newfound 3-Day Lower Highs may guide price back towards the ~$75.5k level below over time,” he said on Wednesday.
BTC/USD three-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com

articles.title: Pro-crypto candidates sweep 241 seats as Congress shifts power
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Stand With Crypto counted 222 pro-crypto House winners and 19 Senate winners in its unofficial election scorecard.
- The group named CLARITY co-sponsors Messmer and Moore among winners, alongside supporters Vindman and Stelson.
- SWC's ratings do not establish a CLARITY voting coalition, while banking and customer-protection disagreements remain unresolved.
Crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto (SWC) counted 222 House winners and 19 Senate winners it rates “pro-crypto” in its Nov. 4 election scorecard, identifying allies for the industry.
The group's results page also listed 106 House winners and eight Senate winners it rated “anti-crypto.” Its tally was marked updated at 9 a.m. ET and showed 384 of 435 House races and 33 of 35 Senate races called.
The group credits Decision Desk HQ for results and says they remain unofficial until certified. The pro-crypto and anti-crypto totals are also smaller than the number of called races displayed for each chamber.
SWC counts winning allies. CLARITY still needs agreement.
The group's scorecard lists 222 pro-crypto House winners and 19 Senate winners. Its unofficial election ratings do not establish a coalition for passage.
SWC's election ratings count winning candidates, not votes on a CLARITY text.
- Stand With Crypto's November 4 tally, marked updated at 9:00 a.m. ET, counted 222 House winners it rated pro-crypto and 106 it rated anti-crypto, alongside 19 pro-crypto and eight anti-crypto Senate winners. Stand With Crypto election scorecard
- Stand With Crypto's tally showed 384 of 435 House races and 33 of 35 Senate races called; it credited Decision Desk HQ and said results were unofficial until certified. Stand With Crypto election scorecard
- The pro-crypto and anti-crypto labels describe Stand With Crypto's ratings; its headline scorecard does not give a party breakdown of the pro-crypto winners or establish support for a particular legislative text. Stand With Crypto election scorecard
- The election scorecard measures SWC-rated candidates winning races, not a new congressional vote on CLARITY; it cannot establish enactment or a timetable. Stand With Crypto election scorecard House clerk: historical CLARITY vote CryptoSlate: CLARITY background
SWC's own ratings, not neutral classifications or future votes. Counts are not a complete division of called races. Senate counts cover election races, not all sitting senators. Unofficial until certified; refreshed stamp is Nov. 4 at 9 a.m. ET.
Method: Reported winner counts use the same 0–250 scale in both chambers. Desktop widths equal count × 2.08; mobile widths equal count × 1.32. No percentages or party breakdown are inferred. The legislative distinction follows the scorecard's scope and retained voting/background evidence.
The figures give crypto supporters a count of candidates the group considers favorable to the industry.
Associated Press reported at 6:26 a.m. GMT that Democrats had won the House and unified control of Congress.
In a Nov. 4 quote post, CEO of Yap Global Otto Jacobsson argued that voters had favored crypto while turning against AI infrastructure. He wrote:
“America still loves crypto, but hates the physical manifestation of AI.”
CLARITY backers among the named winners
In a congratulatory thread, Stand With Crypto highlighted endorsed candidates it said had won their races. The posts connect the broad scorecard to individual lawmakers and candidates with stated positions on crypto legislation.
The account congratulated Mark Messmer on winning Indiana's 8th District and described him as a co-sponsor of the CLARITY Act. It also said Riley Moore won West Virginia's 2nd District and described the endorsed representative as a co-sponsor.
The House clerk's roll call records both Messmer and Moore voting yes when the House passed CLARITY on July 17, 2025.
SWC also congratulated Eugene Vindman in Virginia's 7th District, saying he had backed both CLARITY and the GENIUS Act. Vindman likewise appears as a yes vote on the July 2025 House roll call.
For Pennsylvania's 10th District, the account said Janelle Stelson had won and had expressed support for CLARITY and GENIUS.
The House passed the 2025 CLARITY vote 294-134, with 216 Republicans and 78 Democrats voting yes, according to the clerk. The historical breakdown shows cross-party support in that chamber.
The two sets of numbers describe how representatives voted on a bill in 2025, and which candidates the advocacy group says won the election in 2026.
CryptoSlate reported before the election that CLARITY had failed a Senate procedural hurdle in September amid disagreements involving banking risks, stablecoin rewards and customer protections.
SWC's named winners include lawmakers with recorded support for CLARITY and a candidate who expressed support for it, but those positions do not settle the banking and customer-protection disagreements.

articles.title: Ethereum Dev Targets 2028 for Post-Quantum Transition
articles.text:
Ethereum dev targets 2028 for quantum resistance, a year early
Ethereum researcher Justin Drake said it is their “hope” that Ethereum will achieve its post-quantum and post-AI transition by December 2028.
Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake is targeting December 2028 to complete Ethereum’s post-quantum and post-AI transition, a year earlier than the foundation’s previously announced quantum-resistance deadline.
Speaking at Devcon 8 in Mumbai on Tuesday, Drake outlined the accelerated timeline. “Our hope is that by December 2028 we’ll be able to wrap up the full post-quantum and post-AI transition,” Drake said, adding that developers have 24 months to deliver three additional network upgrades.
The Ethereum Foundation’s September roadmap established December 2029 as its deadline for achieving quantum resistance across Ethereum’s execution, consensus and data layers.
Drake’s remarks signal a more ambitious timeline but do not formally replace the foundation’s existing roadmap, which is scheduled for reassessment in January 2027.
In August, Drake outlined plans for production-ready leanVM technology in 2027, followed by post-quantum deployments across Ethereum’s three layers in 2028.
The timeline has drawn scrutiny from other blockchain developers. In October, Starknet’s community backed research into becoming an independent post-quantum layer-1 network.
StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson previously told Cointelegraph that Ethereum’s 2029 target was “too late,” warning that deadlines could slip.
Related: Ethereum delays Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet launch over security risks

articles.title: Aave and Lido lose $1.7B in massive DeFi capital drop after the Binance hack
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Stablecoin market capitalization fell about $10.8 billion over 30 days, with earlier data showing contraction before the Binance breach.
- Aave's emergency freeze blocked fresh deposits while withdrawals pushed some reserves toward full utilization and higher borrowing costs.
- LlamaRisk's Nov. 2 update retained zero collateral borrowing power for USDT, USDC and USDT0 in affected Aave configurations.
Binance's security breach hit a crypto market whose stablecoin market was already shrinking, as DeFiLlama's dashboard put stablecoin market capitalization at $293.8 billion by Nov. 3, down over $10 billion in 30 days.
Binance's Nov. 3 report estimated that approximately $6.34 billion in assets were impacted on October 29 and said the company would absorb the financial impact.
The exchange's Oct. 29 incident added a separate shock to decentralized lending when an exploiter-linked wallet supplied USDT to the Aave lending protocol.
Aave's risk service provider LlamaRisk reported that an exploiter-linked wallet supplied 60 million USDT and borrowed 19,762 units of Wrapped Ethereum (WETH), worth about $44.6 million at the time.
Its Oct. 30 assessment described the position as overcollateralized and subject to normal liquidation, and said it did not put suppliers at risk.
Guardians subsequently froze 175 Aave V3 reserves and 117 V4 reserves. New supply and borrowing stopped in frozen reserves, while repayments, withdrawals and liquidations remained enabled.
Suppliers could withdraw available tokens, but fresh deposits could not replace them. LlamaRisk said withdrawals pushed some large reserves to 92%-100% utilization, meaning almost all supplied funds were borrowed. Borrowing costs rose, and stewards temporarily reduced the upper part of the interest-rate curves.
The affected reserves had reopened by Oct. 31, and LlamaRisk reported on its Nov. 2 update the restoration of specified non-stablecoin collateral settings and said affected reserves had returned to pre-incident rate curves on Nov. 1.
USDT, USDC, and USDT0 still had zero collateral borrowing power in affected configurations.
The wider contraction began before the Binance breach
Among the large protocols examined, Aave recorded the biggest dollar decline between Oct. 27 and Nov. 3. Its dated daily total value locked (TVL) fell by about $1 billion, and Lido followed with a $713 million decline.
| Protocol | Oct. 27 TVL | Nov. 3 TVL | Decline | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Aave | $17.435 billion | $16.405 billion | $1.030 billion | 
| Lido | $22.557 billion | $21.844 billion | $713 million | 
| JustLend | $6.856 billion | $6.419 billion | $437 million | 
| Morpho | $11.450 billion | $11.092 billion | $358 million | 
| Sky | $5.469 billion | $5.157 billion | $312 million | 
Falling token prices can reduce TVL without depositors moving assets, so a smaller TVL does not by itself establish either capital flight or insolvency.
USDT and USDC accounted for about $8.4 billion of the implied 30-day market-cap decline, based on DeFiLlama's rounded values and percentage changes.
DeFiLlama's separate historical series, which has different coverage from the dashboard, fell from $308.8 billion on Oct. 4 to $303.3 billion on Oct. 27.
Issuer redemptions exchange circulating stablecoins for fiat, differing from moving tokens off an exchange or between wallets. Freezing stolen tokens also does not automatically remove them from supply.
The practical risk is the amount of liquidity available where they need it. Thinner trading pools can produce more slippage for the same trade, lending withdrawals can raise borrowing costs, and falling collateral prices increase liquidation exposure.
Conditions would look healthier with renewed stablecoin net issuance, lending deposits returning, lower reserve utilization with more withdrawable tokens, and steadier collateral prices. A rebound in dollar TVL alone would not show that lending cash had returned.

articles.title: Democrats Win US Senate, Reshaping Crypto Regulation
articles.text:
Democrats claim control of the US Senate
The shift in Senate control could change the path for the CLARITY Act, reshape committee leadership and bring closer scrutiny of Trump’s crypto businesses.
Democrats have won control of the US Senate after flipping Republican-held seats in Texas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa, according to the Associated Press.
The majority was secured after Democrat Senator Josh Turek won the Senate race for Iowa, bringing Democrats and independents who caucus with them to 51 seats.
The result reshapes the outlook for the stalled CLARITY Act and determines which lawmakers lead committees overseeing the industry.
Democratic control could also bring more congressional scrutiny of Trump-linked crypto businesses and regulators’ decisions. Control of the Senate could also affect confirmation of future presidential nominees to regulatory posts.
“It’s too early to say exactly what this means for crypto, but one thing is clear: nothing will pass without cross-partisan support,” Jerome de Tychey, president of Ethereum France and co-founder of EthCC, told Cointelegraph.
“The CLARITY Act failed its Senate procedural vote 49 to 50 in September, and if it isn’t passed by January, the next Congress starts again from scratch. So the industry will have to go back to the table and make the case for blockchain again, on substance.”
De Tychey said some Democratic demands could help strengthen the industry’s regulatory framework.
“Conflict-of-interest rules and customer protection obligations are things a mature industry should welcome. In Europe, we already live with them under MiCA,” he said, referring to the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation.
However, he warned against allowing crypto policy to become entrenched along party lines.
“The biggest risk for crypto in America is for it to become entrenched as a partisan issue; that could set the US back several years.”
Fred Hsu, co-founder and CEO of D3, a core contributor to Doma Protocol, similarly said durable regulation would require support from both parties.
“The midterms are a good reminder that the industry can’t rely on one party to deliver them, and should be making its case to lawmakers on both sides now,” Hsu said in comments provided ahead of the election.
Related: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold

articles.title: Kamino links most of CEO’s KMNO vesting to valuation while holders have no foundation revenue claim
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Most of Michael Weisz’s KMNO allocation requires sustained valuation milestones, according to Kamino’s November 3 release.
- Kamino’s foundation commits $20 million over 24 months, while denying tokenholders a revenue, distribution or equity claim.
- DefiLlama’s November 3 snapshot tracked $607,996 in 30-day protocol revenue and zero holder revenue.
Michael Weisz, CEO of Kamino, has tied most of his KMNO allocation to sustained token valuations, according to the Solana lending protocol’s November 3 disclosure. The same announcement tells holders that owning the token gives them no claim on foundation revenue, distributions or equity.
Kamino’s November 3 release describes both the CEO’s incentive arrangement and a $20 million foundation commitment to support its long-term growth plans over the next 24 months. It leaves capital allocation as the step between money accruing to the foundation and any future financial benefit for holders.
Most of Weisz’s KMNO allocation vests only when progressively higher valuation milestones are reached and sustained, the release says. A temporary increase in price does not satisfy the requirement.
That condition concerns most of his allocation. The release does not say that every founder, contributor or investor allocation follows the same rules, and it supplies neither the numerical milestones nor the period for which each must be sustained.
For holders, the incentive aligns part of the CEO’s compensation with sustained token valuations.
Kamino says the foundation has no shareholders, members or beneficiaries, operates under an independent board, and receives all onchain and offchain revenue and intellectual property. Its description places the protocol’s earnings and the foundation’s broader resources within one organization.
The release then states the limit on what that structure means for holders: “KMNO is not a claim on Foundation revenue, distributions or equity.”
Protocol earnings and holder returns
DefiLlama’s Kamino data, captured at 20:10 UTC on November 3, makes the economic distinction concrete. Over the preceding 30 days, it recorded $5 million in fees, $607,996 in protocol revenue and $0 in tracked holder revenue.
Each number answers a different question. Fees measure charges generated by tracked activity. Protocol revenue measures the portion retained by the protocol. Holder revenue tracks value reaching holders, rather than assuming everything the protocol earns reaches tokenholders.
For Kamino’s lending products, DefiLlama includes interest, liquidation charges and origination charges in fees. Revenue includes interest spreads, part of liquidation charges and all origination charges; for liquidity products, it includes the protocol’s share of liquidity fees.
The $5 million fee total therefore cannot be read as foundation income available for distribution. Even the narrower $607,996 protocol-revenue figure is not a complete statement of foundation earnings, particularly given Kamino’s description of offchain revenue accruing there too.
KMNO’s market snapshot gives scale to the holder-value question: at 20:12 UTC on November 3, CryptoSlate displayed a price of about $0.034, a $200 million market capitalization and $20 million in 24-hour trading volume.
Kamino says the foundation holds reserves beyond its $20 million growth commitment. That commitment describes spending on expansion over two years, rather than a distribution to tokenholders or revenue already earned.
For someone evaluating KMNO, protocol revenue shows what tracked operations retain. Assessing a future holder benefit requires a further explanation of how foundation resources would be allocated, including what is spent on growth, retained in reserves or used in a potential token-support program.
The release cautions that future plans, including potential programs supporting KMNO, may change. Holders can assess the growth commitment and executive alignment now, but any future program will need its own terms before they can judge what benefit it delivers.

articles.title: ZachXBT Names French Bank in Alleged $133M Crypto Theft
articles.text:
ZachXBT identifies French bank as alleged victim of $133M crypto theft
The French bank has not confirmed its alleged involvement in the crypto theft, which ZachXBT said could have resulted in losses exceeding $133 million.
Onchain investigator ZachXBT has identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million, warning that total losses could be higher.
On Wednesday, the pseudonymous crypto sleuth said the institution, which he described as having $235 billion in assets, was allegedly exploited over multiple days. He also suggested that additional losses may have occurred through over-the-counter (OTC) transactions that were not included in earlier estimates.
“I suspect the amount stolen is larger when accounting for OTC activity,” ZachXBT said.
The bank’s alleged involvement has not been independently verified, and ZachXBT has not disclosed how the attackers gained access to the funds.
Cointelegraph contacted Crédit Mutuel Arkéa for comment but had not received a response by publication.
The disclosure follows ZachXBT’s initial report on Monday, when he identified over $106 million in suspicious withdrawals from centralized exchanges.
On Tuesday, he raised the estimated losses to over $133 million after discovering another $27 million in withdrawals, some of which occurred after his initial warning.
Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery previously traced withdrawals from accounts at Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX. It found that approximately $63 million in stablecoins had been converted into Ether (ETH) within four hours.
Kraken and Crypto.com subsequently told Cointelegraph they had restricted accounts or blocked funds associated with the suspected theft. Both exchanges said their platforms remained secure.
Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US

articles.title: Bitcoin rockets above $80,000 for first time since Binance hack despite Democrats sweep, but a historical crash looms
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 despite Democrats taking control of Congress, extending its recovery from the $75,600 election-night low.
- CoinShares says political gridlock may hurt crypto firms more than Bitcoin, while CryptoQuant signals that sellers are nearing exhaustion.
- Yet demand remains weak, and Bitcoin's historical post-midterm rallies have included crashes of nearly 50% before prices recovered.
Bitcoin surged more than 5% from its election-night low to reclaim $80,000 for the first time since Binance's record hack.
The cryptocurrency extended its recovery from approximately $75,600 on Wednesday, shaking off concerns that Democrats' takeover of Congress would undermine President Donald Trump's crypto-friendly agenda.
According to CoinGlass data, this rally liquidated $453.32 million in the past hour, with most of the losses coming from short traders. These losses reach $913.34 million over the past 24 hours.
CoinGlass heatmap screenshot supplied Nov. 4, 2026. Only tiles with a readable dollar value are included; smaller coins are omitted. 'Other' is the heatmap's labeled group, not a calculated remainder. BTC liquidations were 96.3% short and ETH 57.6% short. Values are rounded liquidated position amounts, not traders' net losses. Snapshot time was not shown.
The rally comes less than a week after Binance suffered a $6.34 billion security breach that sent shockwaves through the digital asset market, triggering withdrawals and intensifying an already difficult period for Bitcoin investors.
James Butterfill, head of research at CoinShares, told CryptoSlate that the Democratic sweep had largely been priced into Bitcoin before the election, creating room for a relief rally as political uncertainty dissipated.
His assessment reflects a growing distinction between the potential consequences of divided government for the wider crypto industry and Bitcoin itself.
Butterfill expects Democratic control to complicate efforts to advance the CLARITY Act, while potential investigations into Trump-linked cryptocurrency businesses could divert political attention from regulatory reform.
However, he argued that exchanges, token issuers and other companies requiring new regulatory permissions would be more vulnerable to those developments than Bitcoin.
He said that the cryptocurrency's direction remains more closely tied to real yields, dollar liquidity and exchange-traded product flows.
The broader financial markets have already begun reflecting that shift in attention.
According to institutional trading platform Talos, Bitcoin's DVOL, a gauge of expected volatility, declined 6%, while Wall Street's VIX fell 10% as reduced uncertainty encouraged systematic buying across risk assets.
The retreat in volatility coincided with a weaker dollar and declining Treasury yields, providing a more favorable backdrop for Bitcoin's recovery.
BTC sellers are running out of ammunition
On-chain data suggests the rally is arriving as the selling pressure that dominated Bitcoin's recent decline begins to weaken.
CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said the firm's seller exhaustion model has fallen to levels historically associated with bear-market lows.
The indicator compares the proportion of Bitcoin supply held at a profit with average monthly volatility to assess whether existing holders still have enough incentive to keep selling.
Its latest reading follows a correction of more than 10% from Bitcoin's previous high, during which short-term holders appear to have realized profits and reduced their exposure.
Previous episodes of similarly depressed selling activity have coincided with the formation of market bottoms, although the indicator offers no assurance that prices will immediately recover.
Darkfost identified a critical weakness in the current market: buyers have yet to demonstrate the same conviction as the sellers who recently exited. He said:
“Even if sellers have calmed down, demand is still needed, and Bitcoin is still short of it.”
That concern is especially relevant after three consecutive trading sessions of withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin ETFs, which have deprived the market of an important source of institutional demand.
While the retreat in selling pressure has allowed Bitcoin to recover above $80,000, sustaining that advance will require fresh capital to absorb any renewed profit-taking.
Bitcoin's perfect midterm record conceals a nearly 50% crash
Bitcoin's latest recovery also coincides with a historical pattern that has delivered substantial gains following every US midterm election since 2010.
CryptoQuant data shows the flagship crypto asset has risen over the subsequent 12 months in all four election cycles, generating a median return of 63%.
Those gains occurred under different political arrangements, including the 2018 midterms, when Democrats captured the House while Republicans retained the Senate.
Bitcoin gained 45.8% over the following year, while the comparable returns after the 2014 and 2022 elections reached 36.8% and 80.8%, respectively.
However, those annual figures conceal significant losses suffered by investors who bought immediately after the votes.
Bitcoin plunged 49.7% within approximately six weeks of the 2018 election before recovering. The cryptocurrency suffered a 39.8% drawdown following the 2014 vote and an 18.5% decline after the 2022 midterms, when the collapse of FTX destabilized the market.
Low percentage-change markers transcribed from the supplied CryptoQuant 365-day post-midterm chart. These are post-election lows, not single-day losses or dollar losses. Figures are shown to one decimal point as labeled; the dashboard did not expose raw data or precise calculation conventions. Other closing-price series differ, notably for 2014 and 2022. The 2026 cycle is excluded.
The apparent election effect also coincides with another recurring feature of Bitcoin's history.
US midterms occur every four years, roughly matching Bitcoin's halving schedule. CryptoQuant found that each election since 2010 occurred about 17 to 25 months before the next halving.
The 2014, 2018 and 2022 votes followed major bear markets, meaning the subsequent rallies unfolded as Bitcoin emerged from steep declines.
That relationship faces a different test in 2026.
Bitcoin entered Tuesday's election with a 20.4% gain over the preceding three months, compared with losses of 44% in 2014, 8.3% in 2018 and 16.5% in 2022.
That leaves this year's market in a materially different position from the previous three cycles, potentially weakening the relevance of the historical post-election returns.
Talos' seasonal figures provide another complication. Bitcoin lost 7.4% in October, and November subsequently recorded declines in three of the five previous years when October ended lower, including 2018 and 2025.
That is why Kelly Ye, Talos' head of research, cautioned against extrapolating the initial relief rally into a sustained recovery. She said:
“First reactions aren't always the right ones.”

articles.title: US midterms: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving crypto rules
articles.text:
1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold
Crypto executives expect US regulators to drive crypto policymaking regardless of the midterm election outcome.
With voting underway in the US midterm elections and control of Congress at stake, Maylea Ma, deputy general counsel at 1inch, said she expects federal agencies to drive the next phase of crypto regulation.
The election could reshape the path forward for the stalled CLARITY Act, but Ma said “real movement” in US digital-asset regulation over the next few years will come from the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Treasury, rather than Congress.
Ma said those agencies were increasingly engaging with crypto projects. However, agency engagement does not provide the stability the industry had hoped to secure through legislation.
“The long-term goal, of course, remains a statute that cannot be reversed every time a government changes,” said Ma.
That uncertainty also matters to institutional investors, according to Michael Ho, co-founder of D3, the team behind Doma Protocol.
“With the market structure bill stalled, US crypto policy continues to rest on agency guidance that a future administration can reverse, and that keeps serious capital waiting,” Ho said.
“Whatever the result, clear rules written into law are what will bring institutional capital into tokenized real-world assets.”
In August, the SEC proposed a framework for crypto fundraising, including exemptions for certain token offerings and a safe harbor from treatment as investment contracts. In September, it also updated staff guidance covering token buybacks, crypto networks and staking receipt tokens.
The CFTC, meanwhile, submitted a crypto market regulatory plan for White House review on Sept. 17, two days after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act.

articles.title: US stock perpetuals win clearance, but stock-market halts can still block exits
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The CFTC said individual-equity perpetual futures could begin trading on eligible exchanges, bringing them under joint securities and futures oversight.
- Kalshi says stock-perp positions cannot be opened or closed during scheduled closures, leaving holders exposed to different reopening prices.
- Coinbase's filed controls address halts and disrupted funding, while its public records do not establish a customer launch.
The CFTC said on Nov. 3 that US stock perpetual futures could begin trading on eligible regulated exchanges. These contracts track share prices without a fixed expiration date, but holders remain subject to stock-market halt rules that can interrupt an exit.
Chairman Michael Selig said the contracts had been deemed approved under Regulation 40.3. Eligible venues are designated contract markets also notice-registered with the SEC as securities exchanges, bringing the products into the agencies' joint security-futures framework.
Permission and access are separate
Kalshi says it now offers single-stock perpetuals, with no expiration date, but explicitly warns that they do not trade 24/7. Markets follow schedules with regular closures, and customers cannot open or close positions while a market is closed. Access requires a perpetuals application and educational tutorial; leverage depends on the stock and position size.
For Coinbase, the individual CFTC product record still displayed “Approval Pending” when checked Nov. 4, while the SEC's rulemaking index marked its separate customer-margin proposal withdrawn. Those entries do not overturn the Nov. 3 announcement, but neither establishes a Coinbase customer launch or final terms.
Coinbase's September filing describes cash-settled futures on stocks and ETF shares, without ownership of the underlying shares. Its product submission uses AAPL as a representative specification and makes listing contingent on approvals. Its proposed controls apply to Coinbase's design, rather than setting the terms for every venue.
Securities industry trade group SIFMA's Nov. 2 letter sought further review of proposals from Bitnomial, Coinbase, Kalshi and Nadex, raising concerns about manipulation, thin-liquidity trading and classification.
Under the security-futures halt requirement, a future on a single security must stop trading whenever that security is under a regulatory halt, subject to an applicable exemption. The agencies' joint-rule explanation says exemptions from both sets of requirements are needed.
These controls protect investors by allowing information to circulate and markets to regain order. Their immediate consequence is that an affected holder cannot use a closing trade in the halted contract to reduce exposure.
Buying or selling the same stock, or using its options, cannot be assumed to solve that problem: those markets generally honor the underlying regulatory halt too. A broader-market instrument might remain available during a company-specific interruption, but it leaves company-specific risk.
A venue-only derivatives outage presents a different case. If the cash market or another relevant instrument remains open and accessible, a separate trade may offset some exposure. That is a conditional hedge, dependent on access and liquidity, and it leaves the original perpetual open.
Coinbase's filed Rule 1207 would subject its contracts to US equity market-wide circuit breakers and coordinated halts, while also allowing restrictions for corporate actions, market disruptions and index-price or data outages. Reopening would follow the end of the halt condition and an exchange determination that resumption meets investor-protection and orderly-market requirements. The underlying stock reopening would not, by itself, promise an immediate futures exit.
Funding and price fallbacks leave the position open
Funding payments are cash adjustments on open positions. Changing their calculation is separate from executing a closing trade.
Coinbase's September product submission describes hourly funding and proposes trading from Sunday at 8 p.m. through Friday at 5 p.m. Eastern. Its index design checks input freshness, removes outliers, uses median pricing and falls back to a reference when inputs are insufficient.
The filed framework permits substitute price inputs and allows funding to be suspended, deferred or modified during disruption. The product appendix specifies no funding-rate publication for an entire hour in which trading is closed, paused or halted.
Neither a fallback price nor a funding pause closes the position or guarantees a trade at the reference value. Kalshi separately uses daily funding at 4 p.m. Eastern and warns that closures can leave holders facing a different reopening price. Adverse moves may push an account below maintenance margin and trigger liquidation.

articles.title: Stacks (STX) Bitcoin Bonds: How BTC Earns While Staying in Self-Custody
articles.text:
Key Takeaways
- Stacks’ Bitcoin bond lets holders earn yield paid in BTC, with a 3% target annual yield per bond, while their Bitcoin stays on the Layer 1 (L1), in their own custody. The yield comes from BTC that miners spend to mine Stacks blocks, not from lending out participants' coins.
- Every bonded Bitcoin requires STX worth 5% of its value to be held and locked for the six-month term, making STX the staking capacity for Bitcoin. The first two bonds brought in about 735 BTC, and Bonding Period 2 alone locked 6.7 million STX.
- Two upgrades planned for 2027 are designed to deepen demand for STX capacity, alongside STX’s longer-term role as the gateway to Bitcoin capital markets. Neither upgrade is live yet.
This article is brought to you by Stacks.
Most Bitcoin does nothing. It sits in cold storage, ETPs and corporate treasuries, holding value but earning nothing. Until now, making it productive has usually meant handing it to someone else: a lender, an exchange or a yield platform. That trade-off between yield and custody is exactly what the 2022 lender collapses exposed.
Stacks offers a different route. Through its Bitcoin bond, holders lock BTC on the Bitcoin Layer 1 (L1), maintain custody of their coins, and earn yield paid in BTC. The bond is the first building block of what Stacks calls Bitcoin Capital Markets: markets where Bitcoin earns, collateralizes and trades while staying secured by Bitcoin finality.
This article covers what that gives a Bitcoin holder, how the bond works, and why STX sits at the center of it as the staking capacity every bonded Bitcoin requires.
What Bitcoin Capital Markets Give a BTC Holder
Holders of stocks and bonds take three things for granted: their assets can earn, they can be borrowed against, and they can be traded. For Bitcoin, each of these has typically required leaving the Bitcoin network or giving up custody. Stacks is built to deliver all three while the underlying security stays with Bitcoin.
- Earn: Bond BTC for a fixed term and earn yield paid in BTC. The Bitcoin stays on the L1, in the holder's custody, for the life of the bond.
- Collateralize (planned for 2027): A planned self-custodial lending product would let bonded BTC back a stablecoin loan while it keeps earning yield. The existing Stacks ecosystem already has hundreds of BTC deployed in lending through protocols such as Zest Protocol.
- Trade: Bitcoin-based assets trade on Stacks DeFi venues such as Bitflow, the network's main DEX, alongside products like Hermetica's Bitcoin-backed, yield-bearing synthetic dollar.
Activity on Stacks settles with Bitcoin finality, so it inherits the security of the Bitcoin network rather than relying on a separate chain's guarantees.
Institutions now hold Bitcoin as a form of capital through ETPs, corporate treasuries and custodians, and many want to put it to work without handing custody to a lender or platform. The Stacks bond lets them earn BTC yield while their Bitcoin stays on the L1.
How the Bitcoin Bond Works
A Bitcoin bond lets a participant commit BTC for a fixed term and earn BTC in return, without moving that BTC off the Bitcoin L1. In practice, it works in four steps:
- Bond BTC. The participant bonds Bitcoin for a six-month term. The BTC stays on the Bitcoin L1, in the holder's custody.
- Pair it with STX. Each bond requires STX as staking capacity, currently worth 5% of the BTC value bonded. That STX stays locked until the bond matures.
- Earn BTC. Participants earn rewards paid in native BTC. Each bond has a 3% target annual yield, set before the bond opens and fixed for its term. The next section explains where that BTC comes from.
- Mature and repeat. At the end of the term, the bond matures and the STX unlocks, with new bonding periods open roughly every month.
The first bond, the Genesis Bond, sold out in September 2026. Its first participants were 21Shares, HashKey Cloud, UTXO Management (the asset management arm of public Bitcoin treasury company Nakamoto Inc) and Sypher Capital. At quarter-end, it had 230 BTC bonded.
Bonding Period 2 widened participation through liquid Bitcoin staking and added 505 BTC, bringing the combined total to about 735 BTC.
The current phase, PoX-5, is a deliberate bootstrap with a whitelist of anchor participants. The end-state design, PoX-6, is planned for 2027 as an open auction (covered below). According to Stacks, no other product currently offers BTC-denominated yield for self-custodial Bitcoin staking.
Where the BTC Yield Comes From
The yield is paid by Stacks miners. It does not come from lending out participants' Bitcoin, and it is not paid in a newly issued token.
The source is Stacks' consensus mechanism, Proof of Transfer (PoX). It works like this:
- Miners bid BTC. To win the right to produce a Stacks block, miners commit BTC in a transaction on the Bitcoin network. The more BTC a miner commits, the better its chance of winning the block.
- The winning miner earns STX. The miner that produces the block receives the Stacks block reward, paid in STX, plus transaction fees.
- The BTC goes to participants. The BTC that miners commit is not burned or kept by Stacks. It is transferred to the network's participants, which today means those who bond BTC and lock STX capacity.
In effect, miners pay BTC to receive STX from economic activity, and that BTC flows to bond participants. Proof of Transfer has distributed 4,224 BTC this way since the network launched in January 2021.
For a Bitcoin holder, this means:
- The yield comes from outside your position. Your BTC is not lent, rehypothecated or moved off the L1 to generate it. The BTC you earn is spent by miners competing for Stacks blocks.
- Each bond has a 3% target annual yield, set before the bond opens and fixed for its term.
STX: The Staking Capacity for Bitcoin
The asset being staked in a Stacks bond is Bitcoin. STX is the capacity that unlocks it. To bond BTC and earn BTC yield, a participant must hold and lock STX worth a set share of the bonded BTC, currently 5%, for the full bond term.
That makes STX a capacity asset, a different category of token design. Most token demand comes from inside a protocol's own economy: fees, governance or rewards paid in the same token. Here, demand comes from outside: from Bitcoin holders who want to earn yield. Every Bitcoin that enters a bond creates proportional demand for STX that must be held and locked.
The amount of STX a bond requires depends on three values based on the below formula:
STX required = BTC bonded × capacity ratio × (BTC price ÷ STX price).
Because the capacity ratio is set in value terms, the number of STX needed moves with both prices. If BTC rises relative to STX, each bonded Bitcoin requires more STX. If STX rises relative to BTC, it requires fewer.
Institutional STX locked as capacity is taken off the market for the bond’s six-month term and can’t be sold or traded until the bond matures.
What the First Two Bonds Show
The first two bonds show the mechanism working. Bonded BTC more than doubled from 230 BTC in the Genesis Bond to 505 BTC in Bonding Period 2. Bonding Period 2 alone required 6.7 million STX to be locked alongside its 505 BTC.
Across the network, staked STX rose from 392 million after the PoX-5 hard fork to 493 million after Bonding Period 2, an increase of about 26%.
Bonds run for six months, and new bonding periods open monthly. Each new bond adds a fresh cohort of locked STX, on top of earlier cohorts that have not matured yet. Bonds 3 and 4 will each be 1,000 BTC, about double the size of Bonding Period 2. The table below shows how locked STX would build up if every new bond were that size.
| Month | New cohort locked (STX) | Cohort maturing (STX) | Total bond capacity locked (STX) | 
| 1 | 13.3M | 0 | 13.3M | 
| 2 | 13.3M | 0 | 26.6M | 
| 3 | 13.3M | 0 | 39.9M | 
| 4 | 13.3M | 0 | 53.2M | 
| 5 | 13.3M | 0 | 66.5M | 
| 6 | 13.3M | 0 | 79.8M | 
| 7 | 13.3M | 13.3M | 79.8M | 
Illustrative only. Assumes monthly bonds of 1,000 BTC each at Bonding Period 2 prices (about 13,300 STX per BTC) and a six-month term.
With six overlapping cohorts, about 79.8 million STX would be locked at any given time, around 16% of the 493 million STX currently staked, and larger bonds would raise that level further. Taking that much STX off the market could also support its value, which would make STX block rewards more valuable to miners, incentivizing them to spend more BTC to win those blocks. Because each bond’s 3% target annual yield is set in advance, more BTC from miners means more Bitcoin can be bonded at that target, so each bond helps create room for a larger one.
How Bonds Compare to Token Buybacks
The closest familiar comparison is a token buyback. Both create a demand sink that takes tokens out of circulation, but they are funded and sustained very differently.
|  | Token buyback | Stacks Bitcoin bond | 
| Funded by | The protocol's own treasury or revenue | Outside BTC capital seeking yield | 
| What happens to tokens | Bought and held or burned | Held and locked for the bond term | 
| Scales with | Protocol revenue | The amount of Bitcoin entering bonds | 
| Duration | Permanent if burned; otherwise at treasury discretion | Temporary per cohort; STX unlocks at maturity | 
Locked STX is not removed for good: each cohort unlocks when its bond matures. The demand holds up only if new bonds keep replacing maturing ones, which is why the overlapping monthly cohorts above are central to the model. In exchange, the sink is funded by external Bitcoin rather than by the protocol spending its own resources, and it grows with every bond.
What 10,000 Bonded BTC Would Mean for STX
At Bonding Period 2 prices, 10,000 bonded BTC would require about 133 million STX to be held and locked, roughly 27% of the 493 million STX currently staked.
The calibration point is Bonding Period 2 itself: 6.7 million STX for 505 BTC, or roughly 13,300 STX per bonded Bitcoin. Applying that rate to larger bond sizes gives the following:
| BTC bonded | STX held and locked (approx.) | Share of 493M STX currently staked | 
| 735 (first two bonds combined) | 9.8M | 2.0% | 
| 1,000 | 13.3M | 2.7% | 
| 5,000 | 66.5M | 13.5% | 
| 10,000 | 133M | 27% | 
Illustrative only, at Bonding Period 2 prices. Because the capacity ratio is set in value terms, the STX amounts move with both the BTC and STX prices.
For perspective, 10,000 BTC is a small slice of the Bitcoin held by ETPs and corporate treasuries today. The table is illustrative rather than a forecast, but it shows that STX demand scales directly with the amount of Bitcoin that chooses to earn yield through Stacks.
The Roadmap: Three Levers for STX Demand?
Two upgrades planned for 2027 are designed to deepen demand for STX capacity. Neither is live yet.
Lever 1: An open auction for capacity (planned, PoX-6). Today, capacity goes to a whitelist of anchor participants. Under PoX-6, STX bids would determine how much BTC each participant can bond. Allocation would shift from whitelisted capacity to competitive bidding for a limited supply, turning STX capacity into a market in its own right.
Lever 2: Self-custodial borrowing (planned). A planned lending product would let bonded BTC, still earning yield, back a stablecoin loan. This mirrors the bond-and-repo pairing in traditional finance, where a bond earns its coupon while also serving as collateral for borrowing. For a Bitcoin holder, the same BTC would be productive twice: earning BTC yield and unlocking liquidity, all without leaving self-custody.
Greater capital efficiency makes bonding more attractive, more bonding raises demand for STX capacity, and an open auction lets that demand compete for a limited supply. Together, they would turn a single yield product into a capital market.
Lever 3: STX as the gateway to Bitcoin capital markets (long term). Beyond the two 2027 upgrades, STX’s longer-term role is as the entry point to the markets that form on Stacks. Staking BTC requires STX capacity, every transaction on Stacks pays its fees in STX, and borrowing against staked BTC is planned to build on that same staked position. Those fees go to the miners who produce Stacks blocks, so more activity on Stacks raises how much BTC miners are willing to commit, which flows back to staked BTC and can support more capacity for Bitcoin to come in and earn. For institutions and individual holders alike, that makes STX the gateway holding they need to deploy BTC into whichever yield, credit and trading markets develop on Stacks over time. As those markets grow, so does the role of the asset that gives access to them.
Conclusion: The First Primitive of Bitcoin Capital Markets
For Bitcoin holders, the Stacks bond answers a long-standing trade-off: BTC can now earn BTC yield while staying on the L1, in the holder's own custody. With planned lending and an active Stacks DeFi ecosystem, the same Bitcoin can also be collateralized and traded, all settled with Bitcoin finality.
The bond is the first primitive of these Bitcoin Capital Markets, and STX is the asset that unlocks access to them. Every Bitcoin that bonds requires STX to be held and locked. The first two bonds have already brought in about 735 BTC from participants including 21Shares and HashKey Cloud. If more of the Bitcoin sitting idle in treasuries and ETPs follows, demand for that capacity grows with it.
This article is for informational purposes only and is not financial advice.

articles.title: Bitcoin miners’ daily revenue per unit of computing power falls 8.7%
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin’s October 30 mining curve implied little network growth through December after difficulty rebounded 16.4%.
- November 2 spot hashprice fell 8.7% in a week, showing why a competition pause alone cannot restore dollar earnings.
- Matched forward sales can stabilize mining revenue rates, while power costs, uptime and contract performance still determine operating margins.
Bitcoin miners face weak dollar revenue even as the mining forward market priced in little additional competition through December, according to an October 30 analysis by mining data platform Hashrate Index. That could give miners a respite after difficulty’s 16.4% rebound.
Hashprice, the expected daily mining revenue for a unit of computing power, stood at $32.86 per petahash per second per day on November 2 at 18:00 UTC. That was down 8.7% from $35.99 a week earlier, according to the latest completed weekly snapshot.
Hashrate Index, Luxor’s mining data and research platform, put implied network computing power at 1,056 exahashes per second in November and 1,059 in December in its October 30 analysis. Both were near the approximately 1,062 EH/s average over the mining epoch that ended October 29.
Those are forward-implied levels, rather than observed future hashrate or scheduled difficulty changes. The linked September methodology assumes transaction fees of about 0.02 BTC per block when translating contract prices into implied network growth. Different fee outcomes can therefore change that interpretation.
The curve’s flattening followed a rise in difficulty from 127.45 trillion before September 19’s adjustment to 148.36 trillion on October 29. A pause would leave miners competing at that elevated level.
The November 2 update put average forward hashprice at $33.04 per PH/s/day for November through April 2027. This is an indicative revenue benchmark for that period, with actual execution dependent on agreed contract terms.
What a hedge still leaves exposed
A plateau in competition would limit additional pressure on revenue. Selling forward serves a separate purpose: stabilizing the benchmark revenue rate for output matched to the contract’s quantity and dates, if the contract performs.
In Luxor’s cash-settled contract, a seller receives the difference when the daily index falls below the agreed price and owes the difference when it rises above it. Matching the quantity and dates to actual output matters: the hedge does not ensure the machines keep producing.
A deliverable forward instead provides upfront buyer payment against delivery to Luxor’s mining pool, subject to seller credit checks and possible delivery margin. Luxor is the counterparty to both sides, and its order book displays buying and selling interest that its team must confirm as trades.
For operators with fixed dollar power costs, stabilizing the dollar revenue rate on matched output can improve cash-flow planning. Higher-cost fleets still need that revenue to cover electricity and other expenses; more efficient fleets have more room between gross receipts and costs.
Dollar hashprice also depends on Bitcoin’s price, fees and subsidy, alongside difficulty. Even if competition holds steady, weaker Bitcoin pricing or fees can reduce unhedged revenue.

articles.title: Evernorth’s XRP funding plan could raise $18 million less at lower share price
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Evernorth’s Cantor resale registration became effective October 30, satisfying one condition for its potential XRP financing.
- The original full share allowance illustrates $63 million at November 3’s close, before discounts and expenses.
- Actual XRP demand requires company share sales, settled cash and token purchases, which registration effectiveness alone does not establish.
Evernorth’s route to additional XRP buying cleared a registration condition on Oct. 30, but weaker shares have reduced the value of its original Cantor allowance to about $63 million in a closing-price illustration, before discounts and expenses.
The XRP treasury company’s resale registration became effective for a facility allowing it to sell up to 5,218,935 new shares to CF Principal Investments, a Cantor Fitzgerald affiliate. The milestone advances a potential source of treasury funding, while the amount ultimately raised depends on share sales and market prices.
At XRPN’s Nov. 3 close of $11.98, multiplying the original full share allowance produces approximately $63 million. The same calculation at the Oct. 22 reference price of $15.46 produces $81 million. The difference is about $18 million, or 22.5%.
Those figures measure the same original allotment at two dated closing prices.
The costs between shares and XRP
Evernorth’s Oct. 26 announcement described approximately $80 million of gross proceeds if the facility were fully executed at the Oct. 22 closing price. The commitment is denominated in shares, so a lower price means less cash from the same number of shares.
XRPN closed at $14.20 on Oct. 30, fell to $11.70 on Nov. 2 and recovered to $11.98 on Nov. 3. The latest completed session therefore left the stock below the reference price behind the earlier financing illustration.
The $62.5 million illustration at the Nov. 3 close equates to roughly 48.8 million XRP at a constant $1.28 per token. The $80.7 million illustration at the Oct. 22 close equates to 63.0 million XRP at that same token price. XRP was quoted near $1.28 at 13:10 UTC on Nov. 4, with its price down about 15.5% over 30 days.
Both conversions precede financing costs and allocation choices. Evernorth said some proceeds would support general corporate purposes, including XRP acquisitions and product development in the XRP ecosystem. It has not committed every financing dollar to buying the token.
Under the purchase agreement, Cantor ordinarily pays 97% of volume-weighted average price during the applicable purchase period. That is a 3% discount to the period’s average, rather than a promise to pay the closing price used in the illustration.
Purchases are also generally constrained by 20% of trading volume during that period, the company’s notice estimate and a 4.99% beneficial-ownership limit. Special terms apply to accepted requests above the ordinary participation percentage.
Evernorth also disclosed fee obligations: a nonrefundable $521,893.50 upfront commitment fee, a possible upward adjustment capped at $1 million in total commitment fees, expenses and a separate $200,000 qualified-independent-underwriter fee. The commitment-fee cap does not cover all costs.
Effectiveness satisfies one commencement condition. Other contractual requirements include a final prospectus and compliance, legal, listing and transfer-agent deliverables. Management decides whether and when to send purchase notices.
Cash receipts must connect to token purchases
Fresh XRP demand from this facility requires company share issuance, settled cash proceeds and subsequent XRP acquisition. Cantor’s later resales are a separate transaction: those receipts belong to Cantor. Ordinary secondary stock trading does not itself put cash in Evernorth’s treasury.
As of Nov. 4, the available disclosures did not establish actual facility shares sold, settled proceeds, remaining capacity or subsequent XRP acquisitions. The SEC filing record and company announcements leave those amounts unresolved, without establishing that the facility has gone unused.
The decisive next signal would be a dated company disclosure connecting share-sale receipts to XRP acquired. That would turn potential buying power into documented token demand.

articles.title: Polkadot lost $1.38 million after hacker exploited security flaw fixed four months earlier
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Polkadot lost $1.38 million after a hacker exploited a security flaw fixed in June but never deployed to affected production systems.
- The attacker bypassed an emergency shutdown to resume exploiting dotUSD, Polkadot's newly launched stablecoin, before a critical upgrade took effect.
- Parity is overhauling its security processes after the incident exposed weaknesses in vulnerability assessments, patch deployment and emergency response.
Polkadot's Treasury lost $1.38 million after an attacker exploited a vulnerability developers had fixed months before its new stablecoin launched.
In a Nov. 2 incident report, Parity Technologies, a blockchain infrastructure firm focused on the Polkadot and Kusama ecosystems, revealed that the security flaw had been identified and corrected in its codebase in June but never reached the affected production systems before the Oct. 24-26 attack.
The disclosure exposes a security breakdown surrounding dotUSD, Polkadot's decentralized stablecoin, which launched in October under the governance of the network's decentralized autonomous organization (DAO).
Unlike stablecoins issued by private companies, dotUSD was designed to operate without a centralized issuer, with DOT holders governing decisions through the network's OpenGov system.
However, the vulnerability predated the stablecoin's introduction. Parity initially classified the bug as medium severity because its assessment did not account for how the flaw could interact with dotUSD, which had not yet launched.
The developer later upgraded the vulnerability to critical after the attack exposed its financial consequences.
The breach also followed a public disclosure on Oct. 20, when the security researcher who originally reported the vulnerability posted a forum comment referencing the code fix.
Parity said the researcher removed the comment after being notified that it violated the company's bug bounty rules. The developer believes the disclosure may have given attackers enough information to identify and exploit the vulnerability.
The attacker ultimately manipulated Polkadot Asset Hub's cross-chain messaging system to reduce dotUSD's recorded supply without removing tokens from users' accounts.
That discrepancy distorted prices in the network's DOT/dotUSD liquidity pool, allowing traders to exchange dotUSD for DOT at artificial rates.
The Treasury, which was the pool's sole liquidity provider, absorbed approximately $1.381 million in losses.
Parity stressed that no users lost funds and dotUSD remained fully backed by USDT. However, the company could not establish whether the person who exploited the vulnerability also profited from the subsequent arbitrage trades.
Hacker bypassed emergency shutdown before Polkadot deployed security fix
The incident became more complicated when the attacker circumvented an emergency containment measure intended to stop the exploit.
After suspicious activity was detected on Oct. 24, Snowfork halted its consensus relayers, temporarily preventing further malicious transactions from reaching Polkadot through the Snowbridge network.
However, the attacker operated an independent relayer on Oct. 26, resuming the exploit approximately six hours before developers deployed the security upgrade through OpenGov.
The workaround was possible because Snowbridge allows independent participants to operate relayers, meaning Snowfork's intervention could interrupt its own infrastructure without permanently blocking the attacker's access.
Parity eventually closed the vulnerability through runtime upgrade 2.5.1 on Oct. 26 and rescued the remaining liquidity from the affected trading pool.
A second upgrade followed on Oct. 30, correcting dotUSD's recorded supply without changing individual account balances and resolving a separate issue that had disrupted Snowbridge.
The recovered dotUSD was returned to the Treasury, although the financial losses from the artificial trading activity remained.
Parity acknowledged that its existing security processes failed to account for the evolving risk introduced by new network functionality.
The company said it would strengthen vulnerability assessments, improve deployment checks and expand monitoring for unusual asset issuance.
It is also refining an automated AI-based security framework to identify potentially exploitable code changes earlier in development, while reassessing previously reported vulnerabilities for risks introduced by dotUSD.

articles.title: 195 năm thành lập tỉnh Tuyên Quang: Người trẻ khát vọng dựng xây quê hương
articles.text:
Sáng 4/11, UBND tỉnh Tuyên Quang long trọng tổ chức Lễ kỷ niệm 195 năm Ngày thành lập tỉnh. Dự buổi lễ có Ủy viên Bộ Chính trị, Phó Chủ tịch Quốc hội khóa XVI Đỗ Văn Chiến, cùng các đồng chí lãnh đạo, nguyên lãnh đạo tỉnh Tuyên Quang qua các thời kỳ.
Trình bày diễn văn tại buổi lễ, Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Tuyên Quang Phan Huy Ngọc nhấn mạnh, trải qua 195 năm hình thành và phát triển, vùng đất Tuyên Quang đã hun đúc nên truyền thống yêu nước, cách mạng, tinh thần đoàn kết, ý chí tự lực, tự cường. Những giá trị ấy được bồi đắp qua quá trình lao động, sáng tạo, xây dựng và bảo vệ quê hương của các thế hệ đồng bào các dân tộc.
Theo Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh, những thành quả đạt được hôm nay là kết tinh từ công sức, trí tuệ và sự cống hiến bền bỉ của nhiều thế hệ. Đây vừa là niềm tự hào, vừa là nền tảng để Đảng bộ, chính quyền và nhân dân các dân tộc trong tỉnh tiếp tục đoàn kết, vượt qua khó khăn, khai thác tiềm năng, lợi thế, thực hiện các mục tiêu phát triển kinh tế - xã hội, bảo đảm quốc phòng, an ninh trong giai đoạn tới.
Khép lại diễn văn, ông Phan Huy Ngọc nhấn mạnh 195 năm là hành trình của lao động, sáng tạo, dựng xây và bảo vệ quê hương; đồng thời khơi dậy những giá trị tốt đẹp như cần cù, nhân ái, lạc quan và gắn bó cộng đồng. Từ sự tri ân các thế hệ đi trước, ông gửi gắm quyết tâm tiếp tục xây dựng Tuyên Quang ngày càng phát triển.
Một điểm nhấn tại buổi lễ là phát biểu của hai đại diện tuổi trẻ Tuyên Quang. Không chỉ bày tỏ niềm tự hào về truyền thống quê hương, họ còn đề cập những việc người trẻ cần làm để đóng góp vào sự phát triển của tỉnh trong bối cảnh mới.
Với chủ đề “Khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo - Động lực bứt phá phát triển kinh tế - xã hội tỉnh Tuyên Quang trong kỷ nguyên mới”, anh Lê Thành Trung - Ủy viên Ban Chấp hành Tỉnh Đoàn, Phó Bí thư Chi đoàn Sở Khoa học và Công nghệ, cho rằng khoa học, công nghệ, đổi mới sáng tạo và chuyển đổi số đang mở ra cơ hội phát triển mới.
Từ thực tiễn công tác tại bộ phận chuyển đổi số, anh Trung chia sẻ đã tham gia tham mưu xây dựng khung kiến trúc chính quyền số phiên bản 4.0; quy chế quản lý, vận hành, khai thác dữ liệu dùng chung tại Trung tâm Giám sát, điều hành thông minh (IOC) cấp tỉnh; đề xuất phát triển kinh tế số và chương trình thúc đẩy ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI), dữ liệu lớn (Big Data) trong quản lý nhà nước, phát triển kinh tế - xã hội giai đoạn 2026-2030.
Theo anh Trung, sau sắp xếp đơn vị hành chính và triển khai mô hình chính quyền địa phương hai cấp, yêu cầu kết nối, phối hợp và quản trị trên địa bàn rộng hơn đặt ra nhiều nhiệm vụ mới. Vì vậy, cán bộ trẻ cần chủ động làm chủ công nghệ, đề xuất sáng kiến, dám nhận trách nhiệm, đồng thời hỗ trợ người dân, doanh nghiệp tiếp cận các nền tảng số, nhất là ở vùng sâu, vùng xa và khu vực biên giới.
Nếu câu chuyện của anh Trung gắn với công nghệ và quản trị hiện đại, phát biểu của anh Sùng Mạnh Hùng - cán bộ văn hóa xã Đồng Văn, lại mang đến góc nhìn từ chính đời sống vùng cao.
Là người dân tộc Mông sinh ra và lớn lên trên cao nguyên đá Đồng Văn, anh Hùng kể về tuổi thơ gắn với những dãy núi đá tai mèo, nương ngô bám đá và tiếng kèn Mông giữa núi rừng. Cuộc sống còn nhiều khó khăn, nhưng chính mảnh đất ấy đã hun đúc trong anh nghị lực vượt khó, tình yêu quê hương và niềm tự hào về nguồn cội.
Từ trải nghiệm của mình, anh Hùng cho rằng điều kiện sống và cơ hội phát triển giữa các vùng miền có thể khác nhau, nhưng khó khăn không thể trở thành rào cản khiến người trẻ từ bỏ ước mơ. Thanh niên cần chủ động học tập, làm chủ tri thức, nghề nghiệp, mạnh dạn khởi nghiệp và gắn khát vọng cá nhân với lợi ích gia đình, cộng đồng.
Đáng chú ý, đại diện thanh niên dân tộc Mông nhấn mạnh trách nhiệm gìn giữ bản sắc văn hóa trong quá trình phát triển. Theo anh, bảo tồn truyền thống không có nghĩa là khép mình trước cái mới. Người trẻ cần trân trọng tiếng nói, trang phục, phong tục, di sản văn hóa của các dân tộc; đồng thời bài trừ hủ tục lạc hậu, xây dựng nếp sống văn minh và ứng dụng công nghệ số để quảng bá hình ảnh con người, thiên nhiên, văn hóa Tuyên Quang.
Thay mặt tuổi trẻ các dân tộc trong tỉnh, anh Hùng khẳng định quyết tâm tiếp tục học tập, lao động, khởi nghiệp, ứng dụng khoa học công nghệ, tham gia các hoạt động an sinh xã hội và bảo tồn giá trị văn hóa dân tộc. Trong khi đó, anh Trung nhấn mạnh chất lượng công việc và hiệu quả phục vụ người dân phải là thước đo đóng góp của cán bộ trẻ.
Sau 195 năm hình thành và phát triển, Tuyên Quang bước vào chặng đường mới với những thời cơ và yêu cầu mới. Từ quản trị số đến phát triển sinh kế, từ đổi mới sáng tạo đến gìn giữ bản sắc, những người trẻ đang tìm cách tiếp nối truyền thống bằng chính tri thức, trách nhiệm và khát vọng cống hiến của mình.

articles.title: Bộ trưởng Chiến tranh Hegseth hứng 'bão' sau thất bại thảm hại của đảng Cộng hoà
articles.text:
Theo CNN, Hạ viện có thể bỏ phiếu luận tội người đứng đầu Lầu Năm Góc ngay trong tuần tới.
Lo ngại trước thất bại thảm hại trong cuộc bầu cử ngày 3/11, nhiều nghị sĩ Cộng hòa và đồng minh nhanh chóng tìm cách đổ lỗi cho ông Hegseth về kết quả bầu cử. Trong các cuộc trao đổi kín, họ cho rằng ông đóng vai trò chủ chốt trong việc thuyết phục Tổng thống Donald Trump tấn công Iran mà không có chiến lược rút lui, cũng như không có kế hoạch ứng phó với những hệ quả chính trị tất yếu.
Chiến dịch công kích quyết liệt này diễn ra bất chấp việc các chiến lược gia của đảng Cộng hòa tại Hạ viện và Thượng viện thừa nhận riêng rằng, những vấn đề của đảng không chỉ là cuộc chiến ở Iran, dẫn đến thất bại tương đương năm 2008 và sẽ mất nhiều năm để khắc phục. Tuy nhiên, vào thời điểm hiện tại, các lãnh đạo đảng vẫn tránh trực tiếp quy trách nhiệm cho ông Trump về thất bại này.
Ngay cả trong số các nghị sĩ Cộng hòa tại Hạ viện vượt qua đòn giáng ngày 3/11, không ai định quay lưng với tổng thống khi ông vẫn còn 2 năm nhiệm kỳ. Tuy nhiên, sự trung thành đó không dành cho ông Hegseth - vị bộ trưởng có phong cách đối đầu, người đã không tạo dựng được nhiều mối quan hệ hữu hảo tại Đồi Capitol kể từ khi tiếp quản quyền chỉ huy Lầu Năm Góc.
Các nghị sĩ Cộng hòa tại Hạ viện có thể sẽ bỏ phiếu trực tiếp phản đối Bộ trưởng Chiến tranh trong vài ngày tới. Hạ nghị sĩ Thomas Massie của đảng Cộng hoà nói với CNN rằng ông dự định khởi xướng cuộc bỏ phiếu luận tội ông Hegseth, khi Quốc hội trở lại làm việc vào tuần tới. Nhiều nguồn tin từ đảng Cộng hòa cho biết, họ kỳ vọng nghị quyết này sẽ được thông qua.
Nhiều nghị sĩ Cộng hòa nói với CNN rằng ông Hegseth đã phóng đại cơ hội Mỹ giành chiến thắng trong cuộc xung đột một cách nhanh chóng và dễ dàng. Họ cáo buộc ông tiếp tục thúc đẩy leo thang quân sự, dù có rất ít dấu hiệu cho thấy cách làm này có thể buộc Iran đầu hàng.
Theo họ, cuộc xung đột sau đó đã biến thành vũng lầy, khiến Mỹ bị cuốn vào Trung Đông vô thời hạn, làm trầm trọng thêm cuộc khủng hoảng chi phí sinh hoạt và kích hoạt làn sóng phản đối của cử tri đối với đảng Cộng hòa trong cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ.
Ngày 4/11, Phó Tổng thống JD Vance đưa ra tuyên bố đáng chú ý, rằng “lý do chúng ta thất bại là cuộc chiến”, mặc dù ông không quy trách nhiệm cụ thể cho bất kỳ cá nhân nào.
“Mọi thứ đang bắt đầu chuyển hướng” liên quan đến cuộc chiến và ông Hegseth, một cựu quan chức cấp cao của Lầu Năm Góc nhận định. “Đây chủ yếu là chiến dịch do Bộ Chiến tranh dẫn dắt, bởi chính các ông đã lựa chọn sử dụng hành động quân sự để giải quyết một vấn đề đối ngoại”, cựu quan chức nói.
Ông Trump bảo vệ
Tổng thống Trump có thiện cảm cá nhân với ông Hegseth, và đã nói với các trợ lý rằng ông Hegseth nên chống trả những nỗ lực luận tội hoặc điều tra.
“Chỉ mới 2 ngày trước, tổng thống còn ở trong phòng cùng ông ấy và nói: ‘Anh là người giỏi nhất của tôi. Anh là người tốt nhất mà tôi có’”, một quan chức tiết lộ.
Theo một nguồn tin, ông Trump cũng có thể cảm thấy cần phải giữ ông Hegseth ở lại nếu ông quyết định tiếp tục tiến hành các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào Iran. Ngoài ra, trong bối cảnh phe Dân chủ giành được đa số mới tại Thượng viện, các nỗ lực bổ nhiệm thành viên mới vào Nội các của chính quyền đương nhiệm sẽ trở nên phức tạp hơn.
Ngày 4/11, khi được hỏi về công việc của ông Hegseth, Tổng thống Trump đã bảo vệ chiến dịch quân sự và phủ nhận kế hoạch sa thải ông, đồng thời nói rằng Bộ trưởng Chiến tranh đang “làm rất tốt”.
“Nếu phải quyết định lại, tôi vẫn sẽ phải làm điều đó một lần nữa”, ông Trump nói về quyết định phát động chiến tranh.
Nhà Trắng lên án khả năng phe Dân chủ tiến hành các cuộc điều tra về Lầu Năm Góc. Người phát ngôn Lauren Bis nói trong một tuyên bố: “Nếu phe Dân chủ lựa chọn theo đuổi những cuộc điều tra giả tạo và các chính sách cực đoan của cánh tả, thì họ đang lựa chọn hành động chống lại người dân Mỹ.”
Tuy nhiên, một số nghị sĩ Cộng hòa cho rằng việc ông Trump tìm người để đổ lỗi cho những thất bại trong cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ chỉ còn là vấn đề thời gian, và họ coi ông Hegseth là mục tiêu hiển nhiên.

articles.title: Ngôi nhà mang nét Huế từ những vật liệu cũ và đồ thủ công
articles.text:
TPO - Những vật liệu đã qua sử dụng được đưa vào ngôi nhà với diện mạo mới, kết hợp hoa giấy, nghệ thuật giấy bồi và các chi tiết thủ công mang dấu ấn văn hóa Huế. Công trình hướng đến một không gian sống giản dị, gần gũi và yên tĩnh.
Thay vì lựa chọn những vật liệu hoàn toàn mới, ngôi nhà được thiết kế với nhiều chất liệu và đồ vật đã qua sử dụng. Những món đồ cũ được giữ lại, sắp đặt và kết hợp trong một tổng thể mới, tiếp tục phát huy giá trị sử dụng và lưu giữ dấu ấn của thời gian.
Cách tiếp cận này tạo nên nét riêng cho công trình, nơi vẻ đẹp không đến từ sự hoàn hảo hay đồng nhất của vật liệu mà từ những khác biệt về màu sắc, bề mặt và dấu vết sử dụng.
Điểm đáng chú ý là việc đưa các yếu tố văn hóa Huế vào không gian nội thất. Hoa giấy Thanh Tiên, một sản phẩm thủ công truyền thống của vùng đất cố đô, xuất hiện cùng những chi tiết lấy cảm hứng từ nghệ thuật giấy bồi.
Thay vì tái hiện nguyên vẹn hình ảnh một ngôi nhà Huế xưa, thiết kế sử dụng các chất liệu văn hóa quen thuộc và thể hiện chúng theo ngôn ngữ đương đại. Nhờ đó, những yếu tố truyền thống hiện diện một cách nhẹ nhàng, không khiến không gian trở nên nặng tính trang trí.
Ánh sáng tự nhiên cũng được chú trọng trong cách tổ chức nội thất. Những khoảng nắng đi vào từng góc nhỏ, làm nổi bật bề mặt vật liệu cũ, màu sắc của đồ thủ công và sự khác biệt giữa các chất liệu.
Sự kết hợp giữa ánh sáng, vật liệu tái sử dụng và những chi tiết thủ công tạo nên bầu không khí ấm áp, gần gũi. Không chạy theo sự cầu kỳ, ngôi nhà hướng đến nhịp sống chậm rãi, nơi con người có thể tạm rời những bận rộn thường ngày để dành thời gian nghỉ ngơi.
Thông qua việc tiếp tục sử dụng những món đồ cũ và đưa nghề thủ công truyền thống vào thiết kế, ngôi nhà cho thấy một cách tiếp cận gần gũi với văn hóa bản địa. Những chất liệu mang dấu ấn thời gian được kết hợp trong đời sống hiện đại, tạo nên một không gian có bản sắc riêng.
Từng thu hút hàng nghìn người tham gia, các phiên đấu giá đất tại Thanh Oai nay hạ nhiệt rõ rệt. Phiên mới nhất chỉ có 47 khách hàng, giá trúng cao nhất đạt 56,08 triệu/m2.
Lãi suất tiết kiệm hạ nhiệt, nhà đầu tư bắt đầu tính toán phân bổ dòng tiền sang bất động sản, kỳ vọng đón đầu cơ hội khi thị trường có thêm nguồn cung mới.
Nghe tin cả 3 căn hộ của gia đình cùng nằm trong diện sai phạm, ông Tuấn rơi vào cảnh thấp thỏm, ngày đêm lo lắng về nguy cơ phải rời nơi ở đã gắn bó nhiều năm.
Trong bối cảnh thị trường bước vào giai đoạn cạnh tranh dựa trên chất lượng thực và năng lực tạo giá trị bền vững, chuẩn mực ngày càng trở thành nền tảng định hình cách doanh nghiệp phát triển sản phẩm, tổ chức vận hành và xây dựng lợi thế dài hạn. Từ chất lượng được hiện thực hóa ở từng dự án đến khả năng duy trì sự nhất quán trên toàn hệ sinh thái sản phẩm, hành trình nâng chuẩn cũng chính là quá trình doanh nghiệp chuyển hóa những chuẩn mực thành năng lực cốt lõi, từ đó tạo ra giá trị ở quy mô ngày càng lớn.
Ngày 4/11/2026, MIK Group chính thức động thổ dự án The Harbor Skyline tại đảo Vũ Yên, Hải Phòng. Với quy mô gần 50ha, dự án được phát triển theo mô hình thành phố cao tầng trên đảo, đồng thời đánh dấu lần đầu dòng căn hộ cao tầng I Series của MIK Group hiện diện tại thành phố Cảng.
TPO - HĐND thành phố Hà Nội thông qua điều chỉnh danh mục dự án thí điểm nhà ở thương mại, đưa 14 khu đất rộng 109,1 ha ra khỏi danh sách và bổ sung 2 khu đất rộng 45,5 ha. Trong đó có 7 dự án nhà ở thương mại tại phường Vĩnh Hưng.
TPO - 35.000 căn chung cư có thể được mở bán tại Hà Nội năm sau; Người có tiền mặt bắt đầu săn bất động sản giá tốt; Ninh Bình đấu giá 360 lô đất 'vàng’, giá khởi điểm cao nhất 95 triệu đồng/m²; 3.790 căn hộ bỏ trống ở Thủ Thiêm có giá khởi điểm gần 18.300 tỷ đồng;... là những thông tin nổi bật của Bản tin Địa ốc 24H ngày 4/11.
Thay vì tập trung phát triển căn hộ hàng chục tỷ ở trung tâm, doanh nghiệp có thể đi ra xa hơn, tận dụng lợi thế giá đất và kết nối metro để tạo nguồn cung nhà ở 2-3 tỷ đồng.
Với mức thanh toán ban đầu 5%, The Emerald Boulevard thu hút sự chú ý trên thị trường bất động sản bằng giải pháp tài chính thiết thực, giúp khách hàng chủ động kế hoạch sở hữu căn hộ hạng A tại điểm đầu Quốc lộ 13.
TPO - Giữa không gian đô thị hiện đại của TP.HCM, ngôi nhà ba tầng gợi nhắc kiến trúc phố xưa qua mái ngói đỏ, cửa vòm, lam gỗ và sân lát gạch tàu. Những vật liệu quen thuộc được kết hợp với cách tổ chức không gian thông thoáng, đáp ứng nhu cầu sinh hoạt đương đại.
TPO - Chuyên gia đề xuất không giao dự án mới đối với những chủ đầu tư "chây ì", chậm làm thủ tục để cơ quan nhà nước cấp sổ hồng cho người dân là chế tài cần thiết để nâng cao trách nhiệm doanh nghiệp, song phải phân định rõ nguyên nhân chậm cấp sổ, tránh đẩy rủi ro về phía người dân.
Tựa như một biệt phủ vương giả ẩn mình giữa non nước Ninh Bình, Emeralda Resort Tam Cốc đã ghi dấu ấn với Giải Vàng (Gold Award) tại VMARK Hospitality · F&B Excellence Award 2026. Lấy cảm hứng từ kiến trúc truyền thống Bắc Bộ, dự án mở ra hành trình trải nghiệm văn hóa và di sản, đồng thời khẳng định giá trị của sự giao thoa giữa bản sắc địa phương, thiên nhiên và tiêu chuẩn nghỉ dưỡng đương đại.
TPO - 360 lô đất ở liền kề tại khu dân cư mới phía Đông Nhà thi đấu Thể dục thể thao tỉnh Ninh Bình được đưa ra đấu giá với tổng diện tích hơn 5,2ha, giá khởi điểm từ 44-94,65 triệu đồng/m². Tổng giá khởi điểm của toàn bộ khu đất lên tới hơn 3.000 tỷ đồng.
Những dự án nằm giữa cầu Rồng và cầu sông Hàn, sở hữu vị trí đắc địa bên dòng sông biểu tượng của Đà Nẵng. Với tầm nhìn khoáng đạt cùng khả năng kết nối thuận tiện tới khu vực trung tâm tạo nên lợi thế khác biệt, góp phần gia tăng sức hút của dự án trên thị trường căn hộ cao cấp tại thành phố biển.
Việc tuyến đường sắt Bến Thành - Cần Giờ thi công đồng loạt từ ngày 30/10 không chỉ góp phần mở rộng không gian phát triển hướng biển của TP.HCM, mà còn đặt nền móng giải quyết bài toán an cư thế hệ mới. Tại “Quận Nhất mới” Vịnh Tiên thuộc Vinhomes Green Paradise, khoảng cách giữa sự nghiệp tại trung tâm và chốn trở về bên thiên nhiên rừng - biển đang dần được xóa nhòa.

articles.title: Hoắc Kiến Hoa khiến Lâm Tâm Như sợ hãi
articles.text:
Trang HK01 đưa tin mới đây Hoắc Kiến Hoa tham gia show Tiểu S không vui do Từ Hy Đệ (Tiểu S) và Patrick dẫn dắt, để quảng bá cho tác phẩm mới Kỳ tích phòng cấp cứu. Nam diễn viên hiếm hoi chia sẻ về những ảnh hưởng của vai diễn đến cuộc sống cá nhân.
Theo Hoắc Kiến Hoa, quá trình quay phim Như Ý truyện kéo dài suốt một năm. Không gian quay khép kín, đoàn phim cũng không tổ chức các buổi liên hoan khiến nam diễn viên cảm thấy ngột ngạt.
Ngày nào nam diễn viên cũng phải học thuộc lời thoại bằng cổ văn. Sau mỗi ngày ghi hình, nam diễn viên thường trở về phòng để học thuộc kịch bản. Anh hóa thân vào nhân vật vua Càn Long đa nghi, nóng nảy với nhiều cảnh quát tháo khiến cảm xúc của Hoắc Kiến Hoa bị bào mòn. Thậm chí, nam nghệ sĩ còn phải lén uống rượu vì áp lực quá lớn.
Hoắc Kiến Hoa thừa nhận sau nửa năm khi đóng máy, anh vẫn chưa thoát khỏi vai diễn. "Vì đã sống trong bộ phim suốt một năm, khi trở về nhà, tôi vẫn nghĩ mình là hoàng đế. Ngay cả cách nói chuyện cũng quen dùng văn ngôn. Thậm chí lúc ăn cơm, tôi còn ngồi ngay ngắn rồi hô lớn: Nào! Dùng bữa!", Hoắc Kiến Hoa hài hước chia sẻ.
Ngoài ra, Hoắc Kiến Hoa cho biết trên phim anh nhiều lần tát và quát mắng phi tần khiến Lâm Tâm Như cảm thấy sợ hãi, đến mức không dám xem bộ phim.
Hoắc Kiến Hoa thừa nhận anh là ông bố yêu chiều con gái. Anh là người thường đưa đón con đi học. Thỉnh thoảng, nam diễn viên sẽ đeo kính râm và hỏi bé Cá Heo Nhỏ: "Thấy bố có giống người nổi tiếng không?", nhưng bất ngờ là con gái thường lạnh lùng phớt lờ anh.
Nam diễn viên thừa nhận con gái khá bướng bỉnh, nhưng thực ra rất tự hào khi có người khen bố điển trai.
Lâm Tâm Như và Hoắc Kiến Hoa phát triển tình cảm từ mối quan hệ bạn bè kéo dài 10 năm. Ngày 20/5/2016, phòng làm việc của Lâm Tâm Như xác nhận trên Weibo chuyện tình cảm với Hoắc Kiến Hoa.
Đến ngày 5/7 cùng năm, họ công bố tin vui kết hôn. Hôn lễ được tổ chức ở Bali (Indonesia) vào ngày 31/7/2016.Ngày 6/1/2017, Lâm Tâm Như sinh con gái Cá Heo Nhỏ tại Đài Loan (Trung Quốc).
Ban đầu, dư luận nghi ngờ Hoắc Kiến Hoa bị ép cưới. Biểu cảm lạnh lùng của anh tại hôn lễ càng củng cố tin đồn đó. Tuy nhiên, theo thời gian, hai người dần chứng minh cuộc hôn nhân giữa họ có tồn tại tình yêu.
Hoắc Kiến Hoa từng chia sẻ trong chương trình Có hẹn với Lỗ Dự hẹn hò rất vất vả, phải né tránh paparazzi. Tuy nhiên, sau khi công khai tình cảm, tối hôm đó, anh nắm tay Lâm Tâm Như đi ăn lẩu, cảm thấy vô cùng hạnh phúc.
Lâm Tâm Như từng tiết lộ chuyện tình cảm giữa họ không phải kiểu nồng cháy như phim thần tượng, mà thiên về bình dị và trầm lắng hơn.
Cô thừa nhận hai vợ chồng không phải lúc nào cũng đồng quan điểm trong việc nuôi dạy con. Nhưng nếu có khác biệt, họ trao đổi riêng tư, không tranh cãi trước mặt con. Cả hai cơ bản đều tôn trọng nhau và cũng kiên nhẫn trong cách chăm sóc, giáo dục bé Cá Heo Nhỏ.

articles.title: Xe hybrid của Hyundai lập kỷ lục doanh số ở Mỹ
articles.text:
Theo InsideEVs, có khoảng 29% tổng doanh số Hyundai tại Mỹ trong tháng 10 thuộc về các dòng xe hybrid.
Đây là tỷ trọng cao nhất từ trước tới nay của nhóm xe lai xăng-điện trong doanh số Hyundai tại Mỹ. Số liệu này xuất hiện khi khách hàng tiếp tục tìm kiếm các dòng xe tiết kiệm nhiên liệu, giữa bối cảnh giá xăng ở xứ cờ hoa vẫn duy trì ở mức cao.
Hyundai không tách riêng doanh số xe hybrid trong các báo cáo hàng tháng, thay vào đó gộp chung lại theo từng dòng xe. Hãng xe Hàn Quốc cho biết các phiên bản hybrid của Santa Fe và Palisade đã thiết lập kỷ lục doanh số mới trong tháng 10.
Ở diễn biến tương tự, doanh số mẫu xe thuần điện Hyundai Ioniq 5 đã tăng 21% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái để đạt 1.981 xe.
Tại thị trường Mỹ, Hyundai cho biết đã bán được 73.452 xe trong tháng 10, tăng 5% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái. Doanh số tích lũy từ đầu năm hiện đạt 770.916 xe, tăng 3% so với năm 2025.
Thương hiệu “cùng nhà” Kia cũng báo cáo doanh số chung và doanh số xe điện hóa đạt mức kỷ lục. Hãng này đã bán được 80.008 xe điện và xe hybrid trong tháng 10, nâng tổng doanh số tích lũy từ đầu năm đạt mức 747.394 xe.
Lượng tiêu thụ xe hybrid của Kia tại Mỹ cũng tăng vọt 114% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái, chủ yếu nhờ nhu cầu mạnh mẽ đối với các phiên bản hybrid của Kia Carnival cùng các dòng SUV như Sportage và Sorento.
Ở mảng thuần điện, doanh số Kia EV9 đã tăng mạnh 111% lên 1.406 xe, trong khi doanh số EV6 tăng 58% lên 803 xe. Mẫu xe giá rẻ Kia EV3 cũng sở hữu doanh số khá tích cực, đạt 976 xe trong tháng 10.
