articles.title: Bán hàng xuyên đêm, cuộc đua mới của các chuỗi cửa hàng tiện lợi
articles.text:
Lúc 2h sáng, khi phần lớn hàng quán đã đóng cửa, nhiều cửa hàng tiện lợi như Circle K, GS25 hay 7-Eleven vẫn duy trì hoạt động. Bên trong, đôi khi chỉ có vài khách mua hàng hoặc ngồi lại.
Khác với cửa hàng tạp hóa truyền thống, các chuỗi tiện lợi cung cấp cả không gian có điều hòa, wifi, chỗ ngồi và dịch vụ xuyên đêm. Khách ghé vào ban đêm có thể mua đồ ăn, tài xế dừng chân uống nước, sinh viên tìm chỗ ngồi học tập hoặc chờ đến giờ hẹn.
Đây là một trong những lợi thế giúp mô hình cửa hàng tiện lợi thu hút khách hàng tại các đô thị lớn. Tuy nhiên, việc duy trì hoạt động xuyên đêm cũng đặt ra bài toán về doanh thu và chi phí vận hành.
Thị trường Việt Nam còn dư địa mở rộng
So với Thái Lan, thị trường cửa hàng tiện lợi Việt Nam vẫn còn khoảng cách lớn về quy mô. Theo Thanachart Securities, Thái Lan có 21.652 cửa hàng tiện lợi thuộc kênh bán lẻ hiện đại vào năm 2024. Riêng mạng lưới 7-Eleven tại nước này đạt 15.945 cửa hàng vào cuối năm 2025.
Tại Việt Nam, 5 chuỗi lớn gồm Circle K, GS25, Ministop, FamilyMart và 7-Eleven có tổng cộng khoảng 1.455 điểm bán theo dữ liệu của NielsenIQ năm 2025. Cụ thể, Circle K có 507 cửa hàng, GS25 có 453, Ministop có 177, FamilyMart có 172 và 7-Eleven có 146.
Các thương hiệu đã tích lũy kinh nghiệm vận hành tại nhiều thị trường, từ quản trị ngành hàng, tổ chức chuỗi cung ứng đến phát triển thực phẩm chế biến sẵn.
Circle K và GS25 là hai cái tên có độ phủ đáng kể, chiếm khoảng 66% tổng số điểm bán của 5 chuỗi này. Ministop, FamilyMart, 7-Eleven tập trung mật độ dày đặc tại khu vực TPHCM và miền Nam, tốc độ mở rộng điểm bán thận trọng.
Có mặt tại Việt Nam từ năm 2008, Circle K xây dựng hình ảnh gắn với hoạt động xuyên đêm và nhóm khách hàng trẻ. GS25 khai thác lợi thế từ các sản phẩm mang phong cách Hàn Quốc. Trong khi đó, 7-Eleven, FamilyMart và Ministop có kinh nghiệm phát triển thực phẩm tiện lợi và quy trình quản lý chuỗi.
Thị trường vừa có thêm một đối thủ nội địa đáng chú ý. WinCommerce, đơn vị vận hành WinMart và WinMart+, đưa thương hiệu WiN ON vào thị trường cửa hàng tiện lợi 24/7 với 6 cửa hàng đầu tiên tại Hà Nội và TPHCM từ ngày 22/10.
Động thái này cho thấy doanh nghiệp nội địa cũng muốn tham gia sâu hơn vào phân khúc bán lẻ phục vụ nhu cầu mua sắm nhanh và ngoài giờ.
Cuộc đua bán hàng 24/7
Bà Linh Phạm, tư vấn trong lĩnh vực bán lẻ, cho rằng cửa hàng tiện lợi vẫn là mảng có nhiều cơ hội phát triển tại Việt Nam. Quá trình đô thị hóa, sự gia tăng của tầng lớp trung lưu và nhịp sống ngày càng bận rộn có thể thúc đẩy nhu cầu mua sắm nhanh, thực phẩm chế biến sẵn và dịch vụ ngoài giờ.
Thị trường vì thế đang bước vào giai đoạn cạnh tranh mới. Các thương hiệu ngoại có lợi thế về kinh nghiệm vận hành và nhận diện thương hiệu. Doanh nghiệp trong nước có ưu thế về nguồn hàng, mạng lưới phân phối và khả năng am hiểu khẩu vị người tiêu dùng.
Theo bà Linh, việc duy trì cửa hàng 24/7 có thể giúp doanh nghiệp khai thác thêm doanh thu từ mặt bằng và cơ sở vật chất đã đầu tư. Tiền thuê thường được tính theo tháng, trong khi hệ thống tủ mát, tủ đông và điều hòa vẫn cần vận hành để bảo quản hàng hóa. Mở cửa xuyên đêm vì thế giúp tận dụng những chi phí cố định này.
Tuy nhiên, mở cửa 24/7 không đồng nghĩa chắc chắn tăng hiệu quả kinh doanh. Doanh nghiệp phải tính toán doanh thu tăng thêm có đủ bù chi phí nhân sự, điện năng, an ninh và các khoản vận hành phát sinh hay không.
Mô hình cửa hàng tiện lợi cũng không chỉ cạnh tranh bằng hàng hóa. Với nhiều người trẻ, đây còn là nơi có thể ngồi lại, học tập, gặp bạn bè hoặc chờ đến giờ hẹn. Không gian có điều hòa, wifi và chỗ ngồi giúp cửa hàng trở thành điểm dừng chân ngoài mục đích mua sắm.
Ông William Gramond, Giám đốc Bộ phận cho thuê thương mại, Savills Hà Nội, cho rằng số lượng cửa hàng không nên là mục tiêu duy nhất khi mở rộng. Trước khi quyết định quy mô và mô hình kinh doanh, thương hiệu cần hiểu rõ sức mua, lưu lượng khách và hành vi tiêu dùng tại từng khu vực.
Mỗi điểm bán cần có vai trò rõ ràng trong toàn bộ mạng lưới, thay vì áp dụng cùng một mô hình cho mọi địa điểm.
Cuộc đua cuối cùng vì thế không chỉ được quyết định bởi chuỗi nào có nhiều cửa hàng hoặc sáng đèn lâu hơn, mà còn bởi khả năng thu hút khách quay lại và tạo ra lợi nhuận sau khi tính đủ chi phí vận hành.

articles.title: 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
articles.text:
One of the basic problems of spending too much time on social media is that you are cooking your brain by reading posts from a pack of attention-seeking lunatics. If your social media of choice is the site formerly known as Twitter, and it is your main source of contact with the outside world, you may delusionally throw away nearly $500 million dollars on midterm elections, just like Elon Musk.
17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
He’s not even good at being rich!
He’s not even good at being rich!
In particular, $47 million of that money from Musk’s America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico, who trounced Musk’s preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, with 55 percent of the vote. Talarico even made Musk’s influence a central part of his campaign ads, with the slogan “Texas is not for sale.”
The opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industry
How did Musk get this so wrong? I blame the bubble of X. My former colleague Casey Newton, who has (with some well-earned shame) slunk back to X, explained that he did so because it was the site that was most influential with the AI crowd. In some sense, this is exactly the problem. The agentmaxxing loons of AI influencing are wildly out of touch with normal people. There is, right now, one very important bipartisan position in the United States, and it is: Fuck a data center.
It’s pretty obvious that the opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industry, particularly with the gangster tech regulation of late and the constant stream of threats coming from AI companies. These guys have really tied themselves and their AI aspirations to Donald Trump’s sinking ship, and if you’re hanging out on X all the time, that’s impossible to see, not least because the site’s owner, Musk, is shaping the algorithm in ways that make him feel good.
Since Musk seems to have forgotten what it is like to experience joy, or even mild satisfaction, I have taken the liberty to make a list of things he could have bought to get him a better return on his investment. He probably could flip several things on this list for more money, but at minimum he could have gotten a little rush of pleasure from a new purchase:
- Larry Ellison’s private island ($300 million in 2012, $440 million in today’s dollars per CPI calculator) (source)
- 13 Rolls-Royce La Rose Noire Droptails ($32 million) (source)
- 5 The Graff Diamonds Hallucination watches ($55 million, $78 million today) (source)
- The Washington Post ($250 million in 2013, $360 million today) (source)
- 30 Sunseeker 100 yachts (base price $14.6 million) (source)
- 43 Hope diamonds ($300,000 in 1911, about $10.3 million today) (source)
- Ken Griffin’s NYC penthouse ($239.96 million in 2019, $321 million today) (source)
- 76 New Zealand golden visas ($10 million plus $27,000 application fee in NZD, about $5.77 million in USD) (source)
- 44 30-second Super Bowl commercials ($10 million) (source)
- At least 977 rides on Blue Origin’s New Shepard ($450,000) (source)
- Willem de Kooning’s Interchange (~$300 million, ~$400 million today) (source)
- $14.67 gift card to every Texan (~30 million Texans) (source)
- 34 renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ($13.1 million) (source)
- 223,000 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards (at MSRP of $1,999) (source); 60,000 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards (at “globalized normal price” of $7,240) (source)
- 8 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show Fantasy Bras (source)
- His very own non-Grok version of The Odyssey (budget $250 million) (source)
- 4 sets of Wachtell, Lipton lawyers from the Twitter takeover suit ($90 million fee) (source)
But hey, at least changing the name of SpaceX’s “Superintelligence” division back to “Artificial Intelligence” is free!
Musk spent last night deleting tweets so he wouldn’t look as stupid as he is. Too bad it’s not as easy to delete other things! Texans were already asking questions about sweetheart deals to benefit Musk, and now there’s a wave of politicians who ran against his money coming into power, including the governor and the attorney general of Texas. That may mean unredacting Gov. Greg Abbott’s Musk emails, for instance — answering some questions about the influence Musk bought with Texas Republicans.
So actually, maybe the best investment on that list would be the dream team of lawyers who clobbered Musk on the Twitter deal — because Musk has a bunch of new enemies in power, and the simplest thing in the world they can do to curry favor with their voters is investigate him. Bet you’d never know that if you spent all your time on X.

articles.title: I tried Apple's Siri Recaps. They're surprisingly useful — and a little unsettling | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The betas bring four new AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes.
After just a day with Apple’s Siri Recaps feature on my Apple Watch, I can already see how its value may ultimately outweigh any creepiness factor that comes from the AI-powered audio recording and summarization it provides. However, I also see areas where AI-assisted note-taking can go too far, capturing things that aren’t worth remembering, and where there’s room for improvement.
The first two, sound and song detection, don’t represent potential privacy concerns; they are designed to detect either important sounds — like an alarm or doorbell — or identify a song using Shazam’s technology. The former helps deaf and hard-of-hearing users navigate the world, and the latter is something we’ve already done with our iPhone for nearly two decades now.
It’s the two other features, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps, that have raised concerns. The features record and then transcribe or summarize the conversations happening with and around the Apple Watch’s owner. Live Rewind lets you go back to see what was said in the past 15 seconds, while Siri Recaps summarize audio throughout your day, saving notes of the important things that were said.
Apple has taken care to ensure the privacy of these AI features by processing the audio and running AI models on-device, when possible, and by not identifying speakers, storing raw audio files, and redacting private information, like government ID numbers or personal account information.
Still, some are put off by the idea that we’re now normalizing the idea that technology is always listening.
I find myself sympathizing with both camps. I often lament that we’ve allowed technology to become so pervasive in our daily lives, but I still see the value in what Apple has built.
I haven’t yet had an appropriate time to test Live Rewind, nor do I think this will be a feature I use as often. I’m more likely to say “sorry, what?” or “can you repeat that?” if I missed something that was said, before turning to my Apple Watch for help.
But with Siri Recaps, I immediately saw how this could become a feature I rely on regularly to save important notes for later.
I was able to test the feature in a real-world scenario yesterday, when we were dropping off my teen’s car for repairs and picking up a rental. At both places, employees shared a lot of information about time frames, prices, and policies that were delivered verbally. The information came too fast to stop and write anything down. Yet when I returned to Siri Recaps later in the day, it had captured key details that I may need to refer back to.
For instance, it noted the deductible, the repair time frame, the amount of gas we had in the rental at the start, and other things I wanted to remember.
One complaint is that Siri Recaps had mixed this information with other topics that were later discussed in the home, like an errand we needed to run and what time babysitting was this week, something we were discussing in order to create an appointment on the family calendar with an appropriate alert time frame.
I think these items should have been saved in a separate note titled “family schedule and errands,” rather than in the same note with the car repairs, but under a separate heading.
Because I configured Siri Recaps to run at all times, it also captured non-essential things, like our “plan” to watch the midterms coverage on TV, which is not the kind of thing you’d normally jot down a note about. It also was a stark reminder that the feature was listening in on our everyday conversations. That’s something that could feel invasive in different scenarios, if the subject being discussed was more personal in nature.
This had me considering turning off the Recap feature while at home in the evening, so family dinner table chatter doesn’t become note fodder.
While I appreciated that the Recap picked up a reminder about an errand I needed to run from one of the family conversations, other tidbits it saved — like what we were watching on TV — would only be valuable if you were exporting a Siri Recap note to Apple’s Journal app, because it was something you wanted to record for personal reasons.
I’d like to see these sorts of extraneous details saved as separate notes — or at least as dedicated sections that could be exported or deleted on their own at the end of the day.
I’d also love to be able to swipe left on an individual bullet point to remove it from the Siri Recap entirely, rather than having to enter edit mode, place the cursor, and then start deleting the text I don’t need.
Another option I’d like to have would be a setting that would allow you to automatically export any saved Siri Recap (the ones you click the bookmark icon to save) to Apple’s Notes app, instead of that being an extra step.
These Recaps could go into their own folder in the Notes app for easy reference. I can understand why this option is not the default, given how many different ways people use a general-purpose app like Notes. However, it would be useful for those of us who want to keep Notes as the central starting point for all our jotted-down reminders and to-dos.
Though I wasn’t immediately warmed up to the idea that my Watch was always listening, so to speak, I see the value of this sort of automated note-taking in daily life.

articles.title: iPad mini 8 pin "trâu" hơn Apple công bố
articles.text:
Viên pin nhỏ hơn đời trước, thông số công bố không đổi, nhưng một bài thử độc lập cho thấy thời gian duyệt web tăng thêm gần 4 giờ.
Apple vẫn ghi pin iPad mini 8 dùng được tối đa 10 giờ khi duyệt web qua Wi-Fi, con số giống hệt iPad mini 7. Nhưng trong một bài thử nghiệm độc lập vừa công bố, máy trụ được 14 giờ 24 phút.
Bài thử cho máy duyệt web liên tục qua Wi-Fi, độ sáng màn hình cố định ở 150 nit. Trong cùng điều kiện, iPad mini 7 chỉ đạt 10 giờ 36 phút. iPad mini 8 vì vậy dùng lâu hơn khoảng 36%, tương đương gần 4 giờ.
Kết quả này lạ ở chỗ viên pin của iPad mini 8 thực ra nhỏ hơn. Theo nhãn năng lượng Apple công bố cho thị trường châu Âu, dung lượng pin chỉ còn 4.900mAh, giảm khoảng 2,7% so với 5.034mAh của đời trước.
Nguyên nhân chưa được xác nhận. Một nhận định cho rằng chip A20 Pro mới, loại chip cũng có trên iPhone 18 Pro, tiết kiệm điện hơn đời trước. Màn hình OLED cũng có thể góp phần, vì điểm ảnh màu đen được tắt hẳn. Tuy nhiên, phần lớn trang web có nền trắng nên chưa rõ OLED giúp được bao nhiêu trong bài thử này.
Con số 14 giờ chưa phải kết quả cuối cùng. Đơn vị thử nghiệm thường chạy bài test ba lần rồi lấy trung bình, nhưng lần này chỉ kịp chạy một lần và cho biết sẽ cập nhật nếu số liệu thay đổi. Máy thử cũng là bản cao nhất, dung lượng 512 GB, có 5G, màn hình phủ lớp chống chói Nano-texture, giá 1.249 USD (khoảng 32 triệu đồng). Ngoài ra, bài thử chỉ đo việc duyệt web, chưa tính đến chơi game hay quay video.
Ngoài pin, iPad mini 8 là bản nâng cấp lớn nhất từ trước đến nay của dòng máy này. Máy chuyển sang màn hình OLED 8,5 inch thay cho màn LCD 8,3 inch, thân mỏng 5,4 mm, lần đầu có chuẩn chống nước và bụi IP67, và dùng chip A20 Pro. Trong các bài đo, hiệu năng của máy tiến gần iPad Air chip M4. Điểm trừ là máy vẫn không có Face ID và chỉ có tần số quét 60Hz, không có chế độ 120Hz mượt hơn như iPad Pro.
Tại Việt Nam, Apple Store đã niêm yết iPad mini 8 từ 19.499.000 đồng cho bản Wi-Fi 128 GB và 23.699.000 đồng cho bản Wi-Fi kèm 5G cùng dung lượng. Bản 256 GB có giá 22.299.000 đồng (Wi-Fi) và 26.499.000 đồng (5G), bản 512 GB lần lượt là 27.899.000 đồng và 32.099.000 đồng. Riêng lớp kính Nano-texture chỉ có ở bản 256 GB và 512 GB, giá cao hơn. Bạn đọc có thể tham khảo các dòng iPad chính hãng tại gian hàng Apple Flagship Store tại đây.
Giá khởi điểm cao hơn khoảng 5,5 triệu đồng, tức gần 40%, so với mức 13,99 triệu đồng của iPad mini 7 lúc ra mắt cuối năm 2024. Ở Mỹ, máy có giá từ 699 USD (khoảng 18 triệu đồng), cao hơn 100 USD so với iPad mini 7 sau khi Apple nâng giá máy này lên 599 USD (khoảng 16 triệu đồng) hồi tháng 6, với lý do chi phí bộ nhớ tăng.
iPad mini 8 bắt đầu giao tại Mỹ từ 6/11. Tại Việt Nam, Apple chưa công bố ngày mở bán chính thức, người dùng có thể đăng ký nhận thông báo khi có hàng trên website Apple Việt Nam.

articles.title: Google will spend $15B on data centres in Malaysia over two years
articles.text:
Google plans to spend $15B in Malaysia in 2027 and 2028 on data centres, cloud operations, water, power and training. It will expand its Selangor campus and build new ones in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, where it is also funding a $160M water plant.
Google plans to spend $15B on data centres and cloud operations in Malaysia in 2027 and 2028, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The money will also go into local water supplies, power generation and training, the company said.
Google will expand its existing campus at Elmina Business Park in Selangor and build new ones in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, Malay Mail reported. The Elmina site came from a $2B investment Google announced in May 2024.
Alphabet chief investment officer Ruth Porat announced the plan at an event in Kuala Lumpur attended by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
“Our nation possesses the stability, the talent, the ambition to be a premier digital powerhouse in Southeast Asia,” Anwar said.
Google says building the campuses will support more than 37,000 local jobs a year and add about $1.1B a year to Malaysia’s economy. Once they are running, it expects them to sustain more than 9,000 jobs.
Water is a big part of the deal. Earlier this week, Google said it would fund a $160M reservoir and treatment plant in Negeri Sembilan. It will supply 65 million litres of drinking water a day to the data centre and nearby communities.
Water has become a flashpoint for Google elsewhere. Its $15B India data centre has faced protests over local supplies, and on Indonesia’s Batam island, near Singapore, residents have protested dry taps as data centres spread.
Malaysia has become Southeast Asia’s main data centre hub, thanks to low costs, reliable infrastructure and its closeness to Singapore. Oracle, Amazon, Alibaba and ByteDance are all expanding there. The country has more than 6 GW of planned capacity, the largest pipeline in the region.
More money may follow. In late October, Anwar said SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son plans about $50B of AI investment in Malaysia, though SoftBank has not confirmed the figure.
The deal mirrors one Google made in Europe. In September, it said it would put €13B into Finland over the same two years.

articles.title: How I learned to love an obnoxious phone grip
articles.text:
Much like a great recipe, it started with a stick of butter.
How I learned to love an obnoxious phone grip
Making the case for a loud smartphone accessory.
Making the case for a loud smartphone accessory.
This wasn’t real butter; it was a friend’s new phone grip, complemented by a phone case with bold stripes. Butter is in vogue now, or at least that’s what a 12-year-old told me a few months ago. This stick of butter was labeled “unsalty” and committed to the bit by including the appropriate tablespoon markings, just like the real thing. I was enamored. “Where did you get that?” I asked. It was a PopSocket-branded combo, and I found it so irresistible I ordered an equally eye-catching grip a few weeks later. After years of carrying buttoned-up, minimalist tech, I finally said, “To hell with it. I’m gonna have some fun.” I have zero regrets, and it seems I’m not alone in this journey.
Over the past few years I’ve been a vocal, occasionally regretful, member of Team No Phone Case. A case adds bulk and collects pocket lint. Why spend $800 on a piece of tech just to cover it up? If I must use a case, I want it to barely exist. This philosophy worked great with my iPhone 13 Mini, which is perfect as-is. Its size means it’s eminently grippable — no PopSocket necessary and it feels much more secure when I hold it. But phones are big now and are only getting bigger.
Since it’s just held on by a magnet, you can take it off whenever you want to present yourself as a serious grownup
An extended period using Google’s hefty Pixel 10 Pro Fold last year convinced me to adopt a magnetic grip just to use the thing more comfortably. At first, I gravitated toward the minimalist options like low-profile ring stands. But then I saw that stick of butter, and something clicked. A chunky grip is easy to hold. It’s fun. And since it’s just held on by a magnet, you can take it off whenever you want to present yourself as a serious grownup. Why not? I put in an order for a PopSocket shaped like a hot dog, and I was so excited when it arrived I accidentally pulled it apart.
This “why not have fun” ethos has clearly been part of Bailey Hikawa’s mission for the better part of a decade. She’s been making unconventional phone grips and cases out of her Los Angeles studio since 2018. Her designs incorporate input from the disabled community, aiming to offer an easier grip for people who hold their phone differently. But they can be appreciated by anyone who’s ever felt their phone slide out of their fingers. They’re also vibrant and bold. “I would like the phone case to feel like a friend or like a new stuffed animal,” she told The Verge in 2019. Earlier this year, Apple collaborated with Hikawa on a chunky, bright MagSafe grip. Her own online shop includes other grips made of flexible, clear urethane with spaghetti noodles or baby shrimp suspended inside. They’re handmade and the very definition of one-of-a-kind.
In more conventional territory, PopSocket has a surprising number of unusual grips and cases on offer. There’s a classic tomato pincushion, the food truck collection where I found my beloved hot dog, and an aptly named “Sugar Rush” collection. I asked PopSocket founder David Barnett whether I was alone in my pursuit of a bold grip. “We’re seeing more consumers embrace color, texture and personality in their phone accessories,” he told me over email. “I think people want their everyday essentials to feel a little less ordinary. Your phone goes everywhere with you, so why not have a little fun with it?”
I think phone makers are partly to blame here, too. Aside from your stray Cosmic Orange and anything Motorola is doing, phones mostly come in shades of Boring and Light Boring. Don’t even get us started on what passes for a purple phone these days. Maybe a radical reaction to this sameness was inevitable. Whatever the reason, you can find an awful lot of punchy, vibrant grips and cases without much effort. There are color-blocked “dopamine” cases all over TikTok and Amazon, viral phone cases that hold a tube of lip gloss, and OhSnap grips in colors called things like “hazmat honey” and “electric teal.”
Me and my ridiculous PopSocket are in good company. Or we will be — I left it in the office last time I was in New York and its absence has been bumming me out ever since. We’ll be reunited soon enough, but I guess if there’s one downside to being able to take a grip off your phone easily, it’s that you can accidentally leave it behind without much effort.

articles.title: Đông Đô Partners khai trương chi nhánh, mở rộng thị trường phía Nam
articles.text:
Dấu mốc mở rộng hiện diện tại thị trường phía Nam
Ngày 28/10/2026, Công ty Cổ phần Đông Đô Partners tổ chức Hội nghị khách hàng kết hợp khai trương Chi nhánh Hồng Hà tại tòa Nam Á (ESTA) - Office Saigon, số 127 Hồng Hà, TP.HCM.
Trong khuôn khổ chương trình, Đông Đô Partners đã gặp gỡ, trao đổi với khách hàng về thị trường giao dịch hàng hóa phái sinh, đồng thời giới thiệu định hướng phát triển và phương thức hỗ trợ khách hàng trong thời gian tới. Hội nghị cũng tạo cơ hội để doanh nghiệp lắng nghe nhu cầu thực tế, tăng cường kết nối và xây dựng quan hệ hợp tác lâu dài với khách hàng tại khu vực phía Nam.
Được thành lập vào tháng 5/2026, Đông Đô Partners chính thức trở thành Thành viên Kinh doanh số 089 của Sở Giao dịch Hàng hóa Việt Nam (MXV) từ ngày 9/9/2026.
Việc khai trương Chi nhánh Hồng Hà đánh dấu sự hiện diện của doanh nghiệp tại TP.HCM, bên cạnh trụ sở chính ở Hà Nội. Đây là bước triển khai trong chiến lược xây dựng mạng lưới chi nhánh nhằm tăng cường tiếp cận và phục vụ khách hàng tại các địa phương khu vực phía Nam.
Phát biểu tại chương trình, ông Nguyễn Trọng Đạt, Tổng Giám đốc Đông Đô Partners, chia sẻ: “Một văn phòng không đơn thuần là địa điểm làm việc. Đó còn phải là nơi khách hàng có thể tìm đến để trao đổi, được lắng nghe, được tư vấn và nhận được sự hỗ trợ phù hợp với nhu cầu thực tế của mình.”
Theo định hướng này, Chi nhánh Hồng Hà được tổ chức tập trung vào ba chức năng: phát triển kinh doanh, tư vấn và chăm sóc khách hàng. Không gian văn phòng được thiết kế hiện đại, năng động, bố trí bàn ghế tư vấn và hệ thống bảng điện tử, tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho hoạt động tư vấn và chăm sóc khách hàng.
Xây dựng năng lực phục vụ trên nền tảng tri thức và công nghệ
Theo định hướng phát triển, Đông Đô Partners theo đuổi ba giá trị cốt lõi “Tri thức - Công nghệ - Minh bạch”.
Với quy mô khoảng 60 nhân sự, Đông Đô Partners tập trung phát triển hoạt động nghiên cứu, phân tích thị trường và tư vấn giao dịch hàng hóa phái sinh, đồng thời chú trọng cung cấp kiến thức và giải pháp quản trị rủi ro nhằm hỗ trợ khách hàng trong quá trình tham gia thị trường.
Song song với hoạt động chuyên môn, Đông Đô Partners phát triển và ứng dụng các công cụ giao dịch định lượng (Quant Trading) cùng hệ thống tác nhân trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI Agent), phục vụ nghiên cứu, xử lý dữ liệu và hỗ trợ phân tích thị trường.
Doanh nghiệp xác định công nghệ là công cụ hỗ trợ ra quyết định, kết hợp với kiến thức chuyên môn và phương pháp quản trị rủi ro để phát triển dịch vụ bền vững trong lĩnh vực giao dịch hàng hóa phái sinh.
Bên cạnh việc ứng dụng công nghệ, công ty hợp tác với các trung tâm giáo dục và đào tạo chính quy, hướng tới các chương trình nâng cao kiến thức giao dịch và kỹ năng quản trị rủi ro cho khách hàng.
Việc khai trương Chi nhánh Hồng Hà là một phần trong kế hoạch phát triển mạng lưới kinh doanh của Đông Đô Partners. Theo mô hình vận hành, chi nhánh Hồng Hà tập trung phát triển kinh doanh, tư vấn và chăm sóc khách hàng, đồng thời kết nối với các doanh nghiệp địa phương có nhu cầu tham gia thị trường hàng hóa phái sinh. Trụ sở chính tại Hà Nội đảm nhiệm công tác quản lý, phát triển sản phẩm, công nghệ và điều phối hoạt động trên toàn hệ thống.
Chia sẻ tại sự kiện, ông Vũ Công Thắng, Phó Tổng Giám đốc phụ trách Kinh doanh, đã đề cập đến định hướng kinh doanh và kế hoạch phát triển khách hàng của doanh nghiệp trong giai đoạn tới.
Trong 1–3 năm tới, Đông Đô Partners đặt mục tiêu tiếp tục hoàn thiện các sản phẩm, giải pháp công nghệ và chất lượng dịch vụ, đồng thời từng bước phát triển mạng lưới kinh doanh nhằm mở rộng khả năng tiếp cận và phục vụ khách hàng trên toàn quốc.
Với phương châm “Giao dịch bằng trí tuệ, đồng hành bằng uy tín”, doanh nghiệp hướng tới xây dựng nền tảng phát triển dài hạn dựa trên năng lực chuyên môn, ứng dụng công nghệ và sự tin cậy của khách hàng.
(Nguồn: Đông Đô Partners)

articles.title: Google faces backlash for plan that would turn off Search for schools that restrict AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google was met with swift backlash on Tuesday after it announced that schools using Google’s K-12 software will not be able to use Search unless they opt in to using AI tools.
Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” so if a student’s school doesn’t opt in to using AI tools like Gemini, then students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”
Even as Google made this announcement on a busy Election Day, several left-leaning politicians took time to speak up about their concerns.
Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) accused Google in an X post of “extortion,” writing that “Google is threatening schools: if you stop your students from using AI, we will cut off your access to Google Search.” Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) said on X that Google is “more concerned with forcing Gemini into schools than enabling students to succeed.”
Lina Khan, the former Federal Trade Commission chair and staunch advocate against monopolies, also condemned Google’s decision as anticompetitive.
“This highlights the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service,” she wrote. “Multiple courts have found Google liable for violating antitrust laws, and this latest move shows it remains unchastened.”
New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of being a monopoly, commenting, “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.”
While Search is a necessary tool for information gathering, educators worry that its built-in AI overviews could dissuade students from finding answers themselves. For millions of students required to use Chromebooks and Google education tools, using a different search engine isn’t a simple fix.
Google says that it’s working on a “Guided Learning” tool for student accounts in Search, which is supposed to walk students through the process of solving a problem or finding information, rather than just handing them the answer. If a student is struggling with a math problem, for example, the feature may prompt them to refresh their memory about the rules for dividing exponents, instead of spitting out a number.
In response to the backlash, Google pointed out in a post on X that it had listened to educators by turning off access to AI products by default and noted that schools could turn on Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search individually.
“We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google wrote in its statement. “That’s exactly why we are making these changes today to address the feedback we’ve heard from educators in recent months. And we’ll continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.”

articles.title: Parsec founders raise $8.75M from a16z to give AI agents their own PCs
articles.text:
Phaze, started by the team behind remote desktop firm Parsec, raised an $8.75M seed round led by a16z. It lets employees and AI agents use powerful remote computers, so companies can share workstations instead of buying one for each person.
Phaze, a startup from the founders of remote desktop company Parsec, has raised an $8.75M seed round led by a16z, the company said on Wednesday. Indie, NextView, Makers Fund and Lerer Hippeau also invested.
The Utah-based company lets people and AI agents use powerful computers from anywhere. Designers and engineers can run demanding 3D and design software on a remote workstation, while AI agents can control a machine’s screen and apps.
“The computer sitting on your desk shouldn’t determine what compute you can access,” said chief executive Benjy Boxer.
Phaze’s bet is that companies waste money on idle hardware. Instead of buying each employee a top-end workstation, they could pool machines and hand them out as needed, to staff or to agents.
Agents connect through MCP, a common standard for linking AI to tools, which Phaze still labels experimental. In one demo, a Slack bot takes an IT support request, logs into the user’s computer and calls in a human when it gets stuck. Agents get only the access their users have.
Boxer’s previous company, Parsec, was bought by Unity for $320M in 2021.
Others are also building places for agents to work. Baseten bought Blaxel, which makes sandboxes for AI agents, in September, and Perplexity can turn a Mac mini into an always-on agent. The demand is real: AI agents helped sell out Apple’s Mac mini in the US this spring.

articles.title: Bose’s QuietComfort Headphones are more than half off
articles.text:
It’s not often that some of the best noise-canceling headphones you can buy are over half off. But right now, the first-gen Bose QuietComfort Headphones are on sale for $169.99 ($190 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Bose, matching its best price to date. The newer, second-generation version that launched in August is also down to $199 ($160 off) in multiple colors at Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from Bose, which is just $20 shy of the all-time low price.
Bose’s QuietComfort Headphones are more than half off
Both generations of Bose’s noise-canceling headphones are steeply discounted, with prices starting at $170.
While Bose’s original QuietComfort Headphones are no longer the latest model, they’re still a solid option for anyone seeking effective noise cancellation, good sound, and 24-hour battery life without spending a fortune. They also support multipoint Bluetooth connectivity, so you can connect to two devices simultaneously, and they feature a lightweight, foldable design that makes them easy to pack.
The second-generation QuietComfort Headphones build on that foundation with a few worthwhile upgrades for $30 more. Of note, our reviewer John Higgins considers their default sound profile to be the best he’s heard from Bose, even better than the flagship $449 QuietComfort Ultra Gen 2. They also support lossless audio via USB-C. While he thought that vocals sounded a bit muted, he was able to fix the issue by tweaking the three-band equalizer in Bose’s companion app. Higgins also considers the QuietComfort Headphones more comfortable than the Ultra thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck,” the unpleasant sensation of ear pressure from a strong active noise cancellation effect.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 4/11: Xăng trong nước giảm sâu về hơn 23.000 đồng/lít
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 3/11 được điều chỉnh giảm, xuống mức thấp nhất trong gần 4 tuần.
Chốt phiên giao dịch 3/11, theo Reuters, giá dầu Brent giao kỳ hạn giảm 1%, xuống còn 103,44 USD/thùng, mức thấp nhất kể từ ngày 7/10. Trong khi giá dầu WTI hạ 1%, kết phiên ở 95,9 USD/thùng, mức thấp nhất từ ngày 14/10.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (4/11), giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh tăng nhẹ.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 7h12' ngày 4/11 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent được niêm yết ở mức 103,6 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh lên mức 96,61 USD/thùng, tăng 0,54% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới đi xuống trong phiên 3/11 khi thị trường cân nhắc triển vọng đàm phán nhằm chấm dứt xung đột tại Ukraine và Iran, trong bối cảnh những lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung vẫn hiện hữu sau các cuộc tấn công gần đây tại hai khu vực này.
Giới đầu tư đang theo dõi sát những nỗ lực ngoại giao nhằm chấm dứt cuộc xung đột giữa Mỹ-Israel và Iran. Song triển vọng đạt được thỏa thuận hòa bình vẫn còn khá mong manh.
Người phát ngôn Bộ Ngoại giao Qatar Majed al-Ansari cho hay, Mỹ và Iran vẫn cam kết duy trì các nỗ lực hòa giải, đồng thời xem xét những đề xuất nhằm thu hẹp khác biệt giữa hai bên.
Tuy nhiên, một quan chức cấp cao của Iran tiết lộ với Reuters rằng, Tehran và Washington vẫn còn cách xa thỏa thuận chấm dứt xung đột.
Trong khi đó, Qatar đang tăng cường vai trò trung gian nhằm ngăn chặn xung đột có thể bùng phát trở lại sau cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ tại Mỹ.
Bên cạnh diễn biến tại Trung Đông, thị trường dầu mỏ cũng quan tâm đến triển vọng đàm phán hòa bình giữa Nga và Ukraine.
Điện Kremlin xác nhận, Nga sẽ tham gia cuộc đàm phán 3 bên với Mỹ và Ukraine tại Abu Dhabi trong hai ngày 10-11/11.
Nga là nhà sản xuất dầu thô lớn thứ ba thế giới trong năm 2025, sau Mỹ và Arab Saudi. Nếu đạt được thỏa thuận chấm dứt xung đột, Moscow có thể có thêm điều kiện để gia tăng xuất khẩu dầu.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Theo kế hoạch, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính sẽ tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu trong nước vào chiều mai (5/11).
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (4/11) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo thông báo điều hành giá xăng dầu của liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính tối 3/11, giá bán lẻ tối đa xăng E5RON92 được điều chỉnh xuống 23.203 đồng/lít, giảm 1.020 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá xăng E10RON95-III giảm 928 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 23.231 đồng/lít.
Giá dầu diesel 0.05S được điều chỉnh giảm 1.370 đồng/lít, giá bán tối đa còn 28.876 đồng/lít. Trái lại, giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S tăng 378 đồng/kg, lên 23.974 đồng/kg.
Thời điểm điều chỉnh giá bán do thương nhân đầu mối và thương nhân phân phối xăng dầu quyết định. Trong đó, mặt hàng tăng giá được áp dụng không sớm hơn 22h ngày 3/11/2026; mặt hàng giảm giá phải được áp dụng chậm nhất vào thời điểm này.
Trước đó, từ 0h ngày 1/11, xăng E5RON92 đã giảm 1.804 đồng/lít, về 24.223 đồng/lít; xăng E10RON95-III giảm 1.575 đồng/lít, xuống 24.159 đồng/lít.
Như vậy, qua hai lần điều chỉnh, giá hai loại xăng này giảm tổng cộng lần lượt 2.824 đồng/lít và 2.503 đồng/lít.
Dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương cho thấy, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam đang ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Giá bán xăng dầu của các nước lân cận Việt Nam tính đến ngày 3/11 như sau:
Giá xăng tại Thái Lan là 32.550 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); ở Campuchia là 31.887 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); tại Lào là 49.620 đồng/lít; ở Trung Quốc là 36.125 đồng/lít (Chính phủ khống chế giá); còn tại Việt Nam không cao hơn 23.231 đồng/lít.
Giá dầu tại Thái Lan là 33.333 đồng/lít (Chính phủ trợ giá); ở Campuchia là 35.676 đồng/lít; tại Lào là 41.364 đồng/lít; ở Trung Quốc là 33.032 đồng/lít (Chính phủ khống chế giá); trong khi tại Việt Nam không cao hơn 28.876 đồng/lít.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: Pliant raises $80M Series C to open B2B payments to AI agents
articles.text:
Berlin fintech Pliant has raised an $80M Series C to open its B2B payments infrastructure to AI agents, the company said on Wednesday. Seaya Nova and Speedinvest led the oversubscribed round. Illuminate Financial, Motive Partners and Molten Ventures also took part.
The money will fund Pliant’s expansion in the US and Canada, its entry into further markets and its AI roadmap. The round follows three years in which Pliant doubled its business each year. It comes shortly after the company passed $100M in annual recurring revenue.
How AI agents plug in
Pliant combines commercial card issuing, payment accounts, foreign exchange and spend management in one platform. Its own AI agents already automate recurring finance work for customers.
Outside agents, from Claude and ChatGPT to a company’s own automations, connect through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). They can then run payment workflows inside other business processes, with permissions, controls and audit trails built in, Pliant says.
“Whether an established business wants AI to automate its payment processes with the right guardrails, or an AI-native company needs a licensed partner that moves as fast as it does, Pliant is built for that,” said Malte Rau, Pliant’s CEO and co-founder.
The licensed layer
Pliant started in 2020 and is a principal member of Visa and Mastercard. It issues commercial cards in 13 currencies across 32 countries under its European e-money licence, and through regulated partners in the UK and US. It employs more than 300 people across eight offices.
Its customers include travel, insurance and AI-native companies. Banks, fintechs and software platforms also use its infrastructure to run their own commercial card offerings.
“When agents move money, someone still has to be licensed, auditable and liable, and that is the layer Pliant owns,” said Vinoth Jayakumar, general partner at Seaya Nova, in the Business Wire release.
Card networks are testing agent payments too. In October, AI agents started paying supplier invoices in a pilot with Visa, BILL and Billtrust. Synchrony wants to put store cards inside ChatGPT. In corporate cards, US rival Ramp reached a $60bn valuation in October.

articles.title: Titan OS raises $46 million to expand its smart TV OS internationally | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Barcelona-based smart TV operating system maker Titan OS has raised $46 million in new funding, consisting of both equity and debt, the company announced on Wednesday.
The money comes from debt facilities provided by funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, along with existing investors like Highland Europe and Mangrove Capital Partners. The startup, which secured $58 million last year, has now raised $110 million in total. The company said that it could have chosen not to raise money and grow slowly, but it wants to be more ambitious to create more partnerships and expand into more geographies.
Titan OS’s promise to TV makers is that it offers better value from their unit sales by loading an operating system where they can generate money through partnerships with FAST channels (free ad-supported television) and ads on different screens.
The company now serves 30 million users, up from 18 million last year. This includes being a sales partner for TiVo in some regions, along with Tubi in the U.K.
Compared with last year, the startup has also added Sharp, AOC, Vestel, and Skyworth as partners. Its partnership with Philips has been a success, as the Dutch electronics maker has switched to Titan OS and ditched Google TV for its 2026 models.
The extended coverage means that it has a bigger advertiser footprint and better audience engagement metrics to offer to marketers.
“Our bread and butter is the monetization of our inventory on our own network. But the point is that we’re going beyond that. That’s why our reach has increased significantly, which then triggers the flywheel effect by also attracting more sales partners and more agencies that want to spend on our platform, whether it’s owned and operated or via our extensions,” Hyoung-Ung Kim, the company’s newly appointed CFO, told TechCrunch over a call.
In the last year, the company has increased its headcount to 250 people, and also opened an office in London to concentrate on advertising. It already has offices in Barcelona, Amsterdam, and Taipei.
With the new money coming in, the company wants to focus on a few areas. First is content discovery. It still takes everyone a long time to find something to watch. For that, it is using interface tweaks and AI to boost discovery, alongside partnering with more content providers like FAST channels.
“What differentiates us here from the walled gardens is that we do not have our own content offering. Like Google is trying to channel people to YouTube. We do not have that, and we are impartial in our role in content discovery. We are working and trying to reduce time spent searching,” Tobias Pfalzgraff, SVP of people and marketing at Titan OS, said.
Pfalzgraff also emphasized that the company is using AI to improve its ad recommendation and segmentation. While the company is dominant in Europe, it thinks that there are only a few manufacturers creating their own operating systems; more set makers would like to adopt its operating system, just like Philips did. The company also said that with increasing costs of hardware due to AI, manufacturers are thinking about long-term revenue generation opportunities as gadget sales slow down.
“The TV hardware industry is not a very profitable business. That’s why they are so reliant on partners like Titan OS that share revenue after the sale of the TV. But now, of course, the chip sets, the chip prices are increasing more and more. Right. With the AI boom, they have basically doubled down on our partnership,” Kim said.

articles.title: Gemini for Home now plugs into AT&T’s smart security system
articles.text:
AT&T’s smart home security system now integrates with Gemini for Home. The company says its Connected Life system is the “first” home security product to integrate with Google Home Premium, enabling a bunch of Gemini-powered features that can summarize home events, search your video history, and more.
Gemini for Home now plugs into AT&T’s smart security system
AT&T’s Connected Life system now supports Gemini-powered features that can summarize home events and more.
With the update, Gemini for Home can provide detailed descriptions about events captured by your security cameras, such as who delivered a package and how many items they dropped off. You can also search recorded video footage using natural language questions, like “What dug up the yard last night?” or “Who let the dogs out?”, as well as review daily summaries of activity in and outside your home.
These features are only available with AT&T’s professional $29.99 / month Connected Life monitoring plan. AT&T is also adding the ability to automatically arm or disarm your home based on your proximity to your home.
AT&T launched its Connected Life system last December in partnership with Google and Abode. It’s now taking advantage of Google’s Gemini-powered Home APIs, which allow smart home brands and developers to build AI-powered features into their devices. ADT has also hinted at bringing Gemini for Home features into its security systems.

articles.title: Revolut's valuation jumps 53% to $115B in new share sale as it prepares to launch US bank | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Revolut’s investors have completed a secondary share sale that values the British fintech at $115 billion, 53% more than the price tag it had gained in another share sale a year ago, as the company prepares to launch a U.S. bank in 2027.
Investors including Glade Brook Capital Partners, Coatue, Durable Capital Partners, T. Rowe Price Associates, and Baillie Gifford led the share sale, which brought no new money into Revolut. The company declined to say how much stock was sold.
Founded in 2015 by Nik Storonsky and Vlad Yatsenko, Revolut has grown from a money-transfer app into a financial services platform with more than 80 million retail customers across over 40 countries. It has established banking operations across Europe, and launched banks in the U.K., Mexico, Australia, and New Zealand this year, as well as secured banking licenses in France, Colombia, and Argentina.
The company also began rolling out financial services in India earlier this year, and has received conditional approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national bank, which it plans to launch in the first half of 2027, subject to final regulatory approval.
The London-based company has grown increasingly profitable, achieving profit margins of 38% on revenue of $6 billion in 2025.
Even though Revolut has built much of its business around consumers, its business banking division, launched in 2017, has become an increasingly lucrative endeavor. The division accounts for about 20% of Revolut’s gross profit, James Gibson, head of Revolut Business and a partner at the company, told TechCrunch in a recent interview.
Available across Europe, the U.K., Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, and the U.S., Revolut Business processes more than £36 billion (about $48.6 billion) in transactions each month, including over £1 billion (around $1.35 billion) in the U.S. alone. The division generates more than £950 million (about $1.28 billion) in annualized revenue and holds more than £18 billion (roughly $24.3 billion) in customer deposits, the company told TechCrunch.
Nearly half of Revolut Business’ new customers in the U.S. are newly incorporated companies, the company said.
Revolut is looking to bring its business banking services to more markets, including Mexico, Brazil, and India, Gibson said, though he did not specify when the company expects that to happen. The fintech also aims to grow its business customer base from over 800,000 businesses to a million by 2027, he said.
The company’s rising valuation comes as it weighs a public listing. Storonsky has considered a dual listing in New York and London and indicated a preference for a primary listing in the U.S. However, an IPO, which could reportedly value Revolut at $200 billion, would come no earlier than 2028, depending on market conditions.

articles.title: Google’s Pixel 11 phones are up to 27 percent off
articles.text:
You can save a heck of lot of money on Google’s Pixel 11 phones through November 8th, whether you want the best-for-the-least Pixel 11, or the slightly pricier Pixel 11 Pro that takes better photos. Even the big Pixel 11 Pro XL with a longer-lasting battery is hundreds off its original price.
Google’s Pixel 11 phones are up to 27 percent off
With prices up to $350 off, it’s a good time to consider upgrading if you’re looking for a great Android phone.
The Pixel 11 Pro deal is the most attractive of the bunch, as the $1,099.99 phone with 256GB storage and 12GB of RAM is down to just $799.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and at the Google Store, beating its October Prime Day price by $50. It’s $100 less than the base Pixel 11 model sold for at launch, and it’s the phone to get if you want great camera performance, plus extra features like HiLight that, while cool, weren’t really worth paying a premium to access. I’d be very surprised if the price dropped more for Black Friday.
There’s absolutely nothing wrong with opting for the Pixel 11 instead, especially at its attractive $699.99 ($200 off) price that now matches the cost of the iPhone 17E, following Apple’s September price bump. The Pixel 11 is the most affordable phone that supports Google’s software features that are exclusive to this year’s phones, including Magic Capture, Camera Looks, and Proactive Assistance. It has fast 25W wireless charging (up from 15W with the Pixel 10), and has 12GB of RAM, like the Pixel 11 Pro.
I’m still happily rocking my Pixel 9 Pro, but if I were going to upgrade right now, I’d get the Pixel 11 Pro. Yes, I want the better cameras and HiLight. But really, the main reason I’m lured to the Pro is because the trade-in offers are really generous right now. It’s just $10 more to opt for the Pro over the base Pixel 11. My base Pixel 9 Pro with 128GB of storage can fetch $530 in trade-in credit at the Google Store and $525 at Best Buy, which seems great.

articles.title: “A model can suggest where to look”: Mario Stifano on AI and mining
articles.text:
Mario Stifano is chief executive of Galantas Gold, a gold and copper company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange in Toronto and on AIM in London. He has more than 25 years of experience across exploration, development and producing mining companies. Galantas is developing the Andacollo gold project in Chile, a former producing mine, and the Indiana gold-copper project.
We asked him how the AI and data-centre build-out is changing demand for gold, copper and new mines.
Gold’s role in technology
Gold has traditionally been viewed as a store of value, but it also plays an important role in advanced electronics and computing. As AI and digital infrastructure continue to expand, how do you see gold’s role in the technology sector evolving?
Most people picture gold in a vault or in jewellery. Fewer think about the gold inside the devices they use every day. Engineers have relied on it for decades because it conducts electricity well, doesn’t corrode, and can be made into extremely thin wires and coatings. When a connection has to work every time, those properties matter.
I expect that role to continue as computing becomes more demanding. But I wouldn’t assume every increase in AI investment means the same increase in gold demand. Manufacturers are always looking for ways to use less of an expensive material.
You can see that tug-of-war in the numbers. The World Gold Council reported about 323 tonnes of technology demand in 2025, essentially flat on 2024. AI applications supported demand, but thinner wires, leaner designs and weaker consumer electronics offset that growth. So gold can become more important in specific high-end components without a dramatic jump in total tonnage.
Data centres and metals demand
The rapid expansion of AI data centers is driving demand for copper and other essential materials. How is this infrastructure boom reshaping demand for metals, and where does gold fit into the broader picture?
Start with the electricity. A data centre needs reliable power every hour it operates. That means looking past the servers to the substations, cables, transformers and generating capacity behind them.
The IEA’s latest analysis found that data-centre electricity use grew 17% in 2025. It expects that use to roughly double by 2030, with AI-focused facilities growing faster still. That gives you a sense of the physical build-out that companies are planning.
Copper runs through that whole electrical system. And AI is adding demand at the same time as utilities, transport and industry are investing in electrification. The mining industry has to plan for all of it together.
Gold plays a different role. It’s used selectively in electronics, where reliability justifies the cost, while copper’s exposure is spread across the physical infrastructure. For gold, technology matters, but it is still one part of a market driven mainly by investment, central banks and jewellery.
Supply chain bottlenecks
As tech companies invest billions in AI infrastructure, could growing demand for copper and other critical materials create supply chain bottlenecks that ultimately slow down technological progress?
Yes. The technology industry and the mining industry work on very different timelines. A commitment to spend billions on AI infrastructure doesn’t mean the materials will be there when construction teams need them.
S&P Global found that mines starting production between 2020 and 2024 took almost 18 years on average from discovery. Before construction even begins, a company has to drill the deposit, prove its economics, complete engineering, obtain approvals and secure financing.
For copper, the pressure goes well beyond AI. Data centres compete for supply with electricity networks, electric vehicles and other industries. The IEA’s 2026 outlook estimates that, under today’s policies, existing and announced projects could leave primary copper supply about 25% short of requirements in 2035.
Closing that gap takes more than new discoveries. It means financing projects that can actually deliver, expanding and restarting suitable operations, and recovering more from ore already being processed. Otherwise, technology companies face higher costs, longer equipment lead times and delayed projects.
That’s why I put so much weight on work that has already been done. Our Andacollo gold project in Chile is a former producing mine. We still have refurbishment, technical and financing work ahead of us, but we’re not starting from a blank page.
AI in gold exploration
AI is increasingly being used to analyze geological data and identify mineral deposits. How could these technologies transform gold exploration, particularly when it comes to discovering resources that traditional methods may have overlooked?
One opportunity that really interests me is getting more out of work that has already been done.
An established mining district can hold decades of drilling, surveys and geological records. Different companies collected that information at different times, often looking for different things. There’s real value in bringing it together and asking questions that were hard to investigate before.
Canada is backing exactly this idea, with a federal and territorial pilot in the Northwest Territories that uses AI to scan and analyse drill core already sitting in government storage.
The majors are doing it too. Agnico Eagle works with GeologicAI, combining AI with drill-core scanning to make its resource models more complete and reliable.
At Galantas, our team in Chile spends a lot of time reading drill core and surface geology, and we share some of that work through our Field Notes video series. Technology can help, but experienced geologists still have to understand the core.
And you still have to drill. A model can suggest where to look; it can’t prove you have an economic deposit. For me the test is simple: does it help the team make a better decision about the next drill hole? Exploration capital is limited, so better targeting makes a real difference to how far that capital goes.
New uses for gold in AI hardware
Gold is valued in high-reliability electronic components for its conductivity and resistance to corrosion. Could advances in AI hardware, semiconductors, and high-performance computing create new opportunities for gold, or will its role remain relatively specialized?
Specialised doesn’t mean unimportant. A component can contain very little gold and still depend on it to perform reliably.
There are new applications worth watching. One is co-packaged optics, which places optical connections right next to the processor so AI systems can move data faster and use less power. Some of the optical components and high-frequency electrodes in those designs use gold.
The World Gold Council sees it as a potentially small but meaningful new source of demand if it’s widely adopted in AI data centres. It’s still early.
I’d leave the engineering judgments to the chip makers. From a mining perspective, I want to know three things. Is the technology being adopted commercially? How much material does it need? And can something cheaper do the same job?
There will always be pressure to use less gold because of its price. But where it offers a clear reliability advantage, it earns its place. That points to a specialised role with room to grow, not a story where AI suddenly transforms the whole gold market.
Grids, copper and realistic timetables
Building the next generation of AI data centers requires massive investments in electricity grids and power distribution systems, where copper plays a critical role. Are technology companies underestimating their dependence on physical resources, and what happens if supply cannot keep pace?
I wouldn’t assume the technology companies don’t understand the dependency. The better question is whether everyone in the chain is working to a realistic timetable.
A server can be ordered. A grid connection may need new lines, approvals and equipment that can’t be delivered right away. The IEA has estimated that, unless these constraints are addressed, around 20% of planned data-centre projects worldwide could be at risk of delay. That’s mainly a grid problem rather than a copper shortage, but it shows how physical the AI build-out really is.
The sulphuric acid problem
The supply chain also runs deeper than most people realise. In its 2026 outlook, the IEA warned that the near-term copper supply picture has worsened considerably, partly because of tight supplies of sulphuric acid. Many copper operations need that reagent to process their ore, and Chile, where we operate, is one of the major producers that use the process. Most people in tech have never thought about sulphuric acid, but it can affect how much copper reaches the market.
If supply can’t keep pace, companies will delay projects, pay more or build somewhere else. Long-term purchasing commitments and earlier conversations with suppliers help those suppliers expand with confidence. In mining, we know a good asset is only part of the equation; you also need power, infrastructure and financing. Digital infrastructure is no different.
Machine learning and mining economics
How are machine learning, automation, and predictive analytics changing the economics of gold exploration and production, and could these technologies help smaller companies compete more effectively with established industry players?
The biggest opportunity is getting more value from the money we already spend. Drilling is expensive. Equipment downtime is expensive. Losing recoverable gold during processing is expensive. Those are specific problems technology can help address.
In exploration, better analysis of historical drilling and geological information can help a team decide where to drill next. It doesn’t guarantee a discovery, but better targeting can help a company make more effective use of its exploration budget.
Recovery and maintenance
In production, consider recovery: the percentage of metal in the ore that the plant successfully extracts. In a simplified example, if the material processed contains 100,000 ounces of gold, improving recovery from 90% to 92% means recovering another 2,000 ounces from the same feed. You still have to account for the cost of achieving that improvement, but you haven’t had to mine additional tonnes to access those ounces.
There are practical examples of this approach. BHP and Microsoft have described using real-time plant data and AI recommendations at Escondida to help operators adjust processing conditions with the aim of improving copper recovery.
Predictive maintenance tackles another cost. Identifying a developing equipment problem can allow a repair during a planned shutdown instead of an unexpected failure that interrupts production.
For smaller companies, access to specialist software and service providers can put better analytical tools within reach. But the tools still need reliable data and experienced people. Large operators retain advantages in both.
I would start with a problem we can measure, test the technology and compare the benefit with its full cost. A smaller company doesn’t need to match a major miner’s technology budget. It needs to spend its own budget effectively.
Recycling and new supply
As the technology industry looks for more sustainable supply chains, could advances in electronic waste recycling, AI-driven material recovery, and more efficient production reduce the need for newly mined gold and copper?
Yes, to a degree. Recovering more metal from products we’ve already made makes sense. The question is how much can be collected and recovered economically, and when it becomes available.
The UN’s Global E-waste Monitor found that only 22.3% of the e-waste generated in 2022 was documented as formally collected and recycled. That’s measured by weight, not the recovery rate for any one metal, but it shows how much room there is to improve.
AI-assisted sorting and better processing can help. They still need collection networks, suitable facilities and a business model that covers the cost.
Timing matters too. Recycling depends on products reaching the end of their lives, and copper installed in a grid today may stay in service for decades.
So I see recycling and mining as complementary. More recycling improves supply security and reduces how many new mines we need. It doesn’t remove the need to invest in mining.
What matters most by 2030
Looking toward 2030, which developments do you believe will have the greatest impact on the future of gold and critical metals: AI-powered exploration, rising demand from data centers, or the challenge of bringing new mineral supplies online?
For the period to 2030, I’d put delivering supply first. I also think it’s the one the market gives the least weight.
A discovery made today might be very important, but it’s unlikely to produce metal before 2030. That makes the projects already being permitted, financed and built far more relevant this decade. So is what existing operations can add through expansions, better recovery and sensible restarts.
AI will help with those decisions. I expect much of its near-term value to come from understanding known assets better and helping operations run more consistently.
But the asset still has to work. It needs the right geology and metallurgy, a realistic development plan, financing and the ability to operate responsibly. Better software doesn’t change that.
I’d also separate gold from copper. Data centres are part of copper’s wider infrastructure story. For gold, technology plays a role, but monetary conditions, investment demand and central-bank buying will matter more.
The question I keep coming back to is simple: which projects can actually deliver, at what cost, and when?

articles.title: Vàng vẫn đối mặt nguy cơ giảm tiếp, người mua bắt đáy trở lại
articles.text:
Cú sốc khi vàng đi ngược các yếu tố hỗ trợ
Điều khiến đợt bán tháo lần này đáng chú ý không chỉ nằm ở biên độ giảm, mà còn ở việc giá vàng đi ngược một số yếu tố vốn thường hỗ trợ kim loại quý.
Lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ giảm, đồng USD yếu đi, căng thẳng địa chính trị vẫn hiện hữu - 3 yếu tố lẽ ra sẽ đẩy vàng lên đỉnh cao mới. Song, kim loại quý vẫn xuyên thủng ngưỡng tâm lý 4.000 USD/ounce, có thời điểm xuống dưới 3.900 USD, mức thấp nhất kể từ tháng 10/2025.
Theo phân tích của Goldman Sachs, “thủ phạm” không phải các quỹ đầu cơ mà là các chủ thể chủ quyền (sovereign entities), tức là những quốc gia nắm giữ lượng vàng dự trữ khổng lồ buộc phải bán tháo để đáp ứng nhu cầu thanh khoản cấp bách.
Trong vòng 5 tuần, họ đã xả ròng tới 19,5 tỷ USD vàng, một tốc độ nhanh hơn nhiều so với nhịp mua ròng của các ngân hàng trung ương (khoảng 85 tấn mỗi tháng).
Goldman Sachs gọi đây là cuộc đối đầu giữa hai thế lực “không quan tâm đến giá”: một bên là ngân hàng trung ương mua vào bất kể giá cao hay thấp; bên kia là các chủ thể chủ quyền bán ra bất chấp giá đã giảm sâu, chỉ để có tiền mặt. Trong cuộc đua này, bên bán đang nhanh hơn.
Vàng hồi phục hay chỉ là 'cú nảy mèo chết'?
Sau cú rơi tự do, vàng đã có phiên hồi phục nhẹ lên quanh 3.895-3.907 USD/ounce trong phiên đầu tuần 2/11, khi giá dầu hạ nhiệt, nhưng vẫn ở mức cao do căng thẳng và một bộ phận nhà đầu tư quay lại bắt đáy.
Dù vậy, giới phân tích kỹ thuật vẫn thận trọng.
Trong bài viết có tiêu đề “Gold Rebound or Dead Cat Bounce? $4,000 Holds the Key” (Vàng phục hồi hay chỉ là cú nảy mèo chết? Mốc 4.000 USD là chìa khóa), chuyên gia Fawad Razaqzada của Investing.com nhận định xu hướng kỹ thuật ngắn hạn vẫn nghiêng về phía giảm.
Vàng cần lấy lại vùng 3.942-4.000 USD, rồi xa hơn là 4.066-4.105 USD, mới có thể cải thiện triển vọng. Nếu thất bại, các mục tiêu tiếp theo nằm ở 3.850 USD và thậm chí 3.700 USD/ounce.
“Dead cat bounce”, hay “cú nảy mèo chết”, là thuật ngữ chỉ một nhịp phục hồi ngắn trong xu hướng giảm, sau đó giá có thể tiếp tục đi xuống. Nói cách khác, một vài phiên tăng chưa đủ chứng minh thị trường đã tạo đáy.
Các chỉ báo kỹ thuật rơi vào vùng quá bán có thể tạo điều kiện cho giá xuất hiện nhịp hồi. Tuy nhiên, điều đó không đồng nghĩa xu hướng giảm đã kết thúc.
Vì sao vàng vẫn chịu áp lực?
Một trong những yếu tố gây sức ép lên vàng là triển vọng chính sách tiền tệ của Mỹ.
Tại cuộc họp cuối tháng 10/2026, Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) giữ nguyên lãi suất ở vùng 3,75-4%, nhưng 2 nhà hoạch định chính sách bỏ phiếu ủng hộ tăng thêm 25 điểm cơ bản.
Thị trường ngày 3/11 định giá khoảng 85% khả năng Fed tăng lãi suất một lần nữa vào tháng 12. Lãi suất cao làm tăng chi phí cơ hội của việc nắm giữ vàng, bởi kim loại quý không đem lại lợi suất định kỳ như trái phiếu hay tiền gửi.
Đồng thời, nó củng cố sức mạnh của USD, khiến vàng trở nên đắt đỏ hơn đối với người mua nước ngoài.
Giá dầu leo thang do căng thẳng địa chính trị càng làm trầm trọng thêm lo ngại lạm phát, qua đó gián tiếp đẩy Fed vào thế phải giữ chặt chính sách tiền tệ.
Mốc 4.000 USD và lực mua bắt đáy
Bất chấp bức tranh kỹ thuật ảm đạm, vẫn có những lý do để không quá bi quan. Lực cầu vật chất từ châu Á đang quay trở lại. Các thị trường vàng lớn như Trung Quốc và Ấn Độ thường tăng cường mua vào khi giá điều chỉnh sâu, tạo ra một “tấm đệm” tự nhiên cho thị trường.
Ngoài ra, các ngân hàng trung ương vẫn là người mua ròng, dù tốc độ chậm hơn, nhưng họ chưa hề đảo chiều chính sách tích lũy vàng.
Về mặt kỹ thuật, 3.886-3.900 USD đang đóng vai trò là vùng hỗ trợ quan trọng. Nếu vàng giữ được vùng này và vượt qua 4.000 USD, kịch bản “dead cat bounce” sẽ bị vô hiệu hóa, nhường chỗ cho một đợt phục hồi bền vững hơn. Ngược lại, thủng 3.850 USD sẽ mở đường cho đợt bán tháo mới.
Với nhà đầu tư cá nhân, đây là thời điểm của những quyết định khó khăn. Bắt đáy có thể mang lại lợi nhuận lớn nếu mốc 4.000 USD được lấy lại.
Nhưng nếu đó chỉ là một nhịp “dead cat bounce” trong một xu hướng giảm dài hơn, cái giá phải trả sẽ không nhỏ. Như Goldman Sachs lưu ý, vị thế bán chưa được thanh lý hết và rủi ro giảm giá vẫn chưa biến mất.
Một điều chắc chắn: vàng đã không còn là “nơi trú ẩn an toàn” đơn giản như nhiều người tưởng. Vì thế, nhà đầu tư cần theo dõi đồng thời diễn biến lãi suất, USD, dòng vốn và hoạt động mua bán trên thị trường.

articles.title: Aformic raises $6.95M to move its factory robots into AI data centres
articles.text:
Aformic, which makes self-driving forklifts and carts for factories, raised a $6.95M seed round led by Veteran Ventures Capital. It says it has more than $34M in orders and plans new robots for building and maintaining AI data centres.
Industrial robotics startup Aformic has raised a $6.95M seed round led by Veteran Ventures Capital, the company said on Wednesday. ff Venture Capital, Mana Ventures, Red Beard Ventures and Alamo Angels also took part.
Based in Duncan, South Carolina, Aformic makes self-driving forklifts and carts that move parts and materials around factories and warehouses. They navigate without tape or markers on the floor, and its Qursor software plans their routes and assigns tasks.
The company was spun out of AIUT, a Polish industrial automation group, and still has an engineering and production centre in Gliwice, Poland.
Aformic says it has won more than $34M in orders and has hundreds of robots in use. Its customers include Toyota, Hitachi, 3M, Hyundai Mobis and Oshkosh Defense. Over the past year, it says, its robots drove more than 186,000 miles inside customers’ plants.
“AFORMIC was built to automate the industries that matter,” said chief executive Michal Fiuk, a US Army veteran.
The money will fund more engineers and sales staff, work on Qursor, and new robots for other jobs, including helping to build and maintain AI data centres. Data centre builders say a shortage of skilled workers is now one of their biggest bottlenecks.
Investors are backing factory robots in a big way. Earlier this week, Tutor Intelligence raised $75M from a16z for robots that customers rent by the hour, and Toyota spin-out Walden Robotics launched with $300M in July.

articles.title: Xbox previews two new ways to control cloud games
articles.text:
I revealed yesterday that the new Xbox Nano controller supports a Wi-Fi connection directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming, and now Microsoft is making it official today. Two new Xbox previews will let players try out using a phone as a controller on smart TVs, as well as cloud connect on the Xbox Nano to connect directly to cloud servers.
Xbox previews two new ways to control cloud games
Xbox Cloud Gaming is getting a phone controller and new direct Wi-Fi connectivity for the Xbox Nano.
“Instead of a Bluetooth connection to your TV, cloud connect uses your Wi-Fi to connect directly to the cloud server running your game,” says the Xbox team. “That can help reduce input latency, so gameplay may feel more responsive.”
Players in the US will be able to preview the new cloud connect option for the Xbox Nano controller starting today. If you’re not in the US you will be able to preview a new phone controller option on smart TVs. The controller is available on the Xbox Cloud Gaming website, allowing people to use the streaming service without a dedicated Bluetooth controller.
Microsoft says “both experiences are still being tested” and that “availability and supported games or devices may be limited” during this beta phase. You’ll need to use the Xbox beta app for Android or the Xbox Accessories app on PC to set up cloud connect on the Nano controller, and the smart TV phone controller just requires a toggle of preview features from the Settings > Account section of Xbox Cloud Gaming.

articles.title: Why are premium domains so expensive?
articles.text:
Premium domains are expensive because each name exists only once, and short, memorable ones are long gone. Registries and owners price them on demand. They help brands get remembered, but they do not boost Google rankings, and some renew at premium prices.
Registering a normal .com address is cheap. Since 1 November, registrars pay Verisign, which runs .com, $10.97 a year per name, after a 7% rise, Domain Name Wire reported. Yet Voice.com sold for $30M in 2019.
The gap comes down to scarcity. Every domain name exists only once, and the short, clear words people remember were registered decades ago. No amount of money creates a second one.
Two kinds of premium
Some premium names have never been registered. Registries, the companies that run each extension, flag short or keyword-rich names in advance and charge more for them. Some keep charging a premium every year.
Most famous premium names, though, are resold by people or companies that already own them. The owner sets the price, which is usually negotiable. After the sale, these names normally renew at the standard rate.
What buyers are paying for
A short, familiar name is easier to say, type and remember, so more people find a business without searching for it. It can also make a young company look established. Swedish startup Lovable recently took over lovable.com from an Italian lingerie brand.
What a premium name does not buy is a better Google ranking. “Keywords in a TLD do not give any advantage or disadvantage in search,” Google says.
Hype moves prices too
Demand can lift a whole extension: the AI boom pushed .ai, Anguilla’s country code, past 1M registrations. It earned the island $80M from January to July, nearly half its government revenue, the Jamaica Gleaner reported. Slovenia’s .si saw 20,000 sign-ups in a day after Trump renamed AI “Super Intelligence”.
Check the renewal price
The sticker price can mislead. A domain sold for $1 in its first year may renew at $20, and some registry premiums stay expensive every year. Before buying, check the first-year price, the renewal fee and what you would pay to transfer it.
